title: Derrick Henry says he's not thinking about retiring
summary: At 32, Derrick Henry is the NFL's oldest starting running back.
full_text: At 32, Derrick Henry is the NFL's oldest starting running back. But he's not even thinking about retiring. Henry made that clear in a social media post after seeing a post that quoted him as saying he wants to retire as a Raven. Henry responded by saying that while he would love to play with the Ravens for the rest of his career, he never said anything about retiring with the Ravens or anyone else, because retiring isn't on his mind. "I would like to finish my playing career with Ravens . I never said anything about retiring lol, I’m enjoying being a Raven. I’ll worry about that retirement sh* later," Henry wrote. Despite his advancing age, Henry is still playing at a high level. Last year he started all 17 games and carried 307 times for 1,595 yards, an average of 5.2 yards per carry, and scored 16 touchdowns. All of those numbers are better than his career averages. In Henry's mind, retirement is a long way off.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Panthers QB Haynes King: Dream come true to showcase my talent in front of Hall of Famers
summary: King, the Panthers' undrafted rookie quarterback, turned in a big game that culminated with the game-winning touchdown as time expired.
full_text: NFL preseason games don't matter in the standings, but they matter a lot to undrafted rookies trying to make the team. And few undrafted rookies have had as impressive a preseason debut as Panthers quarterback Haynes King in Thursday night's Hall of Fame Game. King completed 21 of 34 passes for 180 yards and two touchdowns, with no sacks and no turnovers, and he also ran for 39 yards, including the game-winning touchdown run as time expired. King spoke afterward about how much it meant to him to play like that in Canton, Ohio, in front of dozens of Hall of Famers in town for enshrinement weekend. "It was a dream come true," King said. "Growing up, you hear about all these first-ballot Hall of Famers, and to see some of them walking in front of you before the game is pretty amazing. And to be able to showcase your talent in front of them is a dream come true." The 25-year-old King spent six years in college football and was the ACC Player of the Year at Georgia Tech last season, but he went undrafted because he was regarded as more of a runner than a passer. He looked very comfortable throwing the ball on Thursday night. "I'm very excited that I got this opportunity, and I feel like I went out there and operated at a high level," King said. "I allowed everybody around me to play better as well." When King dove across the goal line on the final play of the game, the Panthers' sideline went crazy, and head coach Dave Canales loved that. "Haynes is a fantastic athlete and he just finds a way to win, and that's what he did," Canales said. "Really proud of the group and also proud of the whole team celebrating. That's something we pride ourselves on, celebrating how hard we work on these situations and then watching it come alive."
author: Michael David Smith

title: Adam Vinatieri: I love the Patriots, but Carlie Irsay-Gordon was my choice to induct me
summary: "I love both organizations," Vinatieri said. "Living in Indy, what the Irsay family meant to me, Jim just meant the world bringing me into that organization, and Carlie I'm so excited watching her taking over her dad's legacy."
full_text: When Adam Vinatieri was elected to the Pro Football Hall of Fame, he had a decision to make: Would he be presented for induction by someone from the Patriots or the Colts? Vinatieri chose Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon to present him at the enshrinement ceremony, which will take place on Saturday in Canton, Ohio. Vinatieri told Mike Florio on Football Night in America that to him, it was a clear choice because of what Irsay-Gordon's father, the late Colts owner Jim Irsay, had meant to him. "I love both organizations, I've got so many memories and so many great friends on both sides," Vinatieri said. "Living in Indy, what the Irsay family meant to me, Jim just meant the world bringing me into that organization, and Carlie I'm so excited watching her taking over her dad's legacy." Unlike the Baseball Hall of Fame, which presents players wearing one team's cap, the Pro Football Hall of Fame does not induct players as representatives of any one team, and if it did, a case could be made for Vinatieri representing either of his two NFL teams. Vinatieri played for the Patriots from 1996 to 2005 and for the Colts from 2006 to 2019. He was a first-team All-Pro for both teams and he was a Super Bowl champion for both teams. And now he's a Hall of Famer for both teams. But only one person will serve as his presenter, and Vinatieri wanted the owner of the Colts.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Sean McVay declines to discuss Rams' plans for Australia travel
summary: On most topics raised during a press conference, Rams coach Sean McVay is willing to provide reporters with an answer.
full_text: On most topics raised during a press conference, Rams coach Sean McVay is willing to provide reporters with an answer. On the subject of his team's travel plans to Australia for a Week 1 game against the 49ers, he is not. Amid reports that the Rams will barnstorm in and out of Melbourne, arriving the day before the game and exiting the day after, McVay opted not to go there on Thursday. The transcript from the team, which usually consists of a summary of each question before McVay's full answer, included the full question-and-answer exchange as to whether the Rams have finalized their plans for Australia. McVay: "Yeah, but I'd rather just keep it in-house." Reporter: "Why?" McVay: "What's the reason to talk about it, you know? Honestly, I would respectfully just say we have, but I'd prefer not to talk about it." Reporter: "Is it a strategic thing?" McVay: "I just don't want to talk about it. What does it matter?" Reporter: "Well, fans, I think, are curious." McVay: "We won't be there long enough for the fans to really have any curiosity about it." Reporter: "You guys have taken different ways of doing it compared to a lot of NFL teams. Last year, you went to London, very short turnaround, played very well against the Jaguars. This is a longer trip, and are you going to do something similar or are you going to give yourself more runway?" McVay: "Yeah, I'd rather not talk about it." McVay's comment regarding not being there long enough for the fans to have curiosity seems to confirm that it will indeed be a short trip. Surely, McVay has a reason for not elaborating. Maybe he hasn't had a chance to fully explain it to the players. Maybe some of them are grumbling about it, and he needs to get them to buy in before he takes it public. Regardless, McVay likely didn't decide randomly to not address one specific subject. And it's not as if the Rams will be able to conceal their ultimate itinerary. Everyone will know when they fly to Australia, and everyone will know when they return to L.A.
author: Mike Florio

title: Aaron Rodgers insists he doesn't care about criticism
summary: The week began with Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers causing a ruckus on ESPN, where he sharply criticized Dr.
full_text: The week began with Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers causing a ruckus on ESPN, where he sharply criticized Dr. Anthony Fauci — and ESPN. The appearance prompted sharp criticism of Rodgers. Rodgers has since insisted that he doesn't care. “ I don’t give a [crap] about anything that people think about me unless they’re in my corner and I would ask them for advice,” Rodgers told Jarrett Bell of USA Today . “I don’t care about the criticism from people like that,” Rodgers said. “Most people have made up their mind about me, so it doesn’t matter what I say. It’s not going to change their mind because most people aren’t listening to the content of your words. They’re wanting to attack your character because they think you’re MAGA or they think you’re whatever tag they put on you — conspiracy theorist, anti-science. They’ve already made up their mind about me before this.” But the stuff Rodgers said on Monday reinforces, and confirms, those preconceived notions. If, after all, someone is regarded as MAGA or a conspiracy theorist or anti-science and that person then says things consistent with one or more of those labels, why would anyone feel any differently than they already do? Besides, other things Rodgers told Bell contradict his "I don't give a shit" vibe. Rodgers explained that he posted photos of his recent reconciliation with his estranged family not to celebrate the occasion but to counter lingering criticism of his perceived role in cutting them off. “I feel like it was part of the full-circle nature of this last season for me,” Rodgers told Bell. “There’s been a narrative out there. There’s not been a lot of information that’s truthful about it. And I think that the personal life should stay personal and private. . . . “But I feel like it was part of the full-circle to just one-time post something, and never again. So that that narrative can finally be put to rest.” If Rodgers doesn't care what people think of him "unless they're in my corner and I would ask them for advice," why violate his "personal and private" life to "shut down" a narrative that doesn't trouble him? If he truly doesn't give a shit what anyone thinks, why would he give a shit about shutting down their narratives? Rodgers is a complicated figure, to be sure. And there are plenty of inconsistencies in the things he says and does. Since he doesn't care if anyone outside his inner circle thinks that, he won't care that someone is pointing it out.
author: Mike Florio

title: Haynes King leads Panthers to 33-30 win on final play of Hall of Fame Game
summary: Haynes King wasn't drafted despite being the ACC Player of the Year last season.
full_text: ''' Haynes King wasn't drafted despite being the ACC Player of the Year last season. The Panthers signed the former Georgia Tech star quarterback as a free agent, and he showed Thursday night maybe someone should have drafted him. Third on the team's depth chart, King replaced veteran Kenny Pickett with 9:38 remaining in the first half and the Panthers trailing 14-7. King completed 21 of 34 passes for 180 yards and two touchdowns, a 15-yarder and a 5-yarder. He also ran for 39 yards on three carries, including scoring on a 5-yard jaunt on the final play of the game. It gave the Panthers a 33-30 victory. In one of the most entertaining Hall of Fame Games ever, the Cardinals gained 425 yards and the Panthers 378. Rookie Carson Beck started for Arizona and went 15-of-19 for 188 yards and a touchdown before turning it over to fourth-string quarterback Kedon Slovis, who was 9-of-10 for 106 yards and a touchdown.
author: Charean Williams

title: Carson Beck throws for 188 yards, TD in impressive preseason debut
summary: Carson Beck has played in much bigger games than the Hall of Fame Game, so it probably should come as no surprise that the lights weren't too bright or the stage too big.
full_text: Carson Beck has played in much bigger games than the Hall of Fame Game, so it probably should come as no surprise that the lights weren't too bright or the stage too big. Beck started for the Cardinals in the first preseason game of the NFL season. He showed up and showed out. Beck played a little more than a half, completing 15 of 19 passes for 188 yards and a touchdown. He hit Reggie Virgil for what would have been a big gain on his final throw of the night in the third quarter, but Isaiah Simmons knocked it out. He directed scoring drives of 96, 50 and 61 yards, throwing a 5-yard fade to a well-covered Simi Fehoko for a touchdown on the team's second scoring drive. The Cardinals were tied with the Panthers 17-17 when Beck left with 10:15 remaining in the third quarter. Fourth-stringer Kedon Slovis replaced Beck.
author: Charean Williams

title: Lions held firm at a bump above Bijan Robinson for Jahmyr Gibbs
summary: It's clear that both Falcons running back Bijan Robinson and Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs wanted to get to $25 million in new-money APY on their new contracts.
full_text: '' It's clear that both Falcons running back Bijan Robinson and Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs wanted to get to $25 million in new-money APY on their new contracts. Both can do it, but only by reaching their full upside packages. After the Falcons gave running back Bijan Robinson a deal with a value of $22.25 million per year, the Lions weren't inclined to do much more. In the end, Gibbs got a slight bump over Robinson. The problem with a hold-in is that it has to end at some point, because the season eventually starts. And both the team and the player need the player to be ready to go. For Gibbs, who had more "old money," the three-year, $67.5 million deal combines with his existing $17.476 million to create a five-year, $84.976 million contract. The per-year average from signing is $16.99 million. (Robinson's five-year deal has an average of $16.36 million.) We'll have a full breakdown of the Gibbs terms. The Robinson terms are here .
author: Mike Florio

title: Aaron Donald decision could be made in the coming days
summary: Donald could be on the field for 30-40 snaps in Week 1 vs. 49ers.
full_text: ' Get ready for a potential Michael Jordan-style press release . As retired defensive tackle Aaron Donald continues to work his way back into football shape, a decision regarding his potential return could happen in the coming days, per a source with knowledge of the situation. Donald's goal is to find out whether he can get back to being Aaron Donald again, the dominant, three-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year who has already done more than enough to be a no-brainer first-ballot Hall of Famer. If he decides to return, the Rams would ramp him up the same way they did when he missed all of training camp in 2017 and 2018, due to a holdout. The goal will be to get him on the field to engage in football activities in a team setting a few weeks before playing in a game. And if Donald does indeed emerge from retirement, the Rams would take him to Australia for the Week 1 game against the 49ers — with a goal, we're told, of having him on the field for 30-40 snaps.
author: Mike Florio

title: Cowboys rookie LB Jaishawn Barham has a groin injury
summary: Cowboys rookie linebacker Jaishawn Barham left Thursday's practice early.
full_text: ' Cowboys rookie linebacker Jaishawn Barham left Thursday's practice early. Todd Archer of ESPN reports that Barham has a groin injury that is not expected to keep him out long. Barham, a third-round pick, has stood out in camp. Barham has taken some first-team reps at inside linebacker, with defensive coordinator Christian Parker lauding Barham for bringing "a physicality and a demeanor to the inside of the defense." “It’s his ability to apply the things we’re coaching,” head coach Brian Schottenheimer said, via Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram . “We see and know the physicality, but to see it and apply it has been great.” In two seasons at Maryland and two at Michigan, Barham totaled 193 tackles, 23 tackles for loss, 12 sacks and seven pass deflections in 48 games.
author: Charean Williams

title: Jaguars sign LB Jahlani Tavai
summary: The Jaguars signed linebacker Jahlani Tavai, the team announced Thursday.
full_text: The Jaguars signed linebacker Jahlani Tavai, the team announced Thursday. In a corresponding move, the Jaguars waived linebacker Jared Bartlett with an injury designation. Tavai, 29, was released by the Patriots in March after spending the past two seasons in New England. In 2025, Tavai totaled 42 tackles and a forced fumble in 12 games with seven starts. He saw action on 228 defensive snaps and 218 on special teams. Tavai entered the NFL as a second-round pick of the Lions in 2019 and has played 107 games with 67 starts in his seven seasons. He has recorded 432 tackles, 25 tackles for loss, 14 quarterback hits, 14 passes defensed, six forced fumbles, 5.5 sacks, four interceptions and two fumble recoveries.
author: Charean Williams

title: NFL suspends Saints WR Brock Rechsteiner for the first six games
summary: The NFL has suspended Saints wide receiver Brock Rechsteiner for the first six games of the 2026 season.
full_text: The NFL has suspended Saints wide receiver Brock Rechsteiner for the first six games of the 2026 season. The NFL announced the suspension on the personnel notice for Thursday. It did not indicate the reason. Rechsteiner, an undrafted rookie, is eligible to participate in all preseason activities, including games, before the reduction to 53 players. It could mean the end of the NFL journey for the former Jacksonville State player. Rechsteiner is the son of Scott Rechsteiner, who wrestled under the aliases Scott Steiner and Big Poppa Pump and is in the WWE Hall of Fame. His uncle, Rick Steiner, was his father’s tag team partner, and Brock’s first cousin, Bronson Rechsteiner, currently wrestles as Bron Breakker.
author: Charean Williams

title: Falcons put Jalon Walker on IR, claim DB Keidron Smith off of waivers
summary: The Falcons officially brought linebacker Jalon Walker's season to an end on Thursday.
full_text: The Falcons officially brought linebacker Jalon Walker's season to an end on Thursday. Walker was placed on injured reserve after tearing his ACL in practice this week. The 2025 first-round pick will have surgery and then spend the coming months working his way back to health for his third season. The NFL's daily transaction report shows that the Falcons filled the open roster spot by claiming defensive back Keidron Smith off of waivers. He was cut by the Jets on Wednesday. Smith had 15 tackles in three games for the Jets last season. He had seven tackle in nine appearances for the Broncos in 2024.
author: Josh Alper

title: Cowboys claim TE Zack Kuntz off waivers
summary: The Cowboys lost Princeton Fant for the season to a torn ACL and they replaced him on the roster with another tight end on Thursday.
full_text: ' The Cowboys lost Princeton Fant for the season to a torn ACL and they replaced him on the roster with another tight end on Thursday. The NFL's daily transaction report shows that they have claimed Zack Kuntz off of waivers. Fant was placed on injured reserve in a corresponding move. Kuntz was waived by the Raiders on Thursday to end a brief stint with the team. He was a 2023 Jets seventh-round pick and played in two games during his time with the team. Jake Ferguson, Brevyn Spann-Ford, Luke Schoonmaker, Michael Trigg, and DJ Rogers are the other tight ends on the Cowboys roster.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jahmyr Gibbs agrees to three-year deal worth $22.5 million annually
summary: The Lions' fourth-year running back will receive $51.5 million in guarantees.
full_text: Jahmyr Gibbs' return to practice was a sign that a long-term deal with the Lions was close. Indeed, according to a source, the running back has agreed to a three-year, $67.5 million deal that could be worth up to $75.75 million. He will receive $51.5 million in guarantees. His deal follows Bijan Robinson and Jonathan Taylor's agreements with their teams this week. Gibbs had been holding in as he sought a long-term deal with the team. Gibbs, 24, enters his fourth season after 3,580 rushing yards, 39 rushing touchdowns, 1,449 receiving yards and 10 receiving touchdowns in his first three seasons while sharing time with David Montgomery. The Lions traded Montgomery to the Texans in the offseason. Gibbs has earned Pro Bowl honors in all three of his NFL seasons after the Lions made him the 12th overall pick in 2023.
author: Charean Williams

title: Colts sign free agent TE Pharaoh Brown
summary: The Colts signed free agent tight end Pharaoh Brown on Thursday, the team announced.
full_text: The Colts signed free agent tight end Pharaoh Brown on Thursday, the team announced. In a corresponding move, the Colts placed tight end Sean McKeon on injured reserve. McKeon, who has an undisclosed injury, will finish the season on injured reserve unless he reaches an injury settlement with the Colts. Brown returns to Indianapolis after spending time with the team in 2023. He played for the Cardinals in 2025, appearing in seven games with two starts. Brown caught two passes for 1 yard, while seeing action on 59 offensive snaps and 77 on special teams. Brown has also spent time with the Dolphins (2025), Seahawks (2024), Patriots (2023), Colts (2023), Browns (2018-20, 2022), Texans (2020-22) and Raiders (2017-18). He has appeared in 94 career games with 56 starts, totaling 74 receptions for 752 yards and three touchdowns.
author: Charean Williams

title: Christian Gonzalez: A.J. Brown and I are battling, getting each other better
summary: Thursday's practice at Patriots camp featured some fireworks between wide receiver A.J.
full_text: Thursday's practice at Patriots camp featured some fireworks between wide receiver A.J. Brown and cornerback Christian Gonzalez. Reporters at the workout said Gonzalez appeared to be talking trash to Brown after knocking a pass away from the wideout during a drill where they were matched up against one another. Brown engaged with the corner and wideout Kayshon Boutte stepped in to steer Brown away before things got any more heated. After practice, Gonzalez said that he thinks situations like that will help both players prepare for the weekly battles they have ahead of them. "It’s good on good ,” Gonzalez said. “He’s a No. 1 receiver in this league going up against a No. 1 corner. That’s how it’s going to go. It’s football at the end of the day. There’s never no disrespect or anything. We’re just battling and getting each other better. He’s going to face corners like that, that are going to yap at him and going to try to get in his head, and I’m going to face receivers like that who are strong and come right back at me. It’s great work for the both of us.” The Patriots have another week to go before their first game against another team, but they will get a chance to tangle with the Colts in a joint practice on Tuesday.
author: Josh Alper

title: Joe Buck, Troy Aikman enter contract year at ESPN
summary: The first hint came in April, when Joe Buck declared that he'd like to spend the rest of his career at ESPN — with the caveat that no talks had commenced on a contract that expires after the upcoming season.
full_text: The first hint came in April, when Joe Buck declared that he'd like to spend the rest of his career at ESPN — with the caveat that no talks had commenced on a contract that expires after the upcoming season. With the upcoming season coming very soon, both Buck and on-air partner Troy Aikman are entering the final years of their deals together. Via Michael McCarthy of Front Office Sports , CAA now represents both Buck and Aikman . As McCarthy notes, it's possible that CAA will negotiate them as a package deal. Both signed five-year deals for Monday Night Football in 2022. ESPN pays Aikman $18 million per year, while Buck gets $15 million annually. It's hard to imagine both leaving, primarily since there won't be many high-rent spots where both could go together. One destination could be Amazon, where both Al Michaels and Kirk Herbstreit have contracts that expire after the 2026 season.
author: Mike Florio

title: Panthers release OL Saahdiq Charles, WR Ainias Smith from IR
summary: The Panthers waived wide receiver Ainias Smith with an injury settlement and released guard Saahdiq Charles with an injury settlement, the team announced Thursday.
full_text: The Panthers waived wide receiver Ainias Smith with an injury settlement and released guard Saahdiq Charles with an injury settlement, the team announced Thursday. Charles went on injured reserve Wednesday with a calf injury, opening a roster spot for the return of offensive lineman Jake Curhan. Charles, 27, spent most of last season on the Panthers' practice squad, appearing in two games. He saw action on 10 special teams snaps. Smith went on injured reserve Wednesday with an undisclosed injury. The Eagles selected him in the fifth round of the 2024 draft. Smith appeared in seven games, starting one, and totaled seven receptions for 41 yards and one touchdown. He spent all of 2025 on the Panthers' practice squad.
author: Charean Williams

title: Jets claim DT Junior Tafuna off waivers
summary: Defensive tackle Junior Tafuna was dropped by the Texans on Wednesday, but he didn't have to wait long to find a new team.
full_text: Defensive tackle Junior Tafuna was dropped by the Texans on Wednesday, but he didn't have to wait long to find a new team. Connor Hughes of SNY reports that the Jets have claimed Tafuna off of waivers. They have waived defensive tackle Patrick Jenkins in a corresponding move. Tafuna signed with the Texans after going undrafted last year and returned to their practice squad after failing to make the cut to 53 players last summer. He did not appear in any regular season games for the team. Jenkins was signed by the Jets on Wednesday, so his stay on the 53-man roster turned out to be a very short one.
author: Josh Alper

title: Madden movie makes Prime Video debut on November 18
summary: On the Wednesday night before the first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game, another piece of NFL-related entertainment will debut.
full_text: '' On the Wednesday night before the first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game, another piece of NFL-related entertainment will debut. Via Rebecca Rubin of Variety , the Madden movie will debut November 18 on Prime Video. It's expected to have a limited theatrical release for awards-qualification purposes in November. It won't be widely distributed. John Madden, the legendary Raiders coach, broadcaster, and video-game mogul, is played by Nicolas Cage. Christian Bale, who played Batman in multiple Christopher Nolan films, plays Al Davis, the maverick owner whom the NFL often regarded as the Joker. The rest of the cast includes Kathryn Hahn. John Mulaney, Sienna Miller, and Shane Gillis. As Rubin notes, it's unclear why the film won't have a national theatrical run.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jon Gruden "fired up" to broadcast Bucs preseason game
summary: Jon Gruden, who won Super Bowl XXXVII as Tampa Bay's head coach, will be in the broadcast booth as the play-by-play announcer for the Bucs' second preseason game against the Chiefs on Aug. 22.
full_text: Jon Gruden, who won Super Bowl XXXVII as Tampa Bay's head coach, will be in the broadcast booth as the play-by-play announcer for the Bucs' second preseason game against the Chiefs on Aug. 22. He spoke with local Buccaneers media on Thursday, saying he's "fired up" for the gig. "We’ve got a great young team here, we’ve added some players," Gruden said in his press conference. "And to be up there with Ronde Barber for three-and-a-half hours, God knows what’s going to happen . But we’re going to have fun. We’re going to celebrate the Bucs and hopefully kick off what’s going to be what’s going to be a really special season." Gruden noted he's planning for the broadcast to be a lot more about Barber than himself. "I’ve heard I’m doing play-by-play, but I don’t know if we’ve solved anything," Gruden said. "It’s going to be Ronde’s show. He’s the star. I’m just — we’re going to have a production meeting, I know, on August 17 and we’re going to finalize the cadence. But I’m excited. I’m a little bit nervous. And as always, really fired up for football season — especially the Buccaneers." Gruden said he's missed the camaraderie of being around a broadcast team, which he got used to while working on Monday Night Football. He left the booth to come back to coaching with the Raiders in 2018. "I had a lot of fun doing it for nine years," Gruden said. "I was very fortunate, on Monday Night Football , especially the years with [Mike] Tirico. We had a lot of fun. We took every game like it was the Super Bowl — we took it very seriously, had a lot of fun. So, I enjoyed the profession. And at this point in my life, I still study football all the time, I’m still a big fan of the Bucs. I live right down the street. So, I’m really excited about it."
author: Myles Simmons

title: Giants CB Dru Phillips to miss time with a knee sprain
summary: The Giants will be missing a member of their secondary for a little while.
full_text: The Giants will be missing a member of their secondary for a little while. Cornerback Dru Phillips did not practice on Thursday and head coach John Harbaugh said, via Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News , that Phillips will miss more time as a result of a knee sprain. The Giants play their first preseason game against the Vikings on August 15. Phillips was a 2024 third-round pick and has played in 31 games over two seasons. He played in all 17 games last year and finished the season with 66 tackles, two interceptions and a fumble recovery while primarily working as a nickel corner. Ar'Darius Washington and Nic Jones are expected to see more time while Phillips is recovering.
author: Josh Alper

title: C.J. Gardner-Johnson "just can't wait" to face Texans in Week 1
summary: Safety C.J.
full_text: '' Safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson was back on the practice field for the Bills on Thursday after missing a few days with a calf injury and continued good health will leave him on track to make his regular season debut with the team in Week 1. That game will be against the Texans, which only adds to the importance for the veteran. Gardner-Johnson opened last season with the Texans, but was released after three games in the wake of a reported altercation with teammates in the wake of a 17-10 loss to the Jaguars in Week 3. Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans didn’t go into details about the reason for the move and said only that he thought it was best for the team. Gardner-Johnson said this offseason that he felt an issue with " the GM’s friend " during training camp set the wheels in motion on his departure and there was other discussion about him not fitting what the Texans wanted defensively, so it's clear that his time with Houston was both brief and eventful. On Thursday, Gardner-Johnson said the experience has added to his anticipation for the season opener. "It's a good team . Not saying nothing on the front office or the staff, but the players . . . they are good," Gardner-Johnson said, via Alaina Getzenberg of ESPN.com. "All the bulls—t that came out, it was lies, but whatever. I just can't wait to see 'em. . . . Be adults about the business. We here, we grown men, we all got kids. A five-second phone call don't justify nothing. And I feel like I need some respect, but I don't care for it no more." Gardner-Johnson will have another one of his former teams on deck in Week 2 when the Lions visit Buffalo for the first game in the new Highmark Stadium. A pair of wins would make for a doubly enjoyable way to start his run in Buffalo.
author: Josh Alper

title: Steelers first-round rookie Max Iheanachor leaves practice early
summary: Steelers first-round rookie Max Iheanachor left practice early Thursday with an apparent injury.
full_text: '' Steelers first-round rookie Max Iheanachor left practice early Thursday with an apparent injury. Alan Saunders of PghSteelersNow reports that Iheanachor walked to the sideline to have head athletic trainer Gabe Amponsah work on his neck and right shoulder area. Iheanachor then spoke with team physician Dr. Aaron Mares before walking toward the training room. Iheanachor, the 21st overall pick, has worked with the second team at right tackle. Broderick Jones moved to Iheanachor's spot for the rest of practice, with Jack Driscoll taking second-team reps at left tackle in Jones' stead. Iheanachor did not allow a sack in his senior season at Arizona State. He appeared in 32 career games, starting 31 for the Sun Devils. He was an All-Big 12 Second Team selection in 2025.
author: Charean Williams

title: Seahawks sign FB Brock Lampe, waive TE Lance Mason
summary: The defending champs have brought in a fullback.
full_text: '' The defending champs have brought in a fullback. Seattle announced on Thursday that the club has signed Brock Lampe. Lampe, 23, entered the league last year as an underrated free agent and spent the season on New England’s injured reserve. The Patriots let him go just late last month. As a corresponding move, the Seahawks waived tight end Lance Mason.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Jets RB Isaiah Davis will miss "a couple weeks" with a knee injury
summary: Jets running back Isaiah Davis will miss some time with a knee injury, coach Aaron Glenn announced Thursday.
full_text: ' Jets running back Isaiah Davis will miss some time with a knee injury, coach Aaron Glenn announced Thursday. Glenn did not specify the nature of the injury but said it is not serious. “He had a minor knee [injury],” Glenn said after practice, via Dennis Waszak of the Associated Press. “He’ll be out maybe a couple of weeks, but he’ll be back . I’m confident that he’ll be just fine going into the regular season.” The Jets open the regular season on Sept. 13 at Tennessee. Davis, 24, is entering his third NFL season after the Jets selected him in the fifth round. He is expected to have a complementary role behind Breece Hall and Braelon Allen while being a core special teams player. He had career highs with 236 yards rushing and 21 receptions last season in 16 games before missing the season finale with a concussion. In two seasons, Davis has rushed for 410 yards and a touchdown on 73 carries and caught 30 passes for 261 yards and a score.

title: Harrison Butker says new rule changed his approach to kickoffs and hurt his field goals
summary: When the NFL changed the kickoff rule two years ago, kickers began to experiment with different ways to kick the ball and make it harder to return.
full_text: ''' When the NFL changed the kickoff rule two years ago, kickers began to experiment with different ways to kick the ball and make it harder to return. Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker says that affected his approach to kicking, and his field goals suffered. Butker has had two straight seasons in which both his field goal rate and his extra point rate were below his career averages, and he says he thinks that's because he was tinkering too much with his kicking motion on kickoffs, at the expense of having a consistent kicking motion on field goals. "Field goals matter the most," Butker said. "Trying to hit those knuckleballs and the funny kickoffs maybe affected the field goals a little bit. I think halfway through the season last year I said, forget the kickoffs — not forget the kickoffs — but I'm just gonna hit a high hang time ball, good location, just focus on the location. I'm not gonna hit a low line-drive knuckleball. And I think that's helped my field goals because it's the same foot-to-ball contact. Good foot-to-ball contact on the field goal and just do the same thing on the kickoff rather than having two different swings. So that helped me the second half of the season and I'm sticking with that for training camp and this season." Butker's down year was far from the biggest problem in Kansas City last season, but the Chiefs are hoping for a more consistent Butker this season — and hoping he's back to making game-winning kicks in big games, after a season in which the Chiefs didn't win many big games.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Todd Monken reveals he offered Joe Thomas a full-time coaching job
summary: For a decade, Hall of Famer Joe Thomas anchored the Browns’ offensive line at left tackle.
full_text: For a decade, Hall of Famer Joe Thomas anchored the Browns’ offensive line at left tackle. With training camp ongoing, Thomas has been at the facility this week to assist with coaching the rebuilt group at the behest of head coach Todd Monken. Monken revealed to reporters after Thursday’s practice that he offered Thomas a full-time job after he was hired in January. “Well, when I was interviewing for the job and then when I got the job, I reached out to Joe ,” Monken said in his press conference. “Joe, obviously, played for [offensive line coach] George Warhop as well. And I said, hey, we’ve got a spot for you if you want to help us coach. And he said, ‘I’d love to coach.’ He said, ‘I don’t think I want to commit to an everyday contract.’ I said, ‘That’s fine. Anytime you want to come out and help our guys, you’re more than welcome.’ And we certainly would welcome him.” With the Browns bringing in offensive tackle Spencer Fano with the No. 9 overall pick of this year’s draft, Thomas likely had some useful pointers for the rookie to excel as he begins his first season.

title: Carson Beck passed every test in NFL debut, here's why history says it doesn't matter
summary: Beck checked every box in his first professional game, but recent rookie quarterbacks prove that preseason performances can be wildly misleading
full_text:
The biggest knock against Carson Beck at Georgia was that he was little more than a glorified game manager. He was surrounded by future NFL stars, and while the first-overall buzz followed him, skeptics wondered how much of the offense he was actually driving. Those questions grew louder in 2024 after names like Brock Bowers and Ladd McConkey left for the NFL and Beck's play became far more uneven.
An elbow injury just before halftime of the SEC Championship Game was the abrupt, inglorious end to his Bulldogs career. And instead of declaring for the draft, Beck transferred to Miami, where he took inventory of where he'd been and what he learned, and rediscovered himself in Coral Gables.
Oftentimes, it's the hard lessons that prompt the change you may not have known you needed. And for Beck, who admitted as much when we talked to him at his Pro Day back in March, he's a much better player today than he was at any point during his time at Georgia.
QB Carson Beck on his growth from Georgia to Miami. 🎙️: @ryanwilsonCBS pic.twitter.com/DU3WYbgX0c
And on Thursday night in the Hall of Fame game, we saw glimpses of what that could look like in the NFL. He's currently third on the depth chart behind Jacoby Brissett and Gardner Minshew, but in a perfect world, Beck would be the 2026 version of Tyler Shough: a Day 2 pick who played a ton of college ball, can run an offense efficiently, and can step into the starting job as a rookie and more than hold his own.
Beck has never been the quarterback who overwhelms you with highlight throws. He wins by staying on schedule . At Georgia, his 38.6% first-down rate ranked in the 95th percentile among draft-eligible quarterbacks from 2015-26, and he got the ball out quicker than anyone in this rookie class. That's also why Arizona made so much sense as a landing spot: Mike LaFleur's offense asks quarterbacks to process quickly, distribute accurately and let the system work for them -- exactly how Beck played his best football in college. And Beck certainly passed every test you could throw at a rookie making his first-ever start, even if it was the Hall of Fame game.
My co-host on the "With the First Pick" podcast, former Titans GM Ran Carthon, has seen a lot in his nearly two decades in NFL front offices; he drafted Will Levis, was in San Francisco with Trey Lance and Brock Purdy, and St. Louis with Jared Goff. Earlier this week, I asked him what he wanted to see from Beck in his preseason debut :
"First, I want to see how efficiently he operates. Can he get in and out of the huddle, get everyone lined up and handle the motions, shifts and adjustments without things speeding up on him? …
"Then I want to see how he handles the bright lights. I know it's just the Hall of Fame Game, but this is his first professional football action. Is it going to be too much for him? …
"My advice would be simple: it's just football. Don't make it any more than that. You don't have to be the hero. Be 1-of-11. Play point guard, get the ball to the guys who can make plays, and just play football."
Beck not only took Ran's advice – he ran with it. And yes, I'll say it again: IT'S JUST ONE PRESEASON GAME. But you'd much rather see it unfold like this than see him throw an interception, take a couple of sacks, and look indecisive before and after the snap. Instead, Beck, whose big-time-throw rate hovered around 3% in college (by comparison, Justin Herbert's big-time-throw rate was 9.2% in 2017 at Oregon), was slinging it early on Thursday night:
What a throw by Carson Beck! @ProFootballHOF Game on NBC Stream on @NFLPlus + Peacock pic.twitter.com/ai2A4lm7z0
Carson Beck to Jalen Brooks. WOW. @ProFootballHOF Game on NBC Stream on @NFLPlus + Peacock pic.twitter.com/VjnMEP2mIQ
. @carsonbeck01 drops it in a bucket 🪣 @ProFootballHOF Game on NBC Stream on @NFLPlus + Peacock pic.twitter.com/fZQpMPha1q
By the time it was over, Beck finished 15 of 19 for 188 yards, a touchdown and no turnovers. And, sure, the rookie gave Cardinals fans plenty to be happy about, at least for one night. So what does it mean beyond one encouraging August performance? If history is any guide, not a whole helluva lot.
Beck's debut belongs in the same bucket as every other rookie quarterback making his first preseason appearance: it's worth watching, worth evaluating and worth filing away – but it's far from definitive. The last decade is littered with quarterbacks who looked like future stars in August before stumbling once the games counted, and just as many who struggled in their first taste of NFL action before developing into franchise quarterbacks.
Here are some of the best reminders – both good and bad – why one preseason game never tells the whole story.
Preseason Week 1 stats: 10 of 12, 139 yards, 2 TD, 0 INT
Prescott looked completely comfortable running the offense in his preseason debut, throwing two touchdowns, and a decade later, he's still entrenched as the starter in Dallas.
Last NFL season (2025, Cowboys)
Preseason Week 1 stats: 11 of 20, 212 yards, 2 TD, 0 INT
Mayfield's debut accelerated calls for him to replace veteran Tyrod Taylor, who was also in his first year in Cleveland.
Last NFL season (2025, Bucs)
Preseason Week 1 stats: 14 of 20, 142 yards, 1 TD; 5 carries, 33 yards, 1 TD
After a slow start, Fields got hot in the second half with big-time throws and highlight-reel runs. The debut immediately fueled public pressure for Chicago to move him ahead of veteran Andy Dalton. Fields made his first start in Week 3 of the regular season.
Last NFL season (2025, Jets)
Preseason Week 1 stats: 13 of 15, 95 yards, 2 TD, 0 INT
Pickett capped his debut with a game-winning touchdown drive and completed all but two of his throws. He made his first NFL regular-season start in Week 5, replacing Mitchell Trubisky.
Last NFL season (2025, Raiders)
Preseason Week 1 stats: 8 of 11, 82 yards, 1 TD; 5 carries, 36 yards
Thompson-Robinson was the clear star of the 2023 Hall of Fame Game, flashing accuracy, mobility and composure that, admittedly, had me believing the Browns had unearthed a late-round gem. He started just 5 games in two seasons for the Browns before being traded to the Eagles (incidentally, this was the trade that sent Pickett from Philly to Cleveland). DTR now plays in the UFL.
Last NFL season (2024, Browns)
Preseason Week 1 stats: 4 of 9, 38 yards, 1 INT
The No. 1 overall pick looked uncomfortable in his preseason debut, and Goff eventually opened the regular season on the bench before developing into one of the best QBs in the league after he was traded from the Rams to the Lions.
Last NFL season (2025, Lions)
Preseason Week 1 stats: 6 of 13, 41 yards
Rosen's preseason debut mirrored his NFL career. He made his first start in Week 4 of his rookie season, but by 2019, he had been traded to Miami. He would play for five more teams over the next three seasons and has been out of the league since 2022.
Last NFL season (2021, Falcons)
Preseason Week 1 stats: 1 of 9, 11 yards
Corral's debut was one of the roughest by any rookie quarterback in recent memory. Once considered the top QB in a weak 2022 class, he never played a regular-season snap in the NFL.

Obviously, Stroud went on to have a lights-out rookie campaign and while he hasn't yet played up to that level the last two seasons, he's helped the Texans to the postseason every year.

title: 2026 Hall of Fame Game where to watch: Carson Beck to start at QB for Cardinals
summary: Football is officially back as the Panthers and Cardinals kick off the preseason in Canton, Ohio, with plenty of new faces on display
full_text:
Football is officially here. The 2026 NFL season begins on Thursday, when the Carolina Panthers and Arizona Cardinals face off in the annual Hall of Fame Game. This preseason game is more unique than the other exhibition matchups. Not only is it the first one of the year, but it's also the only NFL matchup played in "Football Heaven" -- right next to the Pro Football Hall of Fame.
The Panthers are coming off an 8-9 season, which landed them in the playoffs. Carolina became the fifth team in NFL history to win their division with a losing record, and owned the third-worst point differential (-69) by a division winner since 1970. However, the Panthers did have the Offensive Rookie of the Year in wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan , and made several notable additions on the defensive side of the ball this offseason, such as pass rusher Jaelan Phillips and linebacker Devin Lloyd . The goal is to build off what was accomplished in 2025.
Remaining healthy will be a primary goal for head coach Dave Canales on Thursday, as the Panthers have had a rough start to training camp. They lost pass rusher Nic Scourton to a torn ACL on the first day of workouts, then rookie wide receiver Chris Brazzell II tore his LCL. He will miss the entire 2026 season as well.
As for the Cardinals, they are beginning a new era. Jonathan Gannon was fired after a 3-14 season and replaced by former Los Angeles Rams offensive coordinator Mike LaFleur, while the franchise also parted ways with former No. 1 overall pick quarterback Kyler Murray after seven seasons. Arizona became the first franchise in NFL history to finish at least 9 games behind every team in its division. There are pieces in place for the Cardinals, such as tight end Trey McBride and rookie running back Jeremiyah Love , but there's clearly plenty of work to be done. Thursday night is a great opportunity for this new coaching staff to get a look at their young talent in a game situation.
Let's break down the first exhibition matchup of the 2026 NFL season and some players to watch. First, here's how you can watch the game.
Date: Thursday, Aug. 6 | Time: 8 p.m. ET Location: Tom Benson Hall of Fame Stadium (Canton, Ohio) Channel: NBC | Stream: fubo Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Panthers -1.5, O/U 36.5 ( DraftKings Sportsbook)
LaFleur confirmed Wednesday that Love will not play in the Hall of Fame Game. However, the Cardinals have three other preseason matchups for Love to gear up for his rookie season.
The Cardinals made Love the first running back drafted in the top five since Saquon Barkley in 2018. It snapped the longest drought where a running back wasn't drafted in the top five all-time, and Love automatically becomes the highest-paid running back in the NFL with $50.5 million guaranteed in his rookie contract.
Not every franchise would draft a running back in the top three, but Love is that kind of prospect. He led the FBS in rushing touchdowns (35) and total touchdowns (40) over the past two years, and averaged 114.3 rushing yards per game in his final season with Notre Dame. However, we saw an elite running back prospect not live up to lofty expectations just last year, as No. 6 overall pick Ashton Jeanty finished 18th in rushing with 975 yards.
Miami's Carson Beck was the third quarterback selected in this past draft, and he will get the start under center on Thursday night.
In his one season with the Hurricanes, Beck completed 72.4% of his passes for 3,813 yards, 30 touchdowns and 12 interceptions while leading Miami to the College Football Playoff National Championship. CBS Sports compared Beck to former No. 1 overall pick Jared Goff as a prospect, as he's an effective pocket passer. However, Beck clearly struggled when pressured or forced to work off-schedule. With a strong NFL debut on Thursday, he could get the NFL world talking more about the quarterback situation in Arizona.
There are many rookies I'm excited to watch this preseason around the NFL, such as former Arkansas quarterback Taylen Green with the Cleveland Browns , the feisty Indiana corner D'Angelo Ponds , who is now playing for the New York Jets , and the new Tampa Bay Buccaneers wideout Ted Hurst from Georgia State. Former Georgia Tech quarterback Haynes King is definitely on that list as well.
I'm not sure if King is an NFL quarterback, but I'm very sure he's a fun player to watch. King is a dual-threat athlete who is going to scramble on Thursday night. He rushed for 37 touchdowns in his collegiate career, averaging more than one a game over his last two seasons for Georgia Tech. King ran a 4.46 40-yard dash at the NFL combine and is a gritty competitor who will take chances.
Sometimes big things come in small packages, and that's true with Jimmy Horn Jr . The 5-foot-8, 170-pound pass-catcher out of Colorado was a sixth-round pick of Carolina last year, and caught 11 of 15 targets for 108 yards in 13 games played. With rookie Chris Brazzell II out for the season and Xavier Legette nursing an injury, Horn has a legitimate opportunity to compete for touches this year.
While he's a smaller player, Horn possesses impressive speed, is a good route-runner, and is super competitive. He's a tough cover if you leave him one-on-one -- as some Panthers defensive backs have discovered over the past few weeks.
Jimmy Horn’s Speed Is Overwhelming pic.twitter.com/IEmMP7msur

title: Jahmyr Gibbs becomes highest-paid running back in history after agreeing on three-year extension, per report
summary: Gibbs' deal comes on the heels of Bijan Robinson's massive deal
full_text:
Jahmyr Gibbs ' hold-in has come to an emphatic end. Gibbs has become the highest-paid running back in NFL history after he and the Detroit Lions agreed to a three-year, $67.5 million deal that could be worth up to $75.75 million, sources confirmed to CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz. The deal also includes $51.5 million guaranteed.
Gibbs' deal comes two days after the Atlanta Falcons and Bijan Robinson agreed to terms on a three-year extension worth up to $75 million, with $51 million guaranteed. Robinson's deal was the highest for a running back in NFL history.
Earlier in the day, fellow running back Jonathan Taylor agreed to terms with the Indianapolis Colts on a two-year, $44 million extension. Taylor's new deal comes three years after he signed a three-year, $42 million deal that, at the time, was a monumental step for running backs from a monetary standpoint.
Along with Taylor, Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley was a key player in helping the running back position rebound after it was devalued for a time. Barkley became the first running back to earn at least $20 million annually when he signed a two-year, $41.2 million extension last season after rushing for over 2,000 yards and helping the Eagles win the Super Bowl .
Taylor and Barkley are now flanked by Gibbs and Robinson in the "$20 million" club.
Christian McCaffrey ( 49ers )
De'Von Achane ( Dolphins )
Kenneth Walker III ( Chiefs )
Gibbs' production during his first three seasons more than validates his historic extension. According to CBS Sports Research, his 49 touchdowns during his first three seasons are the most in NFL history. He is first in scrimmage yards (3,768) and first in scrimmage touchdowns (38) in the NFL over the past two seasons.
Gibbs is also the second player in NFL history (with Nick Chubb being the first) to average at least 5.0 yards per carry in each of his first three seasons (with a minimum of 150 touches). His 5.9 yards-per-touch average during his first three seasons is tied for the second-most in NFL history since the 1970 merger.
With a new contract in tow, Gibbs will continue the work of helping the Lions rebound from last year's disappointing season. Detroit finished with a winning record for a fourth straight year, but they missed the playoffs for the first time since 2022, when they also finished 9-8.
