summary: Taylor's new deal checks in just behind Falcons' Bijan Robinson
full_text:
Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor is now a much richer man. The star seventh-year back has signed a two-year contract extension with his team that pays him a base value of $44 million, $39 million of which is guaranteed, according to multiple reports . The contract has a maximum value of $47 million. The Colts made the signing official on Thursday.
The deal comes together just days after Atlanta Falcons star Bijan Robinson signed a new deal with a base value of $22.75 million per year, which clearly set the market for running back contracts. Taylor now becomes the second-highest-paid running back in the NFL in terms of average annual value, jumping ahead of Philadelphia Eagles star Saquon Barkley , who sits at $20.6 million.
Christian McCaffrey ( 49ers )
De'Von Achane ( Dolphins )
Kenneth Walker III ( Chiefs )
The $39 million full guarantee, meanwhile, slightly surpasses Robinson for the most ever for a running back, excluding Jeremiyah Love's fully guaranteed rookie-scale contract as the No. 3 pick in this year's NFL Draft , according to Over the Cap.
Taylor had been heading into the final season of the three-year, $42 million extension he signed in 2023. He is set to draw a base salary of $11.98 million in 2026 while counting for $15.562 million against the cap.
Taylor led the NFL in both carries (323) and rushing touchdowns (18) last season, and has run for at least 1,400 yards and 11 touchdowns in each of the last two years. He's heading into his age-27 season and is the clear centerpiece of the Indianapolis offense.
The Colts started last season absolutely on fire offensively under quarterback Daniel Jones , leading the league in scoring for the first half of the season. They slowed down a bit after Jones suffered an initial leg injury, then suffered further after Jones tore his Achilles and the team had to turn to Philip Rivers , whom they signed off the street. With Jones back healthy in time for training camp, they are trying to recapture the form they had at the start of last year, and Taylor is clearly one of the keys to their doing so.
Of course, the Colts also spent a bunch of money to retain Jones this offseason, handing him a two-year, $88 million contract to return to the fold. Field-stretching wide receiver Alec Pierce also received a big-money contract, with the Colts re-signing him for $114 million over four years. Indianapolis is now clearly counting on that trio to hold down the fort down the offense over the next couple of years.
author: Jared Dubin

title: Why you should watch Panthers-Cardinals in Hall of Fame Game, plus ranking the NFL's top 10 play-callers
summary: Here's everything you need to know about the NFL for Aug. 6
full_text:
Hello football friends, and welcome to the Thursday edition of the Pick Six newsletter!
After 179 days of waiting, football is finally back. Have I been counting down since February? Yes, and yes, I clearly need a hobby.
The Hall of Fame Game kicks off tonight, and sure, there's a good chance that you won't be able to name a single player on the field in the fourth quarter, but that's the beauty of preseason football . If you need a reason to watch tonight's game, don't worry, we're going to give you a few reasons why you should tune in. With that in mind, let's get to the rundown.
As always, here's your daily reminder to tell all your friends to sign up for the newsletter. To get them signed up, all you have to do is click here .
The first game of the 2026 season is officially here, which is a good thing, because I was starting to experience football withdrawal symptoms. The game tonight will feature the head coaching debut of Arizona's Mike LaFleur, who was hired in January to take over for Jonathan Gannon.
The game will be kicking off from Canton, Ohio, at 8 p.m. ET on NBC and the fact that NBC has the game is one reason why you should be watching. Tonight's game will mark the NBC debut of former Steelers coach Mike Tomlin, and it will be interesting to see how he handles his new job.
Besides Tomlin, here are a few other things to know heading into tonight's game and a few reasons why you might want to watch:
Breech's pick: Cardinals 20-17 over Panthers (Cardinals cover +1). It's the bottom of the Panthers roster against the bottom of the Cardinals roster, so it's hard to pick a winner here, but I'm going with Arizona, only because I think Mike LaFleur would like to start his career off with a win.
The Hall of Fame Game is just an appetizer when it comes to the festivities this weekend. The main course will be coming on Saturday with the enshrinement of the Pro Football Hall of Fame's class of 2026. If you're planning to watch induction ceremony this weekend, you better clear your schedule on Saturday afternoon because that's when the ceremony will be kicking off. After years of holding the enshrinement ceremony in prime time, the Hall of Fame moved the ceremony to noon ET in 2022, and that's where it will be once again this year. (The ceremony will be televised by both ESPN and NFL Network.)
The Hall of Fame's Class of 2026 consists of five players, including a KICKER. Let's take a look at the class:
Vinatieri is just the third pure placekicker ever to make the Hall of Fame, joining Jan Stenerud and Morten Andersen. One other notable fact about this weekend is that Kuechly will become the second-youngest Hall of Famer ever when he's inducted on Saturday. The 2013 NFL Defensive Player of the Year just turned 35 in April. The only player who was younger at the time of his induction was Gale Sayers, who was 34 when he was enshrined in 1977.
If you're wondering who might make the Hall of Fame in the future, Bryan DeArdo went through and identified one active player from each team who could eventually end up in Canton and you can check that out here .
After ranking the top 10 head coaches in the NFL earlier this week, you might have thought that we were done ranking things, but we're not, we're never done. Today, we're going to rank the top offensive and defensive play-callers in the NFL.
We rounded up 12 of our NFL experts and had them vote on the top play-callers and I'm going to unveil our ranking for the top 10 defensive play-callers.
1. Mike Macdonald ( Seahawks head coach) 2. Steve Spagnuolo ( Chiefs defensive coordinator) 3. Jesse Minter ( Ravens head coach) 4. Vic Fangio ( Eagles defensive coordinator) 5. Brian Flores (Vikings defensive coordinator) 6. Robert Saleh ( Titans head coach) 7. Chris Shula ( Rams defensive coordinator) 8. Vance Joseph ( Broncos defensive coordinator) 9. Anthony Campanile (Jaguars defensive coordinator) 10. Matt Burke ( Texans defensive coordinator)
It's kind of crazy to think that Macdonald and Minter were on the same staff in Baltimore for four seasons (2017-20).
As for the top ranked guys on the offensive side of the ball, you'll have to check out our full story here if you want to see that part of the list.
If there's one thing you can count on every year in the NFL, it's that your going to see multiple new playoff teams during the upcoming season. There have been at least four new playoff teams in every season played since 1990, so it almost feels like a lock that we'll once again see that happen this year.
With that in mind, Zach Pereles decided to take a look around the AFC to try and figure out which teams might make the postseason this year after missing out last year.
Here are the top three teams on his list:
Pereles also made a prediction on several teams that could take a step back after making the playoffs last year and you can check out that list here .
NFL owners aren't allowed to gamble on the NFL, but apparently, they can tell you what they would bet on if they were allowed to gamble and that's what Jimmy Haslam did recently.
The Browns owner has apparently been paying close attention to the Over/Under total that his team has been given and we know that because he specifically mentioned it during a recent press conference.
"I would say this, and we never do this, but I think the odds are for us to win five and a half games," Haslam said. "I'll take the over."
Taking the over on the Browns might seem slightly crazy, but I think I actually agree with him and there's one big reason why: The schedule.
I'm not sure if I've gone completely crazy, but I do think the Browns will top 5.5 wins in 2026. You can read my full breakdown of the situation here .
It's been a busy few days around the NFL, and since it's nearly impossible to keep track of everything, I put together a quick roundup for you.
author: John Breech

title: Renner's 2027 NFL Draft scouting series: Ranking top 10 defensive tackles
summary: After only one defensive tackle cracked Round 1 in 2026, the 2027 class already looks much deeper
full_text:
After a 2026 class that only saw one defensive tackle, Clemson's Peter Woods, sneak into the back end of Round 1, early tape suggests big changes in 2027. Talent abounds throughout this class, with the top six prospects all having a real chance to end up as first-rounders. What makes it so intriguing is the youth. Three of the top four on this list are rising juniors, and all have well-rounded skill sets. That means there will be a lot of competition to track who DT1 will be throughout the season.
Positional rankings: IOL • S • LB • DT • TE • OT • RB • CB • EDGE • WR • QB
Note: ⭐️ represents each player's 247Sports star rating as a high school recruit
For a true sophomore, Stone has some prodigious pop behind his hands. He is a pure power defensive tackle already and ragdolled some of college football's best in the SEC last season. The scary thing is that strength can improve throughout a collegiate and even an NFL career in a way that explosiveness and speed cannot. For him to be this imposing this early on is a strong signal.
David Stone (6’3 310) Oklahoma ✅ Quick to shoot gaps ✅ Reported 35” arm length ✅ 26 pressures during 2025 ✅ 13.0% stop rate was among the highest for any defender in the country during the 2025 season pic.twitter.com/rB4ZScvIA3
This isn't terribly surprising for the former 5-star recruit and top-10 overall player in the 2024 recruiting class. While I'd like to see more production as a pass-rusher than his 28 pressures last season, he doesn't need to improve much to end up a first-rounder.
Trying to block the 6-foot-3, 330-pound Washington doesn't seem like it would be a lot of fun. That's because a. He's very explosive off the line for his size. He's excellent and maintains a low center of gravity into contact. You're not going to be able to keep him out of the backfield if he wants to go there, but you can only hope to get him off-balance enough to keep him from making plays. That combination gives him a high floor vs. the run when projecting him to the NFL.
Oregon DT A’Mauri Washington (6-3, 330) would’ve been my DT2 in THIS NFL Draft Firmly in DT1 talks. So quick off the 🏈w/ridiculous athleticism. Moves like he’s 300 🦆8 batted passes led FBS 🦆12 QB hurries in 2024 🦆18 in 2025 1st Round Bound for 2027 pic.twitter.com/O7VGqPz8mM
He needs more than if he's going to be a consistent pass-rushing threat in the league, though. His ability to separate off blocks once engaged is easily the biggest hole in his game. Most of his wins come at the snap, and his ability to string together moves with his hands still remains to be seen.
While there are a lot of different body types that can play defensive tackle in the NFL, Echoles possesses one that could really only fit at defensive tackle. At 6-foot-2, he is thick from head to toe. The kind of build where I'm not sure he could reach 250 pounds, even with Tony Horton personally training him. It makes moving him in the run game a tall task for opposing linemen.
Will Echoles Cut Ups https://t.co/fTASIhlnhz pic.twitter.com/tnydrCBsbW
At that size, I love that he almost never comes off the field still. He played the most snaps of any Power-4 defensive tackle last season and the third-most in the FBS. Despite the heavy workload, it's rare to see him gassed, and he has a knack for making plays. He finished with the second-most run stops among Power-4 defensive tackles behind only second-rounder Kayden McDonald. That's incredibly impressive for a player who was only 19 years old all season. In what looks like an extremely talented defensive tackle class, Echoles will have a real case for the top player at his position next spring.
Scott got lost in one of the best defensive lines in modern college football history, but he's a dynamic playmaker in his own right. He was an afterthought for the Hurricanes staff to start the season, but by the year's end, he played a career-high 52 snaps in the National Title against Indiana.
I am officially a big Justin Scott fan pic.twitter.com/QlRKaGwQo0
What gets me excited about Scott's sophomore tape is the pass-rushing potential. He had 17 pressures in his final seven games. His two-hand strike stuns most linemen, and then he's quick enough to slip by en route to the quarterback. Obviously, I'd like to see it for a full season, but there's more than enough on tape last year to know Scott has the goods.
Gadson was a backup for two seasons in Lexington after suffering a knee injury in the spring of his freshman year. He broke out in a big way last fall with 20 pressures. He's got high-end traits to be a pass-rush threat at the next level with long limbs and a swift first step. Unfortunately for his draft prospects, Gadson often played out of position at nose tackle for the Wildcats last fall, when he's much more of a 3-4 defensive end. Hopefully, that changes under the new coach, Will Stein.
I was floored when Moten decided to return to school this fall, as he had the kind of twitchy athleticism for a defensive tackle that the 2026 draft class was short on. That could have seen him boosted to a top-50 selection, but now he's back for a fifth season to take a swing at the first round.
Moten's calling card is his light feet as a pass-rusher that allow him to dance past opposing linemen. He pairs them with active hands and good body control to be a consistent pass-rushing threat on the interior.
I've been known to overvalue undersized, athletic 3-techniques in the past, and Brewu is precisely that. What separates Brewu's game from your average 6-foot-1, 285-pound collegiate defensive tackle is his strength through contact. He doesn't get jostled around nearly as much as you'd expect from an undersized tackle and can really do damage with his hands. Make no mistake, however, Brewu is a three-technique only in the NFL. Being as productive as he was in only two seasons at Pittsburgh before transferring makes me excited about where his game could end up by the time he declares for the draft.
Notre Dame DT Francis Brewu: Extremely strong individual pic.twitter.com/ySvO2UfaZ9
Horace Lockett (6’5 362) UCF ✅ Massive frame ✅ 76.9 run defense grade in 2025 ✅ Power to push the pocket ✅ 7.0% career missed tackle rate pic.twitter.com/pqUDpZsZpP
Alexander will forever be known as the transfer portal poster boy after his Instagram post in a Penn State jersey (on a visit) flexing his right biceps featuring a Georgia tattoo (his original school) with a USC profile picture (where he spent 2023-24).
His talent has never been in question as a former top recruit, but his development did not take hold until his first season with the Ducks. You really saw him unlock the high-end strength he possesses throughout his frame. He was far more violent getting off blocks, and he finished with the second-most run stops of any returning defensive tackle.
Oregon DT Bear Alexander really lives up to his name with the violence he brings on every snap. His hands are legitimate weapons. pic.twitter.com/Og5mo1Im0C
Holmes isn't that physically imposing with a slight frame for a defensive tackle and limited length, but he makes up for it with a quick first step and consistent hand placement. No one on this list caught shoulder pads as consistently in the run game as Holmes did last season. Even on a loaded defensive line, I'd argue he was clearly the best run defender. The only question is how that will translate to the NFL, given less-than-prototypical traits at the position? He has another year to prove it's not a fluke.
Note: These aren't necessarily the next three players in my rankings, but rather three prospects who caught my eye for one reason or another.
Sigler isn't an uber-traitsy prospect by any means, but he dominated his competition at Arkansas State last year. That came after three years at West Alabama, where he started his career. If he can be similarly productive in the SEC, he'll get on radars very quickly.
Abasiri looks like a lab-built defensive tackle with incredibly long arms…
author: Mike Renner

title: Predicting every NFL team's best current Hall of Fame candidate: Aaron Rodgers, Travis Kelce among locks
summary: Which player from your favorite team has the best chance to eventually earn a bronze bust in Canton?
full_text:
There is no official criterion when determining who is enshrined in the Pro Football Hall of Fame. That being said, based on who has and who hasn't been enshrined over the past 50 years, it's safe to say that there are certain obvious characteristics when determining bronze busts and gold jackets. And there is no better time to examine those than the 2026 Hall of Fame Game.
Using the interpretation of some of the unspoken criteria used when determining who gets into the Hall of Fame, we've created a list of each NFL team's current player who has the best shot at being enshrined in Canton once their career is over. Here was the criteria used when selecting the most likely players on each NFL team that could be considered a "lock" if their careers ended today:
Did your team's best player make the cut? Let's find out.
Current Hall of Fame lock: No
The hard-hitting safety enters the 2026 season as an eight-time Pro Bowler and two-time first-team All-Pro. It's hard to make the Hall of Fame as a safety, though, so for Baker to truly have a legitimate shot at Canton one day, either he or the Cardinals need to win some hardware in the coming years. Baker is responsible for 1,021 career tackles in 138 regular-season games, including 678 solo tackles. He's exceeded 100 tackles six times, including 164 in 2024.
Current Hall of Fame lock: No
Last season, Robinson unofficially supplanted Saquon Barkley and Derrick Henry as the NFL's best running back. At 24 years old, Robinson is just getting into his prime seasons. If he continues to mimic the success he had in the previous two seasons, Robinson will have a strong argument for his future Hall of Fame candidacy.  Robinson's 3,910 rushing yards through his first 51 games represent an impressive Hall of Fame trajectory.
Current Hall of Fame lock: Yes
Henry punched his future ticket to Canton during his first two seasons with the Ravens, when he hit several career milestones that included 100 career touchdown runs and 13,000 career rushing yards. Henry enters the 2026 season ranked fourth all-time in career touchdown runs and 10th in both career rushing yards and career total touchdowns.
Current Hall of Fame lock: No, but getting closer
Allen has had a great career so far, but he'll need to have a few more Pro Bowl-caliber seasons before he can be considered a future Hall of Famer. With a league MVP in tow, a Super Bowl win may be all Allen needs to be considered a lock for future induction. Allen boasts 30,102 career passing yards and 220 touchdowns. He will also break 5,000 rushing yards and 80 rushing touchdowns by October of this season.
Current Hall of Fame lock: No
A former first-round pick, Brown had the most complete year of his career in 2023, setting career highs with 103 tackles in addition to two sacks, an interception and six pass breakups. After an injury wiped out virtually his entire 2024 season, Brown returned to form last season while helping the Panthers capture the NFC South.
Current Hall of Fame lock: No
Joe Burrow received consideration, but there's no denying that Chase is more deserving of this spot given what he has done in his career up to this point. He's a five-time Pro Bowler who, in 2024, won the coveted "triple crown" after leading the league in receptions, receiving yards and touchdown catches. Chase is certainly off to a Hall of fame start thanks to his 520 catches, 6,837 receiving yards and 54 touchdowns in addition to his individual honors.
Current Hall of Fame lock: No
Thuney's career has included two Super Bowl wins with the Patriots, two more Super Bowl wins with the Chiefs and three consecutive Pro Bowl berths entering this season. Now 33, Thuney will need to continue to rack up Pro Bowl selections if he is going to have a serious Hall of Fame case someday.
Current Hall of Fame lock: No
Ward, who recently received a hefty contract extension, has been one of the league's top cornerbacks since his rookie season back in 2018. Some All-Pros nod, and team success would greatly increase Ward's future Hall of Fame chances. Ward has 18 picks and 104 pass defenses in 110 career regular-season games.
Current Hall of Fame lock: No
Oddly, Lamb's success in Dallas has somewhat gone under the radar. He's been a Pro Bowler each of the last five years and, in 2023, broke Michael Irvin's single-season franchise receiving record. For Lamb's career to seriously merit Hall of Fame consideration someday, he'll probably need to get more All-Pro nods. A receiving title or two wouldn't hurt, either. Lamb has 571 career catches for 7,416 yards and 41 touchdowns.
Current Hall of Fame lock: No
Surtain has quickly blossomed into one of the NFL's premier cornerbacks. He's earned five Pro Bowl nods and two All-Pro selections. In 2024, he became the first defensive back this decade to win Defensive Player of the Year.
Current Hall of Fame lock: No
Hutchinson got the nod over Amon-Ra St. Brown and Penei Sewell , who are also enjoying strong starts to their careers. Less than a year after breaking his leg, Hutchinson recorded a career-high 14.5 sacks in 2025. Barring injury, there's a very good chance that Hutchinson will join the short list of players who have reached 100 career sacks before turning 30.
Current Hall of Fame lock: No, but trending in that direction
Parsons was in the middle of another banner season until he suffered a torn ACL in Week 14. If Parsons can return to his preinjury form, he should be considered a future Hall of Fame lock. Primarily as a member of the Dallas Cowboys, Parsons registered 65 career regular-season sacks and 297 tackles over 77 games.
Current Hall of Fame lock: No, but on the cusp
Hunter would crack any list naming the NFL's most underrated players. The 31-year-old is a five-time Pro Bowler and is currently tied with J.J. Watt on the NFL's career sack list. Hunter is fewer than 10 sacks away from cracking the top-30 in career sacks.
Current Hall of Fame lock: No, but trending in that direction
You can't have a better start to a career than the one that Nelson has enjoyed. Through eight seasons, Nelson has earned eight Pro Bowl and three All-Pro nods. He's two selections away from becoming only the 13th offensive lineman in history with double-digit Pro Bowl nods.
Current Hall of Fame lock: No
Hines has had an impressive career so far, including two Pro Bowl nods and a career-high 17.5 sacks in 2023. He'll have to start stacking up Pro Bowls, however, if he is going to have a legitimate shot at making the Hall of Fame someday. While 2023 has been his signature season to date, he boasts 61 overall career sacks since his arrival from Kentucky.
Current Hall of Fame lock: Yes
The Chiefs have two slam-dunk future Hall of Famers in Kelce and quarterback Patrick Mahomes . Kelce was picked here largely because of the fact that his career is winding down, whereas Mahomes is still adding chapters to his career. Kelce's legacy includes three Super Bowl wins, 11 consecutive Pro Bowl nods and being the postseason's all-time leading pass catcher.
Current Hall of Fame lock: No
Still only 28 (he'll turn 29 later this month), Crosby has been one of the league's most destructive defenders since his rookie season. He's made the Pro Bowl each of the last five years and has led the NFL in tackles for loss twice. Crosby already has 69.5 sacks to his name, including five seasons with double digits.
Current Hall of Fame lock: No, but close
While he is on the downturn of his career, Mack has nonetheless put together a career worthy of future Hall of Fame consideration. His list of career milestones includes a DPOY, nine Pro Bowls, three All-Pros and an All-Decade Team selection. Here are the numbers: 662 career tackles, 481 solo tackles, 113 sacks and 36 forced fumbles.
Current Hall of Fame lock: Yes
Davante Adams and Myles Garrett both have strong Hall of Fame arguments, but Stafford has the edge after winning his first league MVP in 2025. Stafford has also won a Super Bowl ring and is top-10…
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Steelers training camp overreactions: Drew Allar outplaying Will Howard? Is Rico Dowdle the new RB1?
summary: Sorting out what's fact and what's fiction from Steelers training camp
full_text:
LATROBE, Pa. -- For a team that is bringing back most of its starters, there remain a lot of unknowns as it relates to the Pittsburgh Steelers as they continue to move through their second week of training camp.
Who will be backing up Aaron Rodgers when the Steelers open the regular season? Who is the starting running back? Are the new receivers making an impact? Will Mike McCarthy regret his decision to have a tackling-free training camp?
Pittsburgh's two most recent open practices provided insight regarding each of the above questions. And while things could obviously change between now and Week 1, here is what we currently know based on sideline observations from Saint Vincent College earlier this week.
Overreaction or reality: Reality
Allar was slightly more impressive than Howard during this week's practices. He was more decisive in his decision-making, took more chances downfield and was often successful whenever he did stretch the field. He also made some tight throws in traffic that included several impressive completions for scores during red zone drills.
Howard, who has a long history of being entrenched in position battles, is clearly game for the competition. On Monday, two plays after Allar completed a deep pass downfield, Howard decided to go deep himself. The pass wasn't completed, but Howard's decision to test himself in that situation was more notable than the result.
Drew Allar and Will Howard during a recent practice. #Steelers pic.twitter.com/Z0ADAqyz5v
As far as intangibles are concerned, Howard has the leg up in that department. He was the last player off the field on both Monday and Tuesday. In 2024, his leadership helped Ohio State overcome a devastating loss to archrival Michigan to go on an improbable national title run. And speaking of Ohio State, Howard shared the many similarities between Ryan Day and McCarthy following Monday's practice.
Will Howard on similarities between Ryan Day & Mike McCarthy. pic.twitter.com/MaHYpSVpg0
Allar may have the edge now, but the ultimate test will come in the preseason. Furthermore, in addition to competing against each other, Allar and Howard are also competing against Mason Rudolph , the team's veteran backup. McCarthy hasn't ruled out having four quarterbacks on his roster, but it's safe to assume that he is hoping that two of his three backup quarterbacks play well enough during the preseason to convince him that he only needs three on the 53-man roster.
One can also assume that McCarthy would rather keep two young quarterbacks on the roster, which could very well lead to Rudolph being the odd man out. For that to happen, though, Allar and Howard have to take full advantage of their opportunities during the preseason.
Overreaction or reality: Reality
Despite rotating first-team reps with Jaylen Warren , it's clear that Dowdle is the front-runner to be Pittsburgh's starting running back when the regular season starts.
Dowdle, who ran for 1,000 yards during his final season with McCarthy in Dallas, has quickly developed a rapport with Rodgers as a safety valve in the passing game. He is embracing the opportunity to play with and catch passes from Pittsburgh's future Hall of Fame quarterback.
"The best quarterback I've stepped on a field with," Dowdle told CBS Sports following Tuesday's practice. "Smartest quarterback. It's just been get getting out there, getting beside him and working with him. Definitely looking forward to getting out there during the regular season with him."
“That’s the best quarterback I’ve stepped on a field with.” Rico Dowdle on Aaron Rodgers pic.twitter.com/qoKH41HKls
As impressive as Dowdle has been, the Steelers are going to need him and Warren in order to be successful this season. Warren, despite setting career highs last season with 958 rushing yards, 1,291 all-purpose yards and eight total touchdowns, continues to carry a chip on his shoulder after not being selected in the 2022 NFL Draft .
"I don't think that will ever go away," said Warren, who made the Steelers' initial 53-man roster in 2022 after going undrafted. "Whether it's Year 5 or Year 11, I'll still carry that."
Warren's individual goal for 2026 is to rush for over 1,000 yards for the first time. He was asked whether or not he and Dowdle can become the eighth pair of teammates to both rush for 1,000 yards in the same season.
"Oh yeah, for sure," he said. "Our O-line, they've definitely built that chemistry. Everybody's on the same page, and I'm excited for the season to start."
#Steelers Jaylen Warren’s individual goal is to run for 1K for the first time, and he thinks that Rico Dowdle can do so as well. Steelers have had one pair of teammates to each hit 1K in the same season: Franco & Rocky back in 1976. pic.twitter.com/4uoDsvAJXg
While the Steelers' running game appears to be primed for success, that wasn't the case during this week's first two practices as Pittsburgh's backs seldom reached the third level of the defense. That is something to keep an eye on when the Steelers kick off the preseason.
Overreaction or reality: Reality
After an impressive opening week of camp, Wilson was just as impressive during this week's first two practices.
Wilson has received the majority of the reps with Pittsburgh's first-team offense, and he's taken full advance of those reps. Throughout both practices, Wilson was consistently targeted by Rodgers, who is clearly developing trust in Pittsburgh's former third-round pick.
It's easy to see how Wilson has found a way to move up the depth chart. He's spent time with the jugs machine before practice and has continued to catch passes after practice.
Roman Wilson getting some work in before #Steelers first padded practice. pic.twitter.com/mTcabwlQl9
Along with Wilson, Rodgers' top targets thus far have been Dowdle, DK Metcalf , and tight end Pat Freiermuth . Michael Pittman , one of the Steelers' big offseason acquisitions, was noticeably quiet during both practices. So was rookie Germie Bernard , who is clearly still getting acclimated to life in the NFL .
Overreaction or reality: Overreaction
Defensively, the Steelers don't appear to be negatively impacted by the fact that they no longer have a defensive-oriented head coach. In fact, it appears to be the opposite.
Led by new defensive coordinator Patrick Graham, the Steelers' defense made a bevy of notable plays during the first two days of padded practice. That was the case even with the absence of defensive backs Joey Porter Jr . and Jalen Ramsey .
Ironically, two other defensive backs, Brandin Echols and newcomer Jaquan Brisker , have been two of Pittsburgh's biggest defensive standouts thus far. Brisker has made his presence felt both in the secondary and up on the line of scrimmage. Echols made several notable plays earlier this week that included an interception of Rodgers during the early portion of Monday's practice.
Echols' playmaking was complemented by his constant chirping at the offense, a subtle reminder that the Steelers, at their core, are still about being physical and intimidating.
"I've been like that since high school," Echols said. "It's crazy. I used to watch a lot of Jalen Ramsey [going back to] his rookie year when he was with Jacksonville. All the trash talking it, seeing everything he was doing, it just like motivated me. I was like, 'When I get to the NFL, I want to be just like that.'"
Ironically, Echols said one of his favorite receivers in the NFL to exchange banter with is one of his teammates.
"DK," Echols said. "DK brings it out of me. Me and DK are kind of from the same area. He's from Mississippi. I'm from Mississippi. We've got that relationship. We're just trying to make each other better."
As far as the 2026 season is concerned, Echols said that the Steelers' defense is motivated to prove their naysayers wrong.
"We're gonna come out with a chip, especially coming off last year," he said. "You know, just looking at some of the rankings, how they had us placed, we know some…
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Hall of Fame Game kicks off NFL preseason; Jonathan Taylor agrees to $44M deal with Colts
summary: Plus, the 10 most fascinating transfers in college football
full_text:
This is an article version of the CBS Sports HQ AM Newsletter, the ultimate guide to every day in sports. You can sign up to get it in your inbox every weekday morning here .
Earlier this week, our panel of experts ranked the top 10 coaches in the NFL . They're keeping that train rolling today by ranking the top 10 play-callers on offense and defense .
These days, it's incredibly common for offensive head coaches to call plays, and only one coordinator is in our top 10 of offensive play-callers. title: 2026 Hall of Fame Game: Carson Beck heads top 10 players to keep an eye on in preseason opener
summary: With the starters sitting out the Hall of Fame Game, all eyes turn to rookie quarterback Carson Beck and a host of young talent fighting for roster spots
full_text:
Football is back. The Carolina Panthers and Arizona Cardinals will kick off the preseason in the Pro Football Hall of Fame Game tonight in Canton, Ohio. Those two teams will play four preseason games while the rest of the league will play just three.
Panthers head coach Dave Canales has already made his intentions known not to play the starters. However, the term "starters" is relatively subjective at this stage of the preseason. Some starters may be in competition with others whereas others may only be in a starting role due to injury.
The Cardinals have been less direct in their intentions, but are expected to operate under similar guidelines. Rookie running back Jeremiyah Love expressed his desire to play Thursday night, but coach Mike LaFleur seemed to dismiss that idea in media availability earlier this week. For that reason, wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. , cornerback Will Johnson and defensive tackle Walter Nolen III were among the notable names left off the list.
Here are the players I am excited to watch Thursday night:
Starting safeties Nick Scott and Tre'von Moehrig have a combined 14 years of service in the NFL . The team is comfortable with that duo but second-year safety Lathan Ransom and Wheatley will push for a larger role. Wheatley is a long athlete (6-foot-3) who can muddy passing windows and get his hands on the football; as evidenced by his four interceptions over the past two seasons.
Offensive line was high on the list of offseason priorities for Arizona, but offensive guard Chase Bisontis and Williams were the only two drafted. The team did sign veterans Isaac Seumalo and Elijah Wilkinson in free agency, but Williams has starting-caliber traits that may lead to him receiving more playing time as the season progresses. The preseason gives the Cardinals an opportunity to test and establish a baseline for their rookie.
When Taylor-Demerson was drafted, the thought was that he could be the heir apparent to Budda Baker . However, Jalen Thompson is now gone from that secondary and Baker remains. The team signed Andrew Wingard in free agency despite Taylor-Demerson intercepting two passes in just 12 games. Can he continue his development and take ownership of a starting role in Arizona's young secondary?
Under the current coaching staff, a new cornerback emerges every year. Mike Jackson is coming off his best season and Jaycee Horn has become the player Carolina had expected when it selected him in the first round of the 2021 NFL Draft . Undrafted free agent Corey Thornton played 11% of the team's defensive snaps after breaking out last offseason. The team's track record of development, as well as its fourth-round investment in Lee, give reason for optimism.
Harrison-Hunte showed a lot of promise dating to his freshman season at Miami. Although he has yet to reach his full potential, Harrison-Hunte possesses great size. He may get a longer look alongside two other young defensive tackles: Cam Jackson and Lee Hunter .
Kuwatch plays the game sideline to sideline with reckless abandon. Carolina signed Devin Lloyd in free agency so the preseason may be Kuwatch's best opportunity for live-game repetitions, but do not be surprised if the Miami (Ohio) product becomes a key contributor on special teams this season.
Bisontis, a second-round pick, has cross-trained at left and right guard thus far. It sounds as though he will begin the season as a key reserve so preseason repetitions are invaluable. Bisontis is an athletic lineman who was playing his best football toward the end of his final season at Texas A&M, but remains a bit rough around the edges. Will he eventually take a starting role from either Isaiah Adams or Seumalo?
Umanmielen was a third-round pick a year ago and a recent season-ending injury to Nic Scourton places even more pressure on the Ole Miss product to elevate his game. Last season, Umanmielen recorded 1.5 sacks and a forced fumble for the Panthers. Jaelan Phillips was a big ticket free agent signing, but Umanmielen is competing with Patrick Jones II and Trevis GIpson for more playing time.
Hecht was a personal favorite during the pre-draft process. He was viewed as a top 100 overall prospect with starting capabilities but lasted until the fifth round. The Kansas State lineman is now embroiled in a competition with veteran Luke Fortner for the starting center job.
Beck will start for the Cardinals. It will be the first extended look of the third-round pick as a professional and the nation's first impression of LaFleur as a head coach. The game plan is unlikely to express more than a surface level look at the offense, but the opportunities to see Beck this season may be limited. Veteran Jacoby Brissett is the anticipated Week 1 starter and there is no timeline for the Miami product to take over.

title: Aaron Donald works out with Rams as potential NFL return gains momentum
summary: Donald used team equipment during a workout in Los Angeles, requiring the Rams to report his activity on the NFL transaction wire
full_text:
Former Los Angeles Rams superstar Aaron Donald hinted at an NFL return earlier this summer, and on Wednesday, he took a significant step toward rejoining the team. Donald worked out with the Rams in what was the closest thing to official practice participation since his retirement at the end of the 2023 season.
Donald wanted to work out in a football helmet, according to ESPN , and while he did not wear pads during his session in Los Angeles, he used team equipment at the facility during training camp. That required the Rams to report his activity on the NFL's transaction wire.
While Donald stayed in excellent shape during his retirement and regularly posted workout videos, he needs to prove his athleticism remains at an NFL-caliber level to join the Rams. It is not clear how Wednesday's workout went, nor how his body will respond. If everything checks out, though, Donald could reasonably progress to signing with the team and participating in training camp in the coming weeks.
Even if Donald were not ready for game action by Week 1, he could make meaningful contributions to the Rams at some point later in the season. In fact, that could be the preferred scenario, given how much strain a 17-game campaign would put on a body that has not played in two years.
The prospect of a comeback first emerged when the Rams traded for star edge rusher Myles Garrett , bolstering a defensive front that stands among the most formidable in the league. Pairing arguably the greatest pass rusher in NFL history with a former three-time Defensive Player of the Year and perennial first-team All-Pro in Donald would add even more firepower to the most loaded roster in pro football .
Donald said in June that the Garrett trade "for sure got me thinking" and that at 35, he wants to see if "that fire can light back up."
When he retired after the 2023 season, Donald went out on his own terms. He still clearly had plenty left to give, considering he closed his career with another first-team All-Pro season in which he amassed eight sacks and 16 tackles for loss. If he comes out of retirement, it would be a steep ask to expect anything close to his peak production, but as one of the greatest defensive players in league history, he could still make a genuine difference-making impact.

title: Falcons Secondary Loaded with Talent, According to Top 99 Defensive Player Rankings
summary: With the unfortunate injury to Jalon Walker, other pieces of the defense will have to step up to alleviate the loss of his versatility and athleticism. According to Bleacher Report’s Top 99 defensive players ranking, the Atlanta Falcons secondary is loaded with talent to handle the loss of Walker and possibly James Pearce Jr., and […]
full_text: FLOWERY BRANCH, GEORGIA - MAY 27: Jessie Bates III #3 of the Atlanta Falcons runs through drills during OTA's at IBM Performance Field on May 27, 2026 in Flowery Branch, Georgia. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images With the unfortunate injury to Jalon Walker , other pieces of the defense will have to step up to alleviate the loss of his versatility and athleticism. According to Bleacher Report’s Top 99 defensive players ranking , the Atlanta Falcons secondary is loaded with talent to handle the loss of Walker and possibly James Pearce Jr., and his pending suspension. How do the Rankings Work? Bleacher Report graded what looks to be every player in the NFL on a grade of 0-100. After grading, they split them into categories based on their final grade. For the Top 99 ranking, the categories are as follows: The Standard (97-100) Franchise Cornerstones (94-96) All-Pro Ability (90-93) Pro-Bowl Caliber (85-89) High-Quality Starter (80-84) Critical Roster Piece (75-79) Falcons Secondary is Loaded It’s just as Allen Strk wrote this morning . The Falcons have three of the top 60 players, including one of only 10 players who earned a 90+ grade. #58, S Xavier Watts, Grade: 81 Xavier Watts deserved a stronger push for Defensive Rookie of the Year in 2025. He makes up half of the best safety duo in the league with Jessie Bates, allowed Bates to roam closer to the line of scrimmage, and helped unlock the defense and create turnovers. Watts had five interceptions and 11 passes broken up as a rookie, was a plus run defender from depth, and, while there were some lapses, he showed the ability to recover not just physically but also mentally. He didn’t look like a rookie out there; he handled more rotations, living on top of the defense, and the NFL stage like he was meant to be there. Xavier Watts falling to pick 96 was unreal. Rookie who plays with the demeanor of a veteran safety. The #Falcons got an absolute STEAL pic.twitter.com/vLYYdaf0vE — NFL Draft Files (@NFL_DF) September 17, 2025 When the Falcons were able to bring in both Xavier Watts and Billy Bowman, who I believe would have flirted with making this list if not for his injury, in last year’s draft, it felt like a dream come true. Watts’ range and ability to diagnose plays allowed Bates to immediately make an impact closer to the line of scrimmage, a much better role for him as he continues to age gracefully. As for Watts, we have to remember that he is still going into his sophomore season. This was his first action under the NFL microscope, and he knocked it out of the park. Now, it’s time to build on it for even more fireworks in the second act. Watts was listed as the 16th safety, going just behind names like Camryn Bynum, Jaylinn Hawkins, Amani Hooker and Grant Delpit. #56, CB A.J. Terrell, Grade: 81 One of the more underrated corners in the NFL, AJ Terrell is a technician on the outside who forced tight-window throws at the fourth-highest rate in the league last season. He mirrors well, attacks the catch point consistently, and is a willing and able run supporter. Bigger route-runners with a good catch radius take advantage of the space he gives them in off coverage, but he closes and uses leverage well. He doesn’t create a ton of turnovers, but still gets his hands on the football a lot. #Falcons AJ Terrell (top of the screen). Zone vision in the outside 1/3. See the QB/react to the wheel route. pic.twitter.com/zAf7DiA2T3 — Matt Bowen (@MattBowen41) October 28, 2024 A technician through and through, A.J. Terrell continues to give Atlanta’s outside much-needed stability as they revamp the defense. On the other side, we’re still not entirely sure whether it will be his brother Avieon or if they’ll continue to roll with Mike Hughes, as Avieon either stays inside as a nickel or becomes a depth piece. Whichever way it goes, you can count on one thing: A.J. will show up and be a force. Terrell was ranked as the 11th-best outside cornerback, just behind names like Kamari Lassiter, Jaycee Horn, Sauce Gardner, and Trent McDuffie. #8, S Jessie Bates, Grade: 91 Jesse Bates sees things before they happen and shows up exactly where he needs to be to make the play. It’s like watching Mysterio fighting Spider-Man, always appearing in places the quarterback doesn’t want him to be and taking the ball away. Bates is one of the prominent ball-hawks in today’s game, and he seamlessly rotates all around the back end, handling a ton of mental responsibilities. He played closer to the line of scrimmage last season than ever before and played fast, took away underneath routes, and helped condense the offense. A continually impressive player continues an impressive career. Jessie Bates picks off Daniel Jones before the half! ATLvsIND on @NFLNetwork Also streaming on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/MRMc6htH15 — NFL (@NFL) November 9, 2025 What else is there to say about the impact that Jessie Bates has had on this Falcons defense since he first donned the uniform in 2023? Bates has been everything he was promised to be and more as the Falcons continue to find their identity on that side of the ball. Bates is listed as the third-best safety in football behind only Kyle Hamilton and Xavier McKinney. Despite some of the questions up front, there’s no question that the trio of Bates, Watts and Terrell gives this defense a floor that most Falcons defenses did not.

title: The Falcons’ secondary has all the pieces to be a special unit
summary: Building a well-rounded secondary without any weaknesses is one of the most difficult challenges in roster construction. It takes sharp drafting, shrewd signings, and emphasis on assembling capable depth. No matter how star-studded the unit may look on paper, there must be backups on the roster who are ready to step in when necessary. That […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - DECEMBER 29: Xavier Watts #31 of the Atlanta Falcons celebrates an interception with Jessie Bates III #3 during the second quarter at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on December 29, 2025 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images Building a well-rounded secondary without any weaknesses is one of the most difficult challenges in roster construction. It takes sharp drafting, shrewd signings, and emphasis on assembling capable depth. No matter how star-studded the unit may look on paper, there must be backups on the roster who are ready to step in when necessary. That was one of the key components behind the success of the last well-rounded Falcons’ secondary. As was the case for most of Atlanta’s most recent successes, 2017 was the last time they had an ultra-talented group of defensive backs. Keanu Neal, Ricardo Allen, Robert Alford, and Brian Poole were all at their peaks. Desmond Trufant returned to playing at a high level after suffering a season-ending pectoral injury in 2016. Damontae Kazee, Blidi Wreh-Wilson, and C.J. Goodwin were all quality contributors when called upon. It was a solidified group that led to Dan Quinn having his best defense in Atlanta. Despite Jessie Bates’ stellar play and A.J. Terrell firmly established as one of the league’s better corners, the secondary has been lacking in certain areas over most of the past decade. A player like Richie Grant or Jeff Okudah would be too much of a liability for the overall unit to ascend. All it takes is one player for opponents to target and exploit to tear a unit apart. The Falcons’ secondary currently looks well-equipped to be a formidable unit with no glaring concerns. In fact, they possess the Pro Bowl-caliber talent and young ballhawks to far surpass the strong group from 2017. As the team prepares for the season, there should be increased anticipation for a defense that finished tied for sixth in interceptions in 2025. Franchise cornerstones with an emerging star Bates and Terrell alone immediately provide a strong infrastructure with their consistency and leadership. Although the three-time second-team All-Pro got off to a slow start last season, Bates played like the premier safety in the second half of the year. His high football intelligence, tremendous instincts, and coverage range generate big plays while preventing opposing explosive plays over the course of games. Terrell is coming off arguably his best year since his breakout 2021 season, playing strong press coverage and staying composed when battling bigger receivers not named Mike Evans. What sets the secondary apart as a unit with the potential to become elite begins with Xavier Watts. The 2025 third-round pick emerged as a genuine difference-maker with his playmaking ability, reliable open-field tackling, and consistency in taking the right angles when closing on the ball. The overall command he plays with was reminiscent of a four-year player entering his prime. From his fantastic debut against the Buccaneers to his memorable performance in an upset win over the Rams, Watts consistently put himself in position to make plays all over the field. Divine Deablo believes Bates and Watts are the best safety duo in the league. That could be the case if the former All-American from Notre Dame continues on this trajectory. As talented as the secondary was in 2017, they severely fell short in one crucial area. They only produced eight interceptions that season. Although Neal slightly made up for it with three forced fumbles with his punishing style of play, the inability to force turnovers cost the defense in close games where Steve Sarkisian’s offense sputtered. Bates and Watts combined for eight interceptions last season alone. To make things even more tantalizing, they aren’t the only ballhawks on a defense that overwhelmed the Bills and Rams in primetime victories. New corners How Avieon Terrell and Billy Bowman develop will ultimately decide if the secondary can be the all-around special unit it has the potential to be. Besides it being an incredibly heartwarming moment, the decision to select Terrell in the second round was a wise move. Mike Hughes may begin the season as a starter, but there are clear limitations in his skill set as an outside corner. Terrell possesses the physical intangibles and zone coverage acumen to thrive at the pro level immediately. He was around the ball a lot at Clemson. The first-team All-ACC cornerback produced 25 pass breakups and eight forced fumbles during his three years there. While his older brother A.J. rarely forces turnovers, Avieon can bring a new dimension to a secondary with players who know how to get the ball. The same can be said for Billy Bomwan Jr., who showed impressive flashes before suffering a season-ending Achilles injury. The versatile defensive back was one of the standout players in the Falcons’ impressive road win over the Vikings. His knack for recognizing play designs and closing in on the ball in a flash makes him someone who can grow into being a disruptive, dynamic player. While his overall coverage skills in the slot remain a work in progress, Bowman Jr. possesses the capabilities to become a starter with his ultra-aggressive, tone-setting style of play. To have that type of player in the nickel is something the Falcons have lacked since Poole played there. It’s yet to be determined whether Bowman Jr. will be ready to start the season, but The Falcoholic’s own Kevin Knight reported he has been working on the rehab field. Every well-rounded secondary needs a young nucleus of players who could develop into either Pro Bowl-caliber players or dependable starters. Before injuries derailed his career, Neal had all the makings of being a top-tier safety. Allen and Poole became dependable starters for three seasons. Watts, Bowman Jr., and Avieon Terrell have the talent to lead the defense with their unique attributes, alongside Bates and A.J. Terrell. Greater Pressure Following Jalon Walker’s season-ending injury, the secondary will have an even greater onus on them to anchor the defense. Jeff Ulbrich will have his work cut out for him up front, particularly in the first half of the season with James Pearce Jr. likely to serve a lengthy suspension. That will put the secondary at the forefront not only of staying organized on the back end but also of being ready to shoot into gaps and be disruptive. Bates, Watts, and Bowman Jr. were all utilized as blitzers when Ulbrich decided to bring extra pressure. The beloved defensive coordinator’s knack for overloading the strong side led to several sacks on third down last season. While each defensive back will need to raise their cover skills to overcome the devastating loss of Walker, they must be ready to explode to force opposing quarterbacks into uncomfortable decisions. As deflating as it is to lose Walker for the season, expectations should be high for a secondary featuring established stars and emerging prolific talent. They are the best hope to keep a defense faced with major uncertainty up front stabilized. They are the best-equipped group on the roster to turn into a premier unit that opposing offenses will be wary of. Many teams will have to cope with glaring issues during the season. The Falcons’ secondary has all the capabilities to make weekly game-changing plays and drive the team to exceed expectations this season.
author: Allen Strk

title: Ranking every position group on the Ravens’ 2026 roster
summary: The Baltimore Ravens filled out their roster this offseason with a number of notable additions in the draft and free agency. Now, with the 2026 season fast approaching next month, position groups will be finalized across training camp and preseason action over the next few weeks. Which of the team’s position groups are the strongest? […]
full_text: OWINGS MILLS, MARYLAND - JULY 29: Quarterbacks Lamar Jackson #8 and Tyler Huntley #5 of the Baltimore Ravens participate in a drill on the first day of training camp at Under Armour Performance Center Baltimore Ravens on July 29, 2026 in Owings Mills, Maryland. (Photo by Jamie Sabau/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens filled out their roster this offseason with a number of notable additions in the draft and free agency. Now, with the 2026 season fast approaching next month, position groups will be finalized across training camp and preseason action over the next few weeks. Which of the team’s position groups are the strongest? Let’s rank them below in terms of best on the roster, from best to worst. 1. Safety When combining star power and depth, the Ravens have one of, if not the best safety room of any team in the league. Kyle Hamilton is established as a premier talent, while Malaki Starks proved to be a solid pro as a rookie and has the potential for a sophomore leap. Jaylinn Hawkins, who the team signed this offseason, is coming off a strong season as a defensive leader for the AFC Champion New England Patriots. Hawkins gives the Ravens a trio of above-average safeties and lots of flexibility in the secondary. 2. Quarterback Lamar Jackson remains an elite quarterback with a great chance to return to his MVP-caliber ways after an injury-riddled 2025 campaign. Jackson could thrive in Declan Doyle’s new-look offensive system with some new playmakers around him. Tyler Huntley is the ideal backup for Jackson with a proven track record of winning games as a spot-starter. Huntley quickly proved last year that he was a better No. 2 option than Cooper Rush. 3. Running Back Derrick Henry continues to defeat father time and church out elite seasons. Henry should be super productive again as the workhorse in the Ravens’ backfield. Justice Hill remains a solid backup and third down running back but could be pushed by either Rasheen Ali or Adam Randall for playing time. Randall, a fifth-round pick this year, is a sleeper to emerge as a contributor given his versatility and pass-catching prowess. The Clemson product could beat usurp Ali for the No. 3 role to begin the season and have a role on special teams. 4. Cornerback The Ravens’ cornerback room underwhelmed in 2025 given the on-paper talent. The prospects for positive regression in 2026, though, are good. Marlon Humphrey’s ability to rebound from a subpar season will be a major X-factor. Nate Wiggins didn’t make a huge Year 2 jump like many anticipated last season, but is still a proven talented coverage corner and possesses high-level upside. Chidobe Awuzie is a solid veteran and reliable starter. The Ravens have several young cornerbacks competing for the last two spots on the depth chart. 5. Defensive Line The return of Nnamdi Madbuike is a major lift for the Ravens’ defensive line. If he can perform anywhere close to his previous All-Pro level, the Ravens have a more than formidable front seven. The addition of veteran Calais Campbell, even at age 40, is also a significant boost. Travis Jones ascended to another level in 2025 with a career-best season and is an anchoring force in the middle. The Ravens have a crowded group of veterans and young players fighting for the last roster spots in this group and will have solid depth no matter how the pecking order shakes out. 6. Edge Rusher The Ravens got subpar production from their edge rushers last year but made two significant additions this spring in Trey Hendrickson and Zion Young. Hendrickson is well-established as one of the league’s premier pass rushers dating back several years. Although he’s coming off a season-ending injury is now 31 years old, Hendrickson figures to have a big impact. Young also projects as an instant contributor, especially as an edge-setter and run defender, in his rookie season. If Mike Green takes a step forward in his sophomore season like many anticipate, edge rusher could quickly become a real strength for the Ravens. Tavius Robinson is a serviceable rotational player who has proven he can handle starter reps. 7. Inside Linebacker Roquan Smith’s reputation as one of the best off-ball linebackers in the NFL precedes him. However, although he was named to a third straight Pro Bowl in 2025, his play left some to be desired. Smith’s tackles dropped and his playmaking was missing at times; he had no interceptions, sacks or forced fumbles. He’s in good position to perform well as the center of Jesse Minter’s defense this season. Next to Smith, Teddye Buchanan and Trenton Simpson are both viable starting options. Buchanan was emerging as a solid starter in his rookie season before suffering a torn ACL last October. Simpson, meanwhile, has yet to prove himself as a consistent and reliable defensive option, but his potential is still high given his raw athletic abilities. 8. Offensive Line The Ravens are more solidified at offensive tackle than on the interior. Ronnie Stanley remains a quality starter on the left side, as does Roger Rosengarten on the right. The latter has the potential to become an upper-echelon player this year in his third season. Incoming first-round pick Olaivavega Ioane projects as an instant plug-and-play starter at right guard and may quickly prove to be a high-level starter in Year 1. Veteran John Simpson will likely be an upgrade at left guard, even though he’s far from an elite player. The biggest question mark is who will win the starting center job between Ethan Pocic, Danny Pinter and company, and how they will perform throughout the season. 9. Tight End After losing both Isaiah Likely and Charlie Kolar, plus Pat Ricard also, the Ravens took a hit in terms of tight end strength. For the first time in many years, they’re facing a lot of questions with this position group. Can Mark Andrews bounce back after a big dip in production last season? Andrews has shown some signs of athletic decline amidst injuries in recent years. What impact can incoming rookies, both mid-round picks, Matthew Hibner and Josh Cuevas provide right away? 10. Specialists The Ravens have almost had a reliable trio of specialists but that will be put to the test in 2026. Tyler Loop has a lot to prove as the team’s kicker in his second season. Loop was solid overall last season but struggled from beyond 50 yards and had a poor end to the year. Incoming rookie punter Ryan Eckley has big shoes to fill after Jordan Stout departed in free agency. Nick Moore, meanwhile, is established as a solid long snapper.
author: Frank Platko

title: Ravens ramp up physicality at hot, chippy day of training camp
summary: The Baltimore Ravens held a hot practice on Thursday, in every sense of the word. Wednesday’s showers dialed up the humidity at The Castle, and the team’s third padded practice in four days dialed up the intensity. Motors were running hot, as were several players’ tempers. Tight end Mark Andrews and edge rusher Trey Hendrickson […]
full_text: OWINGS MILLS, MARYLAND - JULY 29: Head Coach Jesse Minter of the Baltimore Ravens leads the first day of training camp at Under Armour Performance Center Baltimore Ravens on July 29, 2026 in Owings Mills, Maryland. (Photo by Jamie Sabau/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens held a hot practice on Thursday, in every sense of the word. Wednesday’s showers dialed up the humidity at The Castle, and the team’s third padded practice in four days dialed up the intensity. Motors were running hot, as were several players’ tempers. Tight end Mark Andrews and edge rusher Trey Hendrickson butted heads after one physical blocking encounter, and center Ethan Pocic and linebacker Reid Williford jawed at each other in an unexpected veteran/rookie encounter. Quarterback Lamar Jackson spiked his helmet in frustration after one rough sequence for the offense. And most notably, edge rusher Tavius Robinson and offensive linemen Carson Vinson and John Simpson got in a post-play scrap that was quickly snuffed out by the rest of the team. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said on Tuesday that he does not like to see fights at practice. None of today’s scuffles rose to that level, due in part to Minter’s careful management of his players. He brought the team in for an extended huddle after the Robinson-Vinson-Simpson fracas to ensure the tension did not persist. But after practice, Minter said that he loved the competitive spirit and physicality of the period. In fact, it seemed to be by design. “We wanted it to be a really physical day,” Minter explained. “We wanted it to be a long practice. We wanted them to kind of fight through some things — long drive drills, where it is intentionally an eight- or nine-play drive, regardless of the down and distance. You want to be able to do all that with a high, high level of physicality and also keep your wits about you.” Indeed, Thursday was the Ravens’ longest practice of training camp, extending past the two-hour mark for the first time this summer. Left tackle Ronnie Stanley and defensive tackle C.J. Okoye both left the field early – no major concern for players that tip the scales at well over 300 pounds, but still a reflection of the day’s intensity. Minter even allowed live tackling to end practice with rookie running back Adam Randall getting all three of the offense’s touches in that period. The 6-foot-4, 232-pounder was brought down twice – once by a physical tackle from cornerback Marquise Robinson – and closed it out with a touchdown catch from Skyler Thompson. Even the coaching staff got in on the action. The Ravens’ defensive backs took turns tackling various assistant coaches, who will probably be feeling it tomorrow morning despite multiple layers of protection. The Ravens' defensive backs took turns tackling assistant coaches onto a padded mat. "Coaches will do anything to help the players get better," Jesse Minter said. I really enjoyed watching this, I’m sure you will, too: pic.twitter.com/CyUKuNbVDS — Nikhil Mehta (@nikknowsball) August 6, 2026 “Coaches will do anything to make players better,” Minter said after practice. “We have a great group of coaches. All those guys are willing to do whatever it takes…Much appreciate to those guys for doing that.”
author: Nikhil Mehta

title: The Ravens’ defensive line could make – or break – their 2026 season
summary: In 2025, everything went wrong for the Baltimore Ravens. Their star QB couldn’t stay healthy due to a porous offensive line. They struggled to execute in high-leverage situations and continued a frustrating pattern of blowing late leads. Their disorganized secondary continuously let opposing offenses pick them apart. The list goes on and on, but at […]
full_text: In 2025, everything went wrong for the Baltimore Ravens. Their star QB couldn’t stay healthy due to a porous offensive line. They struggled to execute in high-leverage situations and continued a frustrating pattern of blowing late leads. Their disorganized secondary continuously let opposing offenses pick them apart. The list goes on and on, but at the top of it was the Ravens’ lack of any meaningful pass rush. In prior years, Baltimore was able to generate high sack numbers. Unfortunately, this led to the front-office viewing their defensive line talent through rose-colored lenses, glossing over the broader issue which was that, since the days of Suggs, Ngata, and Dumervil, the Ravens have not consistently pressure opposing passers with four rushers. Even in 2023, when they led the league in almost every major defensive metric, they still ranked in the bottom third of the league in QB pressure rate. Mike Macdonald and other defensive coordinators before him were able to combine creative blitzes with disguised coverages to confuse quarterbacks and make them hold onto the football until the pass rush got home. But when a less-capable defensive coordinator took over, disaster followed. Last year, the house came crashing down in a bad way. After star DT Nnamdi Madubuike was put on injured reserve with a season-ending neck injury in Week 2, the Ravens’ pass rush went from a below average unit to arguably the worst in the NFL. They ranked at or towards the bottom of the league in pressure rate, pass rush win rate, and sacks. Fans watched as opposing quarterbacks sat back in the pocket unfazed as they slowly picked the defense apart. Even if Tyler Loop’s fateful kick made it through the uprights in Pittsburgh, this was not a team that could make a deep playoff run. Fast-forward to this year’s training camp, and the defensive line is in a vastly improved place. After abandoning a trade for Maxx Crosby, the Ravens signed EDGE Trey Hendrickson who is just one year removed from an All-Pro year in which he led the league in sacks. Madubuike also passed his physical and is working his way towards a return to the field. And if Hendrickson and Madubuike are not enough, the Ravens also reunited with DT Calais Campbell and drafted EDGE Zion Young out of Missouri. These moves, along with projected leaps from players like Mike Green and Tavius Robinson, have the Ravens set to catapult from one of the worst defensive lines in the league to one of the best. They have the personnel to generate pressure from the edge and the interior with plenty of depth and versatility to utilize several different looks and schemes along their front. As mentioned, the Ravens have been able to generate big sack numbers in prior years. But when push came to shove against good offensive lines and quarterbacks, mainly in the playoffs, it was clear that the scheme wasn’t enough. They needed more talent. The ability to protect your own quarterback and get pressure on the opposing one is arguably the most telling indicator of success for a team. Last year’s Denver Broncos are a prime example of a team that lacked high-end weapons but were able to reach the AFC Championship because of how well they protected Bo Nix and pressure opposing QBs (second in pressure rate, first in sack rate). It’s a winning formula that has been tested for years and with the Ravens offseason additions, it looks like they are ready to play the game. While on paper, the pass rush looks great, only time will tell if they can become a top-ranked unit in the league. Unfortunately, there are question marks. Hendrickson is on the wrong side of 30, Madubuike is coming back from a career threatening injury, and players like Young and Green are still relatively unproven. ( Editor’s note: pun not intended .) If these players all play to their potential, there’s no reason why this defensive line can’t be one of the best in the league. In that scenario, it’s difficult to imagine the Ravens not having a top defense to pair with an offense that, when healthy, always figures to be near the top of the league with Lamar Jackson, Derrick Henry, and Zay Flowers. In the down-scenario, Hendrickson shows signs of his age, Madubuike cannot come back at the same level, and the young talent doesn’t develop up to their potential. While the former seems to be likely outcome, nothing is guaranteed. As 2025 shows, games aren’t won on paper. But with new head coach Jesse Minter, defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver, and the infusion of pass-rush talent, the Ravens defense is primed for a return to glory. title: C.J. Gardner-Johnson’s surprising return to training camp practice huge for Bills defensive versatility
summary: After C.J. Gardner-Johnson suffered a calf strain last week at Buffalo Bills training camp, everyone thought he’d be sidelined for weeks. That proved not to be the case, as the chippy, high-energy veteran safety returned to the practice field at St. John Fisher University on Thursday for the team’s sixth training camp practice, surprising the […]
full_text: ROCHESTER, NEW YORK - JULY 29: C.J. Gardner-Johnson #22 of the Buffalo Bills gets his fingers taped up during training camp at St. John Fisher University on July 29, 2026 in Rochester, New York. (Photo by Joe Hrycych/Getty Images) | Getty Images After C.J. Gardner-Johnson suffered a calf strain last week at Buffalo Bills training camp, everyone thought he’d be sidelined for weeks. That proved not to be the case, as the chippy, high-energy veteran safety returned to the practice field at St. John Fisher University on Thursday for the team’s sixth training camp practice, surprising the masses as a full participant. Many of Gardner-Johnson’s teammates raved about the play, attitude, and charisma he’s demonstrated in the first week of training camp. Dion Dawkins even detailed his rapidly formed bond with the safety on and off the field, referencing Gardner-Johnson as the teammate he didn’t know he needed. Though Gardner-Johnson is only playing on a one-year prove it deal worth a maximum of $6 million, on the field he can provide much-needed stability at the other safety position opposite Cole Bishop. That stability has frankly been nonexistent after the golden years of Micah Hyde and Jordan Poyer at safety for the Bills. While Buffalo marks his sixth stop in the NFL after being selected by the Saints in the fourth round of the 2019 NFL Draft, Gardner-Johnson has proven to be a game-changing defensive back in all facets of playing the position. He’s had a pair of six-interception seasons — in 2022 and 2024 with the Eagles — and has six years with seven or more pass breakups as a professional. Known for his pesky on-field attitude and penchant for trash talking, Gardner-Johnson also brings an “edge” Bills GM Brandon Beane has repeatedly mentioned as something he and his staff prioritized in many acquisitions this offseason. When C.J. Gardner-Johnson flexed on Tom Brady 💀 #OnePride pic.twitter.com/3E3FvGP3PX — Woodward Sports Network (@woodwardsports) August 30, 2023 In college at Florida, Gardner-Johnson played plenty of nickel corner along with his regular duties safety. Last year in Chicago, he played more nickel than any other spot on the field. In 2024, when Garnder-Johnson won the Super Bowl with the Eagles, he played 805 of his 1,170 snaps at free safety — this 28 year old epitomizes versatility in the secondary. From many fearing he’d be lost for the season at the outset of his injury during the first week of training camp to back on the field less than a week later is enormously encouraging for the Bills as he’s learning a new system as part of a new team. And because Gardner-Johnson is precisely the type of player Buffalo has needed on defense the past few seasons.

title: Should Buffalo Bills fans be worried about kicker Tyler Bass?
summary: The Buffalo Bills were without the services of kicker Tyler Bass for the entire 2025 season as Bass dealt with a painful pelvic injury, but the expectation was that Bass would be healthy and ready to go as the Bills got ready for training camp at St. John Fisher University. It has been nearly a […]
full_text: The Buffalo Bills were without the services of kicker Tyler Bass for the entire 2025 season as Bass dealt with a painful pelvic injury, but the expectation was that Bass would be healthy and ready to go as the Bills got ready for training camp at St. John Fisher University. It has been nearly a year since Bass kicked a football for the Bills—during the 2025 preseason finale against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers—but so far, through the first five practice sessions at camp, Bass has yet to publicly attempt a field goal. Nearly eight months after Bass had surgery to repair a sports hernia, the kicker has not suffered any setbacks as he works his way back onto the field, according to special teams coordinator Jeff Rodgers. That thought was echoed by Bass, who said his body is “feeling good, we’re excited to get back and the process has been really kind of recovering, strengthening.” During a Q&A with the media on Tuesday, Rodgers said that, despite a lack of kicks during the team’s sessions that have been open to the media and fans, Bass has been working on his kicking in situations outside of team practices. The reason why fans haven’t been able to watch Bass attempt field goals and extra points so far at camp? The team hasn’t reached the step in their training camp schedule where they want to work extensively on field goals in game scenarios. “It has been by design,” Rodgers told WGR 550’s Paul Hamilton . “It’s not ‘Don’t let him kick just yet,’ there’s a finite number of things that we can get done on the field and field goal protection is not going to be as competitive in practice as it is in a game, so we take advantage of the walk through time because of the tempo that it requires, but at some point guys have got to start working on that stuff.” Rodgers revealed that, starting with today’s practice, fans curious about how Bass’ recovery can watch him handle field goals and extra point scenarios at camp. Rodgers told reporters that during Thursday’s practice sessions, the Bills will work on field-goal protection scenarios as a team for the third time since gathering at Fisher, and for the first time in pads to replicate game scenarios. Through the first five practices, Buffalo’s special teams units have prioritized working on their kickoffs and punts, while work on field-goal protection has been addressed during walkthrough sessions. “We just go step-by-step with it and try to put him environments that he’s going to be in, we build from there. We’ve done some individual and team stuff, but it hasn’t worked out for us to be on the field quite yet, but that will happen later on this week and then again at the stadium,” Rodgers said. “I don’t think you skip steps, it starts from ground zero and he’s working with two new holders right now (Mitch Wishnowsky and Tommy Doman) and that’s a part of that comfort, so it’s going to be a rep thing, but he looks like he did on tape and everything is going well so far.” The last time Bass kicked in a game was on Aug. 23, 2025, when he converted on three of his four field goal attempts and made both extra points in Buffalo’s preseason finale vs. Tampa Bay. Though Bass attempted to play through the pain he experienced last preseason, he was never able to shake off the discomfort and was eventually placed on injured reserve before the season began. Prior to his injury-plagued 2025 campaign, Bass had appeared in all 83 games since being selected with the No. 188 overall selection in the sixth round of the 2020 NFL Draft. Rodgers said Bass is looking forward to his first opportunity to kick in Buffalo’s new Highmark Stadium, which will occur Saturday night during the team’s annual “Return of the Blue & Red” practice starting at 7 p.m. Bills fans are hoping Bass is able to make a full recovery and return to being an effective offensive weapon. Through his first five seasons, Bass made 131 of his 155 field goals during the regular season (84.5%) and converted 264 of his 274 extra point attempts (96.4%).
