title: Buffalo Bills 2026 scouting reports: C/OG Austin Corbett
summary: The Buffalo Bills lost left guard David Edwards in free agency this offseason, as the veteran signed a lucrative contract with the New Orleans Saints. Edwards was a stabilizing force for a very good Buffalo offensive line, serving almost as the command center in pass protection and blitz pickup. Especially in hostile road environments, you […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NC - AUGUST 26: Carolina Panthers guard Austin Corbett (63) during a NFL preseason football game between the Buffalo Bills and the Carolina Panthers on August 26, 2022 at Bank of America Stadium in Charlotte, N.C. (Photo by John Byrum/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Buffalo Bills lost left guard David Edwards in free agency this offseason, as the veteran signed a lucrative contract with the New Orleans Saints. Edwards was a stabilizing force for a very good Buffalo offensive line, serving almost as the command center in pass protection and blitz pickup. Especially in hostile road environments, you could always count on seeing Edwards pointing out potential threats incoming from opposing defenses. Those are pretty large shoes to fill for whomever ends up winning the starting gig at left guard for the 2026 NFL season. In today’s installment of our “91 players in 91 days” series, we discuss a well-traveled veteran looking to fill Edwards’ shoes this fall. _____________________________________________________________________________ Name: Austin Corbett Number: 63 Position: C/OG Height/Weight: 6’4”, 306 pounds Age: 30 (31 on 9/5/2026) Experience/Draft: 9; selected by the Cleveland Browns in the second round (No. 33 overall) of the 2018 NFL Draft College: Nevada Acquired: Signed with Buffalo on 3/26/2026 Financial situation (per Spotrac): Corbett signed a one-year contract worth a total of $1,487,500. Thanks to the veteran’s salary benefit, his cap hit will be slightly less than that, coming in at $1,262,500 for the season. That number is also what Buffalo will carry in a dead-cap charge if they release him prior to Week 1. As a vested veteran, his entire base salary — $1.3 million — becomes fully guaranteed if he’s on the team for that first week. 2025 Recap: Corbett spent last season with the Carolina Panthers, which is where he’d played from 2022 onward. He began the season as Carolina’s starting center, but a Week 2 MCL injury led to the Panthers placing him on Injured Reserve. When he returned for Carolina’s Week 7 victory over the New York Jets, Corbett started, but this time, he started at left guard. Corbett did not start the following week against the Bills, but after Cade Mays suffered an ankle injury early in the game, Corbett went right back into the lineup at center. He ended up playing in 13 total games for the Panthers, starting 11 games combined at center, left guard, and right guard. According to Pro Football Focus , he was flagged for just one penalty during the season. He allowed two sacks while earning a 67.8 grade overall, which was No. 29 among 81 qualified guards. Positional outlook: Corbett is one of four players listed at center/offensive guard on the current roster. Alec Anderson, Sedrick Van Pran-Granger, and Connor McGovern are the others. Lloyd Cushenberry is listed solely at center. Tylan Grable and Jude Bowry are listed at tackle/guard. Bruno Fina, Da’Metrius Weatherspoon, O’Cyrus Torrence, Ar’Maj Reed-Adams, and Nick Broeker are listed at guard. 2026 Offseason: Corbett is in the mix to replace David Edwards in the starting lineup at left guard. He has seen reps with the first team during early training camp practices, rotating with Alec Anderson in that role as the starting left guard. 2026 Season outlook: Throughout his career, Corbett has been an above-average performer at multiple positions. He was a starter at right guard for a Super Bowl team, as he held down that role for the Los Angeles Rams when they won the title during the 2021 NFL season. The Bills could do far worse than someone with Corbett’s ability and experience in the starting lineup. However, Corbett’s versatility and veteran savvy also makes him an ideal interior line reserve. Whether he wins the left guard competition or not, Austin Corbett is someone the Bills would love to keep on the roster. There were plenty of people, myself included, who assumed that the left guard gig this season would be Alec Anderson’s to lose given the time Buffalo has taken in developing him; however, this is a win-now league, and for the Bills, 2026 is a win-now season. They don’t have time to wonder whether the player they’ve developed is going to be good enough to start, and they certainly won’t give the job to Anderson merely because he’s been here longer. The NFL is a business, and the main goal in this business is winning. If Austin Corbett is better than Alec Anderson, he’ll start at left guard this season for the Bills. If he isn’t, then he’ll likely be an active reserve on game days given that he can slot into all three of the interior positions along the offensive line. Buffalo could decide that they like another young player that they have developed, Sedrick Van Pran-Granger, enough to use Corbett as trade bait, but SVPG has really only played center in his pro career despite his C/G listing. It’s too early to tell which player has the upper hand in the left guard competition, but it wouldn’t surprise me at all if Corbett were to earn the starting gig. He’s started 78 regular season games and six playoff games in his career, which is more than all of the other players vying to replace David Edwards have even played in, let alone started, combined. Corbett is talented enough to win a starting gig with the Bills this season.

title: Recap and Reaction: Haynes King leads Panthers to last second win
summary: The Carolina Panthers played the Arizona Cardinals in an all time preseason game, and Haynes King came away the hero with a rushing touchdown on the game’s final play. First Quarter The Panthers got the ball first, and as one would expect from the Hall of Fame game, not much happened. Kenny Pickett completed two […]
full_text: CANTON, OHIO - AUGUST 06: Kenny Pickett #12 of the Carolina Panthers throws a pass during the first quarter of the 2026 Pro Football Hall of Fame Game against the Arizona Cardinals at Tom Benson Hall Of Fame Stadium on August 06, 2026 in Canton, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Carolina Panthers played the Arizona Cardinals in an all time preseason game, and Haynes King came away the hero with a rushing touchdown on the game’s final play. First Quarter The Panthers got the ball first, and as one would expect from the Hall of Fame game, not much happened. Kenny Pickett completed two short passes to Ja’Tavion Sanders who, to his credit, actually looked a little tough to bring down. A sack ended the drive, and the Panthers punted it away. The Cardinals got a first down on a Carson Beck scramble, but their drive also ended in a punt after a couple of ineffective plays after that. The punt downed the Panthers inside the 2 yard line, and it seemed like that was going to doom the drive before it got started, but they were bailed out by a pass interference call on a Brycen Tremayne go ball. That was only the useful play of the drive, and Sam Martin was called back in. He matched his counterpart with his own punt downed near the goal line. The Cardinals also used a long pass to get out from the shadow of their own goal post, but theirs was via a long completion. That built some momentum, and the Panthers couldn’t stop it. Beck completed some nice passes down the field, including one that got Arizona to the one yard line as the quarter ended. Second Quarter Corey Kiner punched in the touchdown on the first play of the second quarter. The Panthers found their own groove offensively on the ensuing drive. Trevor Etienne had a couple of nice runs and John Metchie had a long catch and run. AJ Dillon had his own nice catch and run and then capped off the response with his own touchdown run. Carson Beck kept dealing. He dropped a bomb to Jalen Brooks to get deep into Carolina territory in one play. A few plays later, he connected on a fade route with Simi Fehoko to put the Cardinals up 14-7. Haynes King checked in, and he went toe to toe with his rookie counterpart. He led the Panthers down the field with a bunch of chunk completions and a nice scramble. He looked composed running through his progressions and paid it off with a touchdown pass on a crossing route to Ja’seem Reed. The Cardinals went on a long but rather uneventful drive on their next possession. Sales Wheatley punched the ball out on one play, but the Panthers couldn’t fall on it. Eventually Jared Harrison-Hunte ended the drive with a sack and forced a field goal just inside the two minute warning. King led a pretty impressive two minute drive. He completed a number of passes to the sidelines, and Jimmy Horn had a nice catch and run. King had Horn open in the end zone on one play, but he missed him. The Panthers settled for a field goal to tie the game at 17 going into the half. Third Quarter Carson Beck continued as the quarterback to start the second half and led another drive into Panthers territory. A holding penalty slowed the drive down, but they almost bounced back to keep it alive with a couple of modest completions. They went for a deep pass off a double move on fourth down, but Isaiah Simmons broke it up (with a little help from an uncalled pass interference on the corner). The Panthers literally handed the ball back two plays later with a fumble. The defense responded well to the sudden change. Another Cardinals penalty put their offense behind the sticks, and then a Nick Hampton sack effectively killed the drive and forced a field goal. King led the Panthers back down the field. He picked up a 3rd and 5 with his feet, but it was called back for a penalty. He was unfazed and picked up the 3rd and 15 with a beautiful layered pass. The quarter ended with the Panthers facing a fourth down just outside the red zone. Fourth Quarter The fourth quarter started with the Panthers facing a 4th and 2. King found Caden Prieskorn on a bootleg to easily pick up the first down and set the Panthers up inside the five. Brad Idzik called a similar play right after going the other direction, and it ended in a touchdown catch for Anthony Tyus. Kedon Slovis hit a big pass to start the next drive, but the Panthers defense did a good job bowing up after that and forcing a field goal. The Panthers did similar with a big run from Miles Davis followed by not much else, which resulted in a matching field goal to restore the four point lead about halfway through the quarter. The Cardinals strung together a few big plays to quickly move the ball deep into Panthers territory as time waned away. The two minute warning hit with the Cardinals on the doorstep of the end zone. On the first play on the other side of the stoppage, they narrowly scored on a sideline completion to Bryson Green. After a couple of missed deep shots, King connected with Casey Washington to get the two minute drill started. He moved the Panthers across midfield. The drive took a major setback when a screen pass got blown up, but King saved it with a 28 yard scramble on 3rd and 14. As a bonus, he got out of bounds to stop the clock without a timeout. A couple plays later, he found Jimmy Horn Jr. inside the five to set up a grandstand finish. Finally, with two seconds left, King broke free from the pocket, he found some open space in the middle and bolted for it, breaking through a couple of Cardinals defenders as he stretched for the game winning touchdown as time expired. Overview Haynes King stole the show. At one point on the broadcast, Cris Collinsworth said something along the lines of “not bad for a guy who wasn’t supposed to be able to throw the ball.” He went undrafted because of questions about his arms, but he certainly looked capable given the situation. He made some quality throws and was very poised throughout the game, and he used his legs when he needed to. The Panthers might have found themselves some nice quarterback depth with an undrafted free agent, which is pretty hard to do. The Panthers heavily rotated every other position on the field, so it was hard to make any real judgments on any other player. A few guys had moments, but there wasn’t anything that would definitively change anyone’s standing on the roster. We’re more likely to see stuff like that in the coming weeks. For now, we get to enjoy a Panthers win in what has to be one of if not the best Hall of Fame Game ever played. It’s certainly setting a high bar for the rest of the NFL season.

title: 2026 Season Opener Countdown: 38 Days Remaining
summary: Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener by for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NC - OCTOBER 25: Star Lotulelei #98 of the Carolina Panthers defends a pass by Sam Bradford #7 of the Philadelphia Eagles in the first half during their game at Bank of America Stadium on October 25, 2015 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Streeter Lecka/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener by for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to change that up a bit by counting down our own list of the Top 100 Panthers of all time. This does not correspond to jersey number, does not need to be somebody who wore a jersey, and will in no way be controversial. #38. Star Lotulelei The Panthers wished upon a falling Star in the first round of the 2013 NFL Draft. Star Lotulelei, considered by most pundits to be one of the best defensive prospects in the draft that year, played his college ball at Utah. He filled a major hole in the Panthers defense at that time, but most people thought he would be long gone before the Panthers picked at 14th overall, especially since that draft was notoriously thin for top tier quarterback prospects. A concerning heart condition made some teams at the top of the draft skittish, passing on Lotulelei in favor of “safer” picks. The Panthers pounced, taking Lotulelei and not looking back. In the end, his heart was never an issue. Star would go on to play the entirety of his rookie contract with the Panthers, coming in and starting immediately in the middle of the Panthers defensive line. His 42 tackles and three sacks his rookie year earned him enough votes to finish fourth in the Defensive Rookie of the Year voting. The following four years as a consistent presence up front for the Panthers defense. While defensive tackles not named Aaron Donald rarely get the flashy stats, Lotulelei was a coaching staff favorite who sacrificed his own box score to eat double teams and let other players make plays. Near the end of the 2014 season, Lotulelei suffered a broken foot, requiring surgery. He reaggravated the injury in training camp of 2015 and was never quite the same player afterwards. After his five years in Carolina, he signed with the Buffalo Bills (Panthers North) and played there for three seasons before retiring. Nose tackles rarely get the credit they deserve from fans and the media, and Star was no exception. His presence in the middle of the defensive line, especially during the Super Bowl run of 2015, allowed other players to make names (and tons of money) for themselves. Those players, like Luke Kuechly, Kawann Short, etc., would undoubtedly agree that while he wasn’t a star, Star definitely earned this spot in our countdown.

Mandatory Credit: Kamil Krzaczynski-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Earlier today, head coach Ben Johnson said, “Today will be our longest practice yet, and we will have some thumping,” and that physicality led to numerous Chicago Bears players leaving the field. We’ll pass along specific injury information if we get it, but for now, here’s who were dinged up: Left tackle Braxton Jones, defensive end Montez Sweat, cornerback Dallis Flowers, and safety Gervarrius Owens. Also, Jaylon Jones wasn’t on the field late in practice, which may or may not be injury-related. Today’s practice was “chippy” per CHGO’s Adam Jahns. “Lots of shoving. A couple skirmishes.” “The Bears’ 7-on-9 run drills were so physical that D’Marco Jackson needed a new facemask,” shared Patrick Finley of the Chicago Sun-Times. Speaking of Jackson, “D’Marco Jackson in the backfield quickly on a blitz. Would have had a sack on Caleb Williams,” per the Bear Report’s Zack Pearson. Another from Pearson regarding the first play of live 11 on 11, “Caleb Williams hits Rome Odunze over middle. He turns it up field and breaks a tackle from Cam Lewis for a touchdown of 43 yards. Offense all ran down to celebrate and was fired up.” From the Chicago Tribune’s Brad Biggs, “Cairo Santos was just 6-for-6 in FG period – distances of 56, 50, 40, 33, 56 and 47 yards.” And fyi, the long snapper rotation continues. Per The Athletic’s Kevin Fishbain, “Down 3 with 1:41 to go, Bears offense goes 65 yards ending with a Caleb Williams strike to Luther Burden for a touchdown to end practice. QB1 was 6-for-6 on the drive.” So the first play of live 11-on-11 was a TD to Rome, and the last play was a TD to Burden! CHGO’s Greg Braggs called today’s overall practice “an up and down day” from the offense. He also pointed out that the “defense made their fair share of plays” while spotlighting flashes from Austin Booker, Gervon Dexter, and Dayo Odeyingbo. Plus, he called out “Early Training Camp hero” wide receiver Kaden Davis for his 3 impressive catches. Here’s your daily reminder that we’re just talking ’bout practice . A few other nuggets from the day. Brad Biggs said that Braxton Jones appears to be “fine” but will need to be checked out to be sure, but “sounds positive.” ( link ) UPDATE: Per ESPN’s Courtney Cronin, “The initial belief is that the injury isn’t long-term in nature with the best case scenario (after the team gathers more info on the extent) being one where Jones would be considered day to day.” Kiran Amegadjie and Jedrick Wills Jr. rotated at left tackle with the starters with Jones out. Daniel Hardy mostly filled in at defensive end with Montez Sweat out, with Dayo Odeyingbo also getting some reps there, but Dayo was inside at defensive tackle a lot today. ( link ) Defensive lineman Shemar Turner (PUP list/Knee) was on a side field getting in some work. Rookie Malik Muhammad was with the ones at nickel with Jaylon Jones out. Cam Lewis, who figures to start at safety while Coby Bryant is out, was getting in some work at corner today. Anthony Johnson Jr. got some work with the starters at safety. ( link ) UDFA Skyler Thomas also got looks at safety with the ones. title: Cash, Stash, or Slash: Montez Sweat
summary: As we continue through this series, we continue to look at veteran players on the Chicago Bears roster and what they should do with them over the next 12 months. Should they extend them (cash), should they cut them (slash), or should they wait and see how the next year plays out (stash)? Next up, […]
full_text: CHICAGO, IL - JANUARY 10: Montez Sweat #98 of the Chicago Bears lines up before the snap during an NFC Wild Card Playoff game against the Green Bay Packers at Soldier Field on January 10, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images As we continue through this series, we continue to look at veteran players on the Chicago Bears roster and what they should do with them over the next 12 months. Should they extend them (cash), should they cut them (slash), or should they wait and see how the next year plays out (stash)? Next up, let’s look at Montez Sweat. Sweat is an interesting player to look at because he is by far the most productive player on the Bears’ defensive line, but many fans don’t think he has lived up to the contract that Ryan Poles gave him when the Bears traded for him from the Washington Commanders. Sweat’s contract expires after the 2027 season. What should the Bears do with him? Montez Sweat: Cash Baring a catastrophic injury or a massive drop-off in play, there’s close to no reason to slash Sweat, but there are plenty of reasons to stash him and see what happens after a couple of seasons. If I’m the Chicago Bears, I give Sweat an extension after this season. Some fans may be surprised at this stance, and I get it; Sweat turns 30 in September, extending him (let’s say 2 years) would be committing dollars to a player in their age 32 and 33 seasons. And it’s not like Sweat is a dynamic edge like a Micah Parsons or a Myles Garrett, but while you look at negatives, more so, look at the reasons why it should happen. First of all, you have to keep someone on the defensive line. It’s not like Ryan Poles is going to be able to go out after this season and just find 4 new DL to play, maybe three with Austin Booker. You need some stability there. Sweat is a reliable pass rusher, a strong run defender, and plays almost every Sunday and turns in a solid game. For fans who want Sweat to terrorize a game, he isn’t going to do that, but he is going to provide steady play and not let his side of the line get destroyed. Ideally, on a great defensive line, Sweat would be your second-best player. He would complement a stud opposite him or in the interior. But the Bears don’t have that, at least not right now. Sweat’s contract has also aged quite well. Sweat is now making half (literally half) of what the top edges in the game are being paid, and you would have to think if the Bears try to extend a solid but not spectacular player in his early 30s, there’s very little reason to think he would be looking for a massive raise in salary. Keeping Sweat around at his current price would be great for the Bears, who need to rework a lot of their defensive line if they are going to elevate this defense into a unit that belongs in the top half of the league. If the Bears want a solid D, you need more players like Sweat, not less. Sweat is not the type of guy who should be the best defensive player on a roster; it’s not his fault that the Bears don’t have better defenders than him. The durability Sweat has and the way he plays, I believe that he should be able to maintain this level of play at least for another three or four years, and if that’s the case, keeping him around as a building block piece on the defense with Devin Bush, Dillon Thieneman, and hopefully some guys like Austin Booker makes sense. Keep Sweat and add around him; subtracting him does very little to strengthen the Bears defense. It makes too much sense: keep Sweat, and fix the mistakes around him; don’t make another by letting him walk.

title: Chicago Bears injury updates (sort of) for Coby Bryant and Kyler Gordon
summary: Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson was asked this morning about a timeline for the return of safety Coby Bryant, who injured his knee at practice earlier this week, and he said the team was still gathering information. And about that 8-10 week timeline that ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported, Johnson said, “I don’t know where […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 19: Kyler Gordon #6 of the Chicago Bears tackles Alvin Kamara #41 of the New Orleans Saints during an NFL football game at Solider Field on October 19, 2025 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson was asked this morning about a timeline for the return of safety Coby Bryant, who injured his knee at practice earlier this week, and he said the team was still gathering information. And about that 8-10 week timeline that ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported, Johnson said, “I don’t know where you guys got that; hasn’t been said here. I’ll let you guys know whenever we know for sure what it looks like for him.” Johnson was also asked about his other injured defensive back, Kyler Gordon (calf), who began training camp on the Active/Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list, and who missed much of the offseason activities as well. “There is no update. He’s continuing to rehab.” As far as updates go, these are pretty thin, but we’re talking about two very important pieces of Dennis Allen’s defense. We’ll share more once we know more. Johnson also said it was good to have linebacker T.J. Edwards back, and that they’ll “continue to get him more involved and ramped up.” He added, “You could certainly feel his presence and hear his communication out there on the defense, which was good to see.” He also had some good stuff on Darnell Wright, the left tackle competition, Austin Booker, and more. You can check out his full press conference here.

title: Bengals working on tackling issues during training camp
summary: It’s no secret the Cincinnati Bengals have been among the worst tackling defenses in all of football over the last few seasons. On Thursday, the team began working on drills to try to improve their tackling issues. Zac Taylor said the Bengals would not be doing live tackling in practice, so the reps will come […]
full_text: Cincinnati Bengals safety Jordan Battle (27) chats with young fans during practice at the Paycor Stadium practice facility in downtown Cincinnati on Monday, Aug. 3, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co It’s no secret the Cincinnati Bengals have been among the worst tackling defenses in all of football over the last few seasons. On Thursday, the team began working on drills to try to improve their tackling issues. Zac Taylor said the Bengals would not be doing live tackling in practice, so the reps will come in drills over the next few practices to get ready for the Thursday preseason game against Detroit. This comes after defensive coordinator Al Golden said Tuesday that the Bengals would hold multiple live tackling drills in each of the next three practices starting Thursday morning. Demetrius Knight driving the pad into the ground and then some on tackling drills. #Bengals @FOX19 pic.twitter.com/ToBFEkYcC3 — Jeremy Rauch (@FOX19Jeremy) August 6, 2026 The improvement starts with the second-year linebackers. Demetrius Knight Jr. and Barrett Carter each finished in the top 15 of missed tackles on the season in 2025. Knight had a 15.0% missed tackle rate, with Carter closely behind that with a 14.8% missed tackle rate. Those numbers will have to improve for this Bengals defense to finish as a top half of the league unit in 2026. The additions of Dexter Lawrence and Jonathan Allen should free the young linebackers up to be in position to make plays this year. Now it is up to them to go out there and get the job done. Another position that will need improved tackling is at the safety position. Going from Geno Stone to Bryan Cook should immediately help at one of those spots. Stone finished the season with an abysmal 18,7% missed tackle rate, often looking like he didn’t want to get physical against the run or after a catch in the open field. Meanwhile, Bryan Cook was one of the better tacklers for a safety in the NFL, finishing the season with just a 5,7% missed tackle rate. The best in the NFL at the position was 4,1% for a player that played in at least 50% of the snaps on the season. At the other safety spot is the returning Jordan Battle. Battle will need to improve on his 13.7% missed tackle rate from 2025. Entering a contract season, it is a make-or-break year for Battle. He has flashed physicality at times against the run, but also has left people scratching their heads with pursuit angles and letting up after a catch near him at times in 2025.

title: Bengals will play starters in preseason opener vs. Detroit Lions
summary: While much of the attention throughout training camp has been paid to the defense’s impressive showing, one storyline that hadn’t gotten any traction until Thursday is how much the starters will play in the preseason, if at all. Well, head coach Zac Taylor clearly said Thursday that the starters will play next Thursday in the first preseason […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OHIO - JULY 29: Joe Burrow #9 of the Cincinnati Bengals performs during the Cincinnati Bengals Training Camp at Kettering Health Practice Fields on July 29, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images While much of the attention throughout training camp has been paid to the defense’s impressive showing, one storyline that hadn’t gotten any traction until Thursday is how much the starters will play in the preseason, if at all. Well, head coach Zac Taylor clearly said Thursday that the starters will play next Thursday in the first preseason game against the Detroit Lions. “They will play a little bit. We’ll just determine how much at a later date,” Taylor said. Perhaps this is another feather in the cap of the Bengals not messing around going into this season, showing a sense of urgency not seen in several years. Joe Burrow said before the Bengals went on their “summer break” that he wished the Bengals could have started training camp right after minicamp. The fact that Burrow won’t have to wait until the regular season to play in an actual game this year is a good thing. Burrow played in both of the Bengals’ first two preseason games last year. In Philadelphia to open the preseason, Burrow was 9-of-10 passing for 123 yards and two touchdowns. A week-and-a-half later against Washington, Burrow engineered a touchdown drive, but before that there was the infamous play where he was running for his life from a Washington pass rush that got free into the Bengals’ backfield. Perhaps none of that this preseason, please. The Bengals will play their first two preseason games at home against Detroit next Thursday night and the Chicago Bears on Saturday, August 22nd. The Bengals’ third and final preseason game is at Philadelphia against the Eagles on Friday, August 28th. CBS will nationally televise that game.

title: Josh Newton reportedly in the “doghouse” during Bengals training camp
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals know who their starting outside cornerbacks will be in 2026. After DJ Turner II’s breakout season in 2025, he is likely going to follow opponents’ primary receivers. After finding his home after moving around the defensive backfield, Dax Hill will start at the other boundary spot. A camp battle many fans were […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OH - OCTOBER 16: Josh Newton #28 of the Cincinnati Bengals looks on from the field after an NFL football game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Paycor Stadium on October 16, 2025 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cincinnati Bengals know who their starting outside cornerbacks will be in 2026. After DJ Turner II’s breakout season in 2025, he is likely going to follow opponents’ primary receivers. After finding his home after moving around the defensive backfield, Dax Hill will start at the other boundary spot. A camp battle many fans were excited to watch heading into training camp was slot corner. Newly signed veteran Ja’Sir Taylor is competing, but returning veteran Jaylen Davis has been taking the bulk of the first-team reps in the slot thus far. Enter Josh Newton. The fifth-rounder from the 2024 NFL Draft saw significant action his rookie year, but on the boundary and in the slot. Newton figured to be in the mix for the slot corner battle, but it appears to be a two-man race between Taylor and Davis at this point. It doesn’t get any better for Newton on the perimeter, either. The second team reps have been going to D.J. Ivey and rookie Tacario Davis. Newton seems to be on the outside looking in, and if a recent report is accurate, Newton could be a surprise cut when the team trims the roster to 53 players. The Athletic’s Paul Dehner Jr. reported that Newton has fallen out of favor with the coaches, something we saw reduce his role in 2025. “Josh Newton remains in the same doghouse that kept his snaps limited down the stretch last season,” Dehner wrote. Newton played 525 snaps his rookie year in 2024 and saw that number slashed to just 275 last season. With the infusion of both young and veteran talent to the cornerback room, Newton could be on the outside looking in when camp closes. Of course, it is very early in camp, and the team hasn’t even played a preseason game yet. There is plenty of time for Newton to turn things around. If other players falter, Newton could have an opportunity to take advantage, but as of now, Newton could be looking for a new home at the end of this month.

title: Bengals training camp Day 7 discussion and news
summary: Many fans probably would have been shocked to hear that the defense is holding its own in training camp so far. There have even been days when defenders have dominated. The presence of defensive lineman Dexter Lawrence and safety Bryan Cook has really changed the feel of this entire defense. That isn’t to diminish players […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 27: Barrett Carter #49 and Demetrius Knight Jr. #44 of the Cincinnati Bengals hold up turkey after the game against the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium on November 27, 2025 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Ishika Samant/Getty Images) | Getty Images Many fans probably would have been shocked to hear that the defense is holding its own in training camp so far. There have even been days when defenders have dominated. The presence of defensive lineman Dexter Lawrence and safety Bryan Cook has really changed the feel of this entire defense. That isn’t to diminish players like Boye Mafe constantly pressuring quarterback Joe Burrow. You can see how much the offense has to account for those guys, and also how easy it is for them to absolutely blow things up. It would be nice to see the offense go off more than a few plays during practice, but it’s safe to say most fans will take this change of pace. At least for now, that is. Bengals News Will Wagner Looks to Engineer Uneventful Year Two “I use my mechanical engineering degree pretty much every day in long snapping,” Wagner said in an interview while at Michigan. “In engineering, I have to know how matter is going to react if I put force in one place compared to another, and it’s the same in long snapping — how is the ball going to fly if I snap it one way versus another?” A very interesting look into the mind of a long snapper. If you have been a Bengals fan long enough you do not take for granted having a quality long snapper in the fold. Training Camp Report | New-Look Defense Turning Heads It was Carter who had a day Tuesday, playing downhill and, for the most part, helping bottle up an inside running game that had gouged holes the day before. Featuring some collisions with tight end Erick All Jr. as fullback. Knight was good, too, but Carter is the guy talking to Golden in his helmet before every play and getting them lined up. The defense as a whole had some really nice things to say about Barrett Carter and his performance so far in training camp. It is something fans will hope to see during the season. I sure I am not alone in that I would willingly eat crow if Carter turns things around. Bengals’ offensive players and coaches say Dexter Lawrence is dominating practices “There’s certain guys in this league like Dexter who wreck a whole game play and you have to do everything around them and you change everything you’re doing,” Risner said. “You’re going to have to change how you block against certain guys. He’s just making us do it really early and really often.” It certainly isn’t surprising to see Lawrence do these kinds of things. When the trade happened many were worried we might be getting a player on decline. It seems like that could not be further from the truth the way the offense is talking. Bengals Legend Anthony Muñoz Ranked Among 100 Greatest Players in NFL History The man truly deserves all the flowers he recieves. He was such a foundational piece over his career, and for too long, he was the only Bengals player in the Hall of Fame. Even though he has some company now, Muñoz will always be the player fans should think of when talking about the best Bengals of all-time. Who would you put on the Bengals Mount Rushmore?

title: Bengals safety Bryan Cook is embracing his leadership role
summary: At practice on Tuesday, cornerback DJ Turner was beaten deep by Ja’Marr Chase on what ended up being an incomplete pass. Turner didn’t have time to get down on himself because free-agent safety acquisition Bryan Cook was quickly by his side to give him a word of encouragement. Then, on the very next play, Boye […]
full_text: Cincinnati Bengals safety Bryan Cook (6) cheers after breaking up a play during practice at the Paycor Stadium practice facility in downtown Cincinnati on Tuesday, Aug. 4, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co At practice on Tuesday, cornerback DJ Turner was beaten deep by Ja’Marr Chase on what ended up being an incomplete pass. Turner didn’t have time to get down on himself because free-agent safety acquisition Bryan Cook was quickly by his side to give him a word of encouragement. Then, on the very next play, Boye Mafe, another free agent acquisition, beat Orlando Brown Jr. around the edge and forced Joe Burrow to throw an errant pass earlier than he wanted. Cook stepped in front of the pass, picked it off, and took it back for what would have been a touchdown had it been a real game. Later in the locker room, Cook reflected on the moment, showcasing his leadership, not only verbally, but with action. “For the most part, it’s just being aggressive, attention to detail, flying around, playing as one, and also being my brother’s keeper,” he said in the locker room after practice . “I know we’re all tired, but make a play. Any given moment, it could happen. I can be tired and have a great break at the post, and then Dexter Lawrence can get a sack. Things like that, it boosts the whole morale of a defense.” The Bengals’ defense has largely been to blame for the team missing the playoffs over the last two seasons. Sure, if they bounced their way one or two times in either season, they could have backed their way into the playoffs, but a team can win if they allow opposing teams to score 30 or more points as often as they did. This offseason, though, the Bengals’ front office took the big swing generations of fans have been asking for. They not only traded the No. 10 pick to the Giants for Lawrence, but they signed Cook, Mafe, Jonathan Allen and Kyle Dugger. Combined with this year’s draft class, the entire defense, except for linebacker, has been reshaped. With Cook’s leadership in the secondary and with the monster that is Lawrence soaking up blockers meant to get to linebackers, the defense will hopefully transform from a liability to a strength.

title: Bengals’ pass rush unit ranked near the bottom of the NFL
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals went all-in on fixing their defense this offseason. Despite losing Trey Hendrickson to the Baltimore Ravens, the Bengals made several additions all across the defense to try to fix the unit that shouldered the blame for missing the postseason the last two seasons. Included in those acquisitions was pass rusher Boye Mafe, […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 16: Myles Murphy #99 of the Cincinnati Bengals pressures Mason Rudolph #2 of the Pittsburgh Steelers during the third quarter at Acrisure Stadium on November 16, 2025 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cincinnati Bengals went all-in on fixing their defense this offseason. Despite losing Trey Hendrickson to the Baltimore Ravens, the Bengals made several additions all across the defense to try to fix the unit that shouldered the blame for missing the postseason the last two seasons. Included in those acquisitions was pass rusher Boye Mafe, who was basically signed as a replacement for Hendrickson. They will also return 2025 first-round pick Shemar Stewart when he returns from his hyperextended knee suffered early in training camp. 2023 first-rounder Myles Murphy is also back and likely motivated after his fifth-year option wasn’t picked up. Also joining the rotation is rookie and former SEC Defensive Player of the Year, Cashius Howell. CBS Sports’ Carter Bahns isn’t very confident in the Cincinnati pass rush this season. He recently released his rankings of all 32 pass rush groups in the NFL and slotted the Bengals near the bottom of the league at 29th. “While the rest of the Bengals’ defense improved on paper this offseason, the edge rusher group said farewell to its leader, Trey Hendrickson. Mafe is an upside-oriented addition who will not fully replace Hendrickson’s pass-rushing prowess, but who displayed flashes of greatness as a young starter for the Seattle Seahawks. The rest of the crew, plus second-round pick Cashius Howell, is extremely young. Cincinnati is banking on its last few drafts starting to pay off. It just might pay dividends, but it is impossible to know for sure until it actually happens,“ Bahn wrote. To be fair, there are quite a few unknowns along the defensive front and specifically at pass rusher, but 29 still feels awfully low when you consider the drastic improvements to the interior defensive line. Dexter Lawrence II should draw a lot of double teams and free up pass rushers to get home. Preseason rankings are just that, preseason predictions. In just over a month, the Bengals’ defense will have a chance to change that narrative on the field.

full_text: Out of all the players participating in Cleveland Browns training camp this offseason, Denzel Boston has certainly received the most excitement from both local and national media members. title: Deshaun Watson, Shedeur Sanders: Browns QB competition lingers on
summary: At Cleveland Browns training camp, installs are coming to an end– an important step, but where do things stand after almost two weeks of practices? New coach. New offensive system. Same questions. Evaluating the Browns quarterback room as constructed was an easy task last season and the year prior. Lack of talent, low ceiling, and […]
full_text: BEREA, OHIO - JUNE 11: Shedeur Sanders #2 of the Cleveland Browns laughs with Deshaun Watson #4 during the Cleveland Browns Mandatory Minicamp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on June 11, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images At Cleveland Browns training camp, installs are coming to an end – an important step, but where do things stand after almost two weeks of practices? New coach. New offensive system. Same questions. Evaluating the Browns quarterback room as constructed was an easy task last season and the year prior. Lack of talent, low ceiling, and uncertainty surrounded the entire room. Deshaun Watson, who is trying to salvage his career, is the only veteran in the room, but he hasn’t played since 2024. Shedeur Sanders and Dillon Gabriel were rookies last year, with Gabriel getting the first opportunity before Sanders last training camp. Sanders eventually took over, but neither him nor Gabriel did enough to prove they could be the starter in the future. Fast forward to today, the QB battle between Watson and Sanders is ongoing. As of now, neither Sanders nor Watson has taken the lead for the starting job. The more things change, the more they stay the same? It’s easy to formulate opinions about the current QB competition when you use a “QB tracker” that is lacking context when it comes to stats. However, as camp goes on, the reports coming out of camp regarding the competition have been back and forth. One day, Sanders is leading the competition, or Watson is leading the competition. At the same time, others are saying no one has stood out so far throughout the competition. Granted, the quarterbacks are learning a new offense, and they are currently going through the install period, but the little things when it comes to playing the quarterback position matter. Browns GM Andrew Berry to @bykevinclark on what he wants to see from whoever wins the QB competition: "Operating and decision-making … there's a set of at least 60 decisions that that player's going to make. And they're not going to be right in all of them. But if they can do… pic.twitter.com/yWbE1wun2h — Daniel Oyefusi (@DanielOyefusi) August 6, 2026 Browns coach Todd Monken on two attributes that are vital for a quarterback to have: mental toughness and accuracy. pic.twitter.com/oZBispXh2C — Daniel Oyefusi (@DanielOyefusi) August 5, 2026 However, the one that stands out as important is the pre-snap process. I was most impressed by the pre-snap operation today. It wasn’t perfect (Todd Monken ripped into a receiver one play) but on a day when Cleveland missed its top two centers, the offense won the cadence battle a couple times. https://t.co/cYEyJ6DWnV — Daniel Oyefusi (@DanielOyefusi) August 5, 2026 It’s clear that head coach Todd Monken is emphasizing the mental side of the quarterback position ahead of the physical. Monken is responsible for evolving Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson and his passing ability, so it’s clear why he is putting a ton of emphasis on that. In terms of the quarterbacks, both Watson and Sanders have had their share of good and bad days, but neither has strung together consistent days. Sanders has talent, but his ceiling is uncertain. Due to his lackluster tape from last season, he’s in a battle with Watson instead of having solidified his position as an NFL starter. There is a case to be made that if Sanders put together quality tape last season, he’s unequivocally the starter. It’s a reason why this is a QB battle, and it’s not because of Watson’s contract. The QB battle between Watson and Sanders will likely take the entire preseason and could come down to the preseason finale against the New England Patriots. However, the battle should be settled after the joint practices and second preseason game. It’s a possibility that the Browns are quietly shopping Sanders, in case he doesn’t win the starting job, due to the overcrowded room. Does that mean Sanders is likely to be traded? Probably not, and Cleveland is hoping it doesn’t come to that. Watson is likely going to play out his contract and move on after the season. Who knows, Gabriel, who many people have written off, could sneak into the competition and win the job, but that is still more of a long shot. The QB battle has no clear leader, and it might be a while before the team finds the answer before the end of the preseason. Where do you think the QB competition stands at this point in the process? title: Browns defender lands at No. 35 on NFL’s Top 100 list
summary: The Cleveland Browns made the decision earlier this summer, after months of contemplation, to trade reigning Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams.  While the trade was equally understandable and regrettable, general manager Andrew Berry held firm that he wanted more than just draft picks from the Rams in return […]
full_text: BEREA, OHIO - JULY 29: Alex Wright #91 and Jared Verse #8 of the Cleveland Browns high-five during Cleveland Browns Training Camp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on July 29, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns made the decision earlier this summer, after months of contemplation, to trade reigning Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams. While the trade was equally understandable and regrettable, general manager Andrew Berry held firm that he wanted more than just draft picks from the Rams in return for the game’s best defensive player. Berry wanted defensive end Jared Verse; otherwise, the deal was off . As the Browns near the end of the second week of training camp, it has been easy to see why Berry coveted Verse. The third-year player has been putting in the work, injecting some new energy into a defense under first-year defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg, and even helping rookie left tackle Spencer Fano get up to speed, knowing the Browns will need Fano to be ready when Week 1 rolls around. No. 35 on the NFL Top 100 Players of 2026… @Browns DE Jared Verse! @NFLFilms pic.twitter.com/YyBgnxW2Hh — NFL (@NFL) August 5, 2026 None of that has gone unnoticed, as head coach Todd Monken remarked this week when asked about Verse’s energy (quote via a team-provided transcript): “That’s really cool. I walked up to Jared and said, ‘Man, we’re so lucky you’re a Brown. I mean, holy s***, how cool is this?’ Because he’s not only a great leader, but he also works his rear end off every day, and after practice he’s trying to get Spencer better. I stood right behind him listening to what he was talking about, and it was bang, bang, bang, five reps in a row of his footwork, then talking through what he was going to do, how he could redirect, how he could use his hands and punch. It was within five reps I saw Spencer get better. It was him teaching like he was a coach, and it was awesome.” It is not just Monken and his teammates that are impressed by what Verse brings to the field, but his peers recognize it as well, which is why Verse moved up 18 spots this year to check in at No. 35 on the annual NFL Top 100 list as voted on by the players, with NFL.com’s Bobby Kownack writing that : Verse’s two-year Rams tenure was marked by success at every turn. The 2024 No. 19 overall pick made the Pro Bowl and won AP NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year in his first season, then followed it up by besting his previous sack total by three amid another Pro Bowl campaign. He’s also now 2 for 2 landing on the NFL Top 100 list. Any future accolades will have to come in new colors, though. Verse was key to the Browns’ willingness to trade Myles Garrett to Los Angeles, casting the 25-year-old in a feature role of Cleveland’s newest rebuild. NFL Pro Insight for Verse: Verse generated a team-high 67 pressures last season and converted 11.2% of those into sacks, nearly double his rookie rate. Verse has made the Pro Bowl in each of his first two seasons, was the league’s 2024 NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year in 2024, and has 12 sacks, 124 tackles, 22 tackles for loss, and 45 quarterback hits. He may not be Myles Garrett, and there is no shame in that, but if Verse keeps up the energy he has shown so far, then opposing quarterbacks may not be able to tell the difference when they face the Browns this fall. Verse joins linebacker Carson Schwesinger, who came in at No. 93 , as the only Cleveland players to make the list so far.

title: Buying Browns owner Jimmy Haslam’s optimism? Some are
summary: Front offices in professional sports will often be asked hard questions and, oftentimes, the front office will dodge those questions and give a response that is deemed “professional.” We’ve all heard the “coach speak.” Sports fans will ask for honesty and transparency from their favorite team, but nine times out of ten, it’s unlikely that […]
full_text: BEREA, OHIO - JUNE 09: Executive vice president, football operations & general manager Andrew Berry of the Cleveland Browns talks with managing and principal partners Jimmy Haslam and Dee Haslam during the Cleveland Browns Mandatory Minicamp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on June 09, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images Front offices in professional sports will often be asked hard questions and, oftentimes, the front office will dodge those questions and give a response that is deemed “professional.” We’ve all heard the “coach speak.” Sports fans will ask for honesty and transparency from their favorite team, but nine times out of ten, it’s unlikely that the fans will get that. The Cleveland Browns are entering Year 2 of a rebuild and, on paper, this team is nowhere near contention for a playoff spot. The looming QB question continues to be a concern for many. Despite that, Browns owner Jimmy Haslam spoke to the media a few days ago and gave interesting comments surrounding the team this season. As it stands, the Browns win total for the year is at 5.5 on multiple sports betting sites. Fans will likely roll their eyes at this statement, but Haslam seems to have some form of confidence that this Browns team will be better than last year. Jimmy Haslam and JW Johnson speaking to reporters after practice. Haslam: “I think the odds are for us to win 5.5 games. I’ll take the over.” pic.twitter.com/pyLh3Lkhpy — Daniel Oyefusi (@DanielOyefusi) July 31, 2026 Haslam also gave another comment surrounding this season: Haslam: "We want to be a contending playoff team in ’27." Johnson: "I just want to say we're not punting on this season by any means. ’27, whatever, that's great. But we have high expectations for this team." https://t.co/7ny3kasJq4 — Daniel Oyefusi (@DanielOyefusi) July 31, 2026 Ownership has a clear vision for the upcoming season, but they also have a clear vision for what this team wants to be the following season. Likely, their expectations are: 2026: Year 2 of a rebuild: Competitive but not contending 2027: Year 3 of a rebuild: Competitive, contending team in the AFC Ownership is not alone in having some confidence in taking the over on Cleveland’s win total: Jimmy Haslam would take the over on the Browns' projected win total of 5.5. It's not as crazy as it sounds. pic.twitter.com/co4mNVMNrE — PFT Live (@PFT_Live) August 3, 2026 It’s clear that the ownership wants to see noticeable progress for the team, but they also know that this team isn’t going to be in the playoff conversation this season. Trading star defensive end Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams might have sped up the team to potentially “punt” the season, but instead of selling, the team chose to retain key players. Cornerback Denzel Ward received a new extension; the same can be said for safety Grant Delpit. Considering that the Browns have an easier strength of schedule, the odds of the team winning more than 5.5 games are plausible; however, many things have to go their way for that to happen. Offensively, the unit has talent but major question marks; defensively, the unit lacks a true alpha, and head coach Todd Monken is entering his 1st year as a head coach. Rebuilding teams can often be ahead of schedule, as we’ve seen before, but don’t expect Cleveland to be one of those teams. It’s possible that this team is a fringe playoff contender next season, but this season expect more of what happened last season, even if they add a win or two. The team will not be good enough to be in playoff contention but not bad enough to be a top 3 team picking in the upcoming NFL Draft. Young, competitive, but just not good enough, just as Haslam seems to be alluding to. Join the conversation! title: Browns get a stray diss from current Eagles defender
summary: Seven days into the 2026 NFL free agency period, Cleveland Browns GM Andrew Berry signed a very good pass rusher in DE A.J. Epenesa away from the Buffalo Bills. The deal was for one-year at $5 million. At the time of the signing, it was assumed that the corner opposite Myles Garrett needed a dynamic […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - JULY 30: Philadelphia Eagles defensive end A.J. Epenesa #57 runs a drill during the Philadelphia Eagles training camp on July 30th, 2026 at Jefferson Health Training Complex in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Seven days into the 2026 NFL free agency period, Cleveland Browns GM Andrew Berry signed a very good pass rusher in DE A.J. Epenesa away from the Buffalo Bills. The deal was for one-year at $5 million. At the time of the signing, it was assumed that the corner opposite Myles Garrett needed a dynamic pass rusher who was decent against the run but had a lot of presence in the opponent’s backfield. RELATED: BROWNS FEEL GOOD ABOUT DEFENSIVE END POSITION The signing got average grades of “B-.” Matt Warren, NFL Community Director for SB Nation and Buffalo Rumblings contributor, gave this note on the Epenesa signing: “Played significant snaps for the Bills. Seems cheap to me.” And so, it was assumed that Berry had gotten a good pass rusher who would compete for snaps with Alex Wright and Isaiah McGuire on that left side. Quality depth was about to come to Cleveland after the franchise lost DE Cameron Thomas to the Atlanta Falcons. Then, 11 days later, Cleveland decided to rescind the contract due to issues with the player when he visited the Berea facility and concerns after he took his physical, a source informed ESPN . After visiting the facility and undergoing a standard medical evaluation, team officials opted not to finalize the paperwork. Similar, but on a much smaller level, to the Baltimore Ravens rescinding their trade for DE Maxx Crosby. Epenesa had played six years in the NFL and was a second-round draft pick of the Bills in the 2020 NFL draft. His forte is being a pass rusher. Last year, he had only 2.5 sacks in 16 games played, but from 2022-2024, he had 19 combined sacks and 31 QB hits. Epenesa kicks the INT to himself! BUFvsCAR on FOX/FOX One https://t.co/HkKw7uXnxV pic.twitter.com/qx0HUbD2PN — NFL (@NFL) October 26, 2025 It generally surprised most folks when Cleveland backed out of the arrangement after being uncomfortable with the medical findings. It wasn’t like Epenesa had ended the 2025 season on any list or was injured in any way. He wasn’t. He appeared in all 17 regular-season games plus the playoffs. The Browns never really stated what the medical issue was with Epenesa. They just announced they had rescinded the deal, and that was that. It wasn’t like the franchise quoted the “Lemon Law” or anything. At the time, Epenesa called it “a weird situation.” On June 10, Epenesa signed with the Philadelphia Eagles but did not disclose terms other than that he inked a one-year deal. Now, Epenesa is discussing his brief time of almost being a Cleveland Brown : “I don’t necessarily want to go back and talk about that. I’ll just leave that in the past and just be happy that I’m not a Brown and that I’m an Eagle. Very healthy, feeling good, and happy to be here.“ Epenesa, age 27, appeared in 91 games over six seasons in Buffalo, including 19 starts.

title: Cobie Durant has made an outstanding first impression in Dallas
summary: After an off day on Wednesday, the Dallas Cowboys were back in action Thursday afternoon, conducting their sixth practice of training camp out in Oxnard, California. With the pads coming on at the start of the week, we’ve seen the intensity rise over the last few practices. While the Cowboys’ first preseason game is still […]
full_text: After an off day on Wednesday, the Dallas Cowboys were back in action Thursday afternoon, conducting their sixth practice of training camp out in Oxnard, California. With the pads coming on at the start of the week, we’ve seen the intensity rise over the last few practices. While the Cowboys’ first preseason game is still over a week away, this week of practice seems to be an indication that Dallas is ready to roll as we inch closer to the preseason opener. It’s not always easy to separate yourself during training camp, but we’ve seen a few players do just that early on. One guy who has been as impressive as any player in Oxnard is free agent acquisition Cobie Durant. The 27-year-old cornerback, who signed a one-year, $4M deal back in March to join the Cowboys, was not viewed as one of their most significant offseason additions. While it was clear Durant was a solid contributor, he was not seen as capable of making the same impact as guys like Rashan Gary and Jalen Thompson. Granted, we are only a week into training camp, but through six practices in Oxnard, Durant has looked as good as any player on Dallas’ defense. The former Los Angeles Ram has put together multiple impressive showings and has many believing he can make a real impact as a starting-caliber corner in the Cowboys’ secondary. as I’ve said: Cobie Durant is simply not having it in training camp. #Cowboys spectacular downfield coverage. pic.twitter.com/mxQeev8DH0 — Patrik [No C] Walker (@VoiceOfTheStar) August 4, 2026 Dak Prescott under duress attempts to squeeze it in to CeeDee Lamb. Cobie Durant says not on his watch — INT. #Cowboys pic.twitter.com/DObKkWUxc9 — Patrik [No C] Walker (@VoiceOfTheStar) August 3, 2026 Cobie Durant tight coverage and a PBU against CeeDee Lamb. pic.twitter.com/u3NTgg9AWe — Joseph Hoyt (@JoeJHoyt) August 3, 2026 There’s reason to believe Durant is capable of carrying this level of play into the regular season. While the former fourth-round pick was never the focal point of the Rams’ defense, he was an above-average contributor during his time in Los Angeles. In 2025, Durant had the best playmaking season of his four-year NFL career. The 27-year-old finished the season with an extremely impressive six interceptions (regular-season + postseason) to go with a career-high six PBUs and a respectable 79.2 passer rating against . With Shavon Revel’s struggles during his rookie year, there is a good chance Durant finds himself as the starting outside corner opposite Daron Bland in Week 1. While in the long term the Cowboys absolutely need Revel to become at least an adequate starting corner, Durant being a capable starter would do wonders for their playoff hopes this upcoming season. The South Carolina State product is battle-tested, having played 650 or more defensive snaps in three consecutive seasons. This is something that will be very important for Dallas’ cornerback room this season. As mentioned above, while Revel may be the future, the Cowboys are in a win-now window. By the looks of the way he has been playing and his starting experience, going with Durant as the second starter will likely give them the best chance to make a serious playoff push this year. We may be just a week into camp, but Cobie Durant looks like he’s ready for the regular season to start as soon as possible.

title: Cowboys countdown to kickoff: Top 100 iconic games – Day 38
summary: It is Day 38 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like […]
full_text: Jan 14, 1996; Irving, TX, USA; FILE PHOTO; Dallas Cowboys tight end Jay Novacek (84) is chased by Green Bay Packers linebacker George Koonce (53) at Texas Stadium during the 1995 NFC Championship Game. Dallas defeated Green Bay 38-27. Mandatory Credit: James D. Smith-USA TODAY Sports | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It is Day 38 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like how big the game was for the organization, how memorable the game was, games that had unusual events take place, games that are a part of NFL lore, Cowboys firsts, and games where the Cowboys just plain dominated. Variety is the spice of life and we have all different kind of Cowboys games to review. At the bottom, we’ll link each day of the countdown so you can go back and check out any you missed. We reach day 38 of our 100-day countdown, when we revisit the Cowboys’ final tune-up before another heavyweight NFC Championship showdown with the San Francisco 49ers. Green Bay arrived at Texas Stadium hoping to prove it was ready to join the NFC’s elite. Dallas had other plans for Green Bay. Sunday, January 8, 1995 — 12:30 p.m. ET Texas Stadium, Irving, Texas Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 35, Green Bay Packers 9 The Cowboys quickly took control of the game. Kevin Williams returned the opening kickoff 36 yards to the Green Bay 49, giving Dallas excellent field position. Troy Aikman and Emmitt Smith then orchestrated a 51-yard drive that culminated in Smith scoring from five yards out. Chris Boniol’s extra point secured a 7-0 lead for the Cowboys less than four minutes into the game. Green Bay answered with a 50-yard field goal from Chris Jacke, but Dallas produced the game’s defining play on its next possession. Backed up at his own six-yard line, Aikman dropped into his end zone and launched the ball deep toward Alvin Harper. Harper made the catch near midfield and raced away for a 94-yard touchdown, stretching the lead to 14-3. The explosion was vintage Harper. Michael Irvin and Jay Novacek handled much of the underneath and intermediate work, while Harper supplied the field-changing strike that broke Green Bay’s confidence. A possession that began inches from Dallas’ goal line ended with the Cowboys celebrating at the opposite end of Texas Stadium. Dallas faced a major concern when Smith left the game in the first quarter with a hamstring injury. Despite rushing seven times for 44 yards and scoring the opening touchdown, the Cowboys were forced to rely on Blair Thomas to carry most of the rushing workload. Instead of letting the injury hinder their offense, Dallas continued to move the ball effectively through Aikman’s passing and Thomas’ steady running. Thomas scored from one yard out midway through the second quarter, extending the Cowboys’ lead to 21-3. Green Bay responded with their only touchdown when Edgar Bennett crossed from one yard, but Brett Favre’s two-point pass failed. Despite the Packers cutting the margin to 21-9, Dallas still had enough time to deliver another blow before halftime. Aikman moved the Cowboys downfield once more and finished the drive with a one-yard touchdown pass to reserve tight end Scott Galbraith. The score came with only seconds left in the half and sent Dallas into the locker room leading 28-9. Dallas slowed the tempo after halftime, trusting its defense and running game to protect the lead. The Packers were held scoreless over the final two quarters, failed on two fourth-down attempts and finished four-of-16 on third down. Thomas completed the scoring with a two-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter. He finished with 70 yards and two touchdowns on 23 carries, giving Dallas exactly what it needed after Smith’s injury. This game belongs on the countdown because it was the bridge between a strong regular season and the matchup everyone had been waiting to see. Dallas had finished 12-4 during Barry Switzer’s first year as head coach, but the season was always going to be judged by whether the Cowboys could get through San Francisco again. By dismantling Green Bay, Dallas earned a third consecutive NFC Championship meeting with the 49ers. #Cowboys vs #Packers 1995 Divisional Round Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 35, Green Bay Packers 9 #DallasCowboys #NFL (📽️: @nfl ) pic.twitter.com/auFZdnnOGe — Mike Poland (@kenfigkowboy) August 6, 2026 Interesting Facts About the Game Harper’s 94-yard touchdown remains the longest offensive play in Cowboys playoff history. title: Unexpected surprises at Cowboys training camp
summary: The Dallas Cowboys have now completed one week of training camp out in Oxnard. It hasn’t just been the California sun that has shined, but also several players and position groups are looking extremely sharp right out of the gate. Dak Prescott is already looking in mid-season form as the 11-year veteran has been wheeling […]
full_text: OXNARD, CALIFORNIA - JULY 30: Javonte Williams #33 of the Dallas Cowboys runs with the ball during training camp at River Ridge Playing Fields on July 30, 2026 in Oxnard, California. (Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys have now completed one week of training camp out in Oxnard. It hasn’t just been the California sun that has shined, but also several players and position groups are looking extremely sharp right out of the gate. Dak Prescott is already looking in mid-season form as the 11-year veteran has been wheeling and dealing on a daily basis. Rookie safety Caleb Downs is everything that people said he was, and his versatility is going to bring a different element to what the Cowboys do defensively under Christian Parker. Also, Qunnien Williams and Kenny Clark are showing how disruptive they can be. While all those things are great to see, they aren’t shockers by any means. However, there been several things that have stood out that most people didn’t see coming. Let’s take a look at three surprises so far at camp. Several RBs are having great camps early Javonte Williams is the undisputed RB1 in Dallas. Don’t tell him that though, because he’s been playing with his hair on fire. He looks explosive running between the tackles, and he’s even been featured in the screen game, which is something that head coach Brian Schottenheimer talked about before camp. With that said, he’s not alone. Jaydon Blue didn’t have the rookie season he wanted in 2025, but he has put that in his rear view. He looks very confident in what he’s doing, and his speed has been on full display with several huge plays so far. Add Phil Mafah’s name to this as well. He worked on his explosiveness during the offseason, and positive results have come about already. Williams had a very good season a year ago with over 1,200 yards, proving that he can be a bell-cow. Dallas needs for him to be fresh at the end of ball games, and the best way to do that is having other reliable options. Blue and Mafah are showing early that this group has the potential to cause a lot of headaches for opposing defenses. Jaishawn Barham looks ahead of schedule Jaishawn Barham was picked in the third round by Dallas back in April, and there was buzz about what he could potentially bring to the Cowboys revamped defense. None if that mattered until he got camp, which is when he would really have to prove if he wanted early playing time. Not only is he showing that he’s going to be a big factor, but Barham looks like a guy who has already been in the league for years. The former Michigan Wolverine has shined in individual drills and during team periods against the likes of All-Pro guard Tyler Smith and the aforementioned Blue. He brings linebacker and edge skills to the table, and Parker intends to take full advantage of that versatility in his philosophy. Needless to say, Barham is undoubtedly ahead of where people thought he’d be right now. Otito Ogbonnia is standing out The Cowboys decided to trade defensive tackle Osa Odighizuwa to the San Francisco 49ers on March 11th. The day before that, they added Ogbonnia to the roster, who played in 41 games with 20 starts over his four years with the Los Angeles Chargers. He has some injury history, including missing eight games with an elbow issue last season. Ogbonnia also has a reputation for stopping the run, and its been no different in camp. In the Cowboys base look, Ogbonnia has been on the field with Qunnien Williams and Kenny Clark, and the trio have been effective consistently. Stopping the run has been a huge issue for Dallas over the years, and Ogbonnia and his 6’4″, 320-pound frame can be a big difference maker. It wasn’t a flashy signing, but Ogbonnia could end up being an impact offseason addition in Dallas.

title: Things we have learned at training camp so far
summary: We are a week into training camp. So far, the Dallas Cowboys have had five practices, and two of them have been with pads on. full_text: OXNARF, CA - JULY 28: Workers drive a cart while setting up for the opening of Dallas Cowboys training camp on Tuesday, July 28, 2026, in Oxnard, Calif. (Smiley N. Pool/The Dallas Morning News via Getty Images) We are a week into training camp. So far, the Dallas Cowboys have had five practices, and two of them have been with pads on. Even during this brief window, we have some answers to some of the many questions we had going into camp. Today we’ll explore a few of those answers. Caleb Downs is a student of the game This may not come as a surprise but the rookie from Ohio State, who received rave reviews from past coaches including Nick Saban, is as studious and focused as advertised. Typically, rookies have growing pains, and while Downs hasn’t been perfect, usually the types of mistakes that are endured when bringing a first-year pro along are those that happen when teaching a rookie a pro system and bone-headed errors that usually take weeks to iron out. Yet, Downs has received nothing but rave reviews for his work ethic and focus, particularly from his head coach, Brian Schottenheimer. TRENDING: Caleb Downs has been a NIGHTMARE for the Cowboys offense. One NFL scout reportedly believes Downs “showcases” similar abilities to Ed Reed (Former Ravens S). The Cowboys rookie safety is going to be a PROBLEM in this league 🔒😳 pic.twitter.com/zomo2IqXSS — Rookie Watch (@RookieWatxh) August 5, 2026 As we continue to progress in camp and see some field action in the preseason, Cowboys fans can only be hopeful that Downs is going to be everything they had wished for (if he plays). The secondary is much improved The secondary unit was terrible last year. Between the entire secondary, only four interceptions were secured by this position group in 2025. In the offseason, the Cowboys addressed these concerns by bringing in the likes of Cobie Durant and Jalen Thompson and, as mentioned earlier, drafting the highly touted Downs in the first round, along with hiring new defensive coordinator Christian Parker, who is also receiving rave reviews from players and coaches alike. Now, as practice gets underway, we’ve gotten a glimpse of this unit in action, and the difference seems to be night and day from last year, both in production on the practice field and in intensity. Watch two things closely: 1. Dak no-looked the throw 2. Cobie Durants instincts beat what otherwise would have been an easy Touchdown Imma say it again… GIVE CHRISTIAN PARKER the keys to the city if a healthy & effective Daron Bland is the 3rd best CB on this Cowboys… pic.twitter.com/vO3dRmUrw4 — Landon Holifield ✭ (@TheLandoShow) August 5, 2026 Durant, Daron Bland and Shavon Revel have been sticky and have made plays, and they’ll need that, along with the fiery attitudes they’ve shown thus far in practice, to make the leaps necessary to turn this unit into a quality unit in 2026. Tyler Guyton is the Cowboys’ starting left tackle Yes, most of us could see right through Schottenheimer’s shrewd motivational tactic when he “opened up” the left tackle position for competition. Even still, given Guyton’s struggles in his first few years, it seemed the competition might be open. Nope, the door was slammed shut on that Tuesday, August 4. Now, again, there may not have been much of a competition between Guyton and seventh-round pick Nate Thomas. Guyton still had to do enough to secure the nomination from Schottenheimer, which isn’t nothing. The Cowboys have an opportunity to put together what could be a special offensive unit in 2026. Guyton, along with fellow offensive tackle Terence Steele, is one of the linchpins for whether or not GOTI (Greatest Offense There Is) is. Here’s Guyton battling Quinnen Williams to further your optimism Quinnen Williams and Tyler Guyton going to war in the interior pic.twitter.com/bUuNiehbWF — Mike Leslie (@MikeLeslieWFAA) August 5, 2026
