title: 3 players pushing for a roster spot at Cowboys training camp
summary: The Dallas Cowboys are at training camp and some of the players have given the coaches a lot to think about so far. There are a few who need a really strong camp to even have a shot at being considered for the team. Some of that has been the result of circumstances out of […]
full_text: May 1, 2026; Frisco, TX, USA; Dallas Cowboys tight end Michael Trigg (46) goes through a drill during practice at the Ford Center at the Star Training Facility in Frisco, Texas. Mandatory Credit: Chris Jones-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Dallas Cowboys are at training camp and some of the players have given the coaches a lot to think about so far. There are a few who need a really strong camp to even have a shot at being considered for the team. Some of that has been the result of circumstances out of their control, and sometimes it’s their own efforts. Next Saturday the team plays its first game of the preseason, and it presents a chance for the fringe players to shine. Who are the fringe guys that have impressed so far? Furthermore, who are the players that are taking advantage of a fast start to make moves toward earning a spot on the roster? Here are the players who are angling for a spot on the team. Michael Trigg Following the draft, Michael Trigg signed with the Cowboys as an undrafted free agent. Dallas signed Trigg to a three-year contract worth up to $3.1M. Trigg was a finalist for the Mackey Award and was named an All-American in his final year at Baylor. Trigg is more like a big wide receiver than a traditional tight end. Because of this, he is a mismatch for linebackers and a handful for them to keep up with him in coverage. He has flashed his talents at training camp, and everyone is starting to take notice. The Michael Trigg hype train is off and running pic.twitter.com/QUsZ5nunYN — RJ Ochoa (@rjochoa) August 3, 2026 The Cowboys also got word that fellow tight end Princeton Fant went down with a season-ending knee injury. Fant may have already been on the fringe, but his absence opens a door that Trigg’s talent could see him run through. With Fant out of the picture, Trigg is going to get extended looks to build on what he’s already done. Two solid preseason games, and the Cowboys may not want to risk losing him. Sam Williams Although Sam Williams has been a part of the team since 2022, it’s very clear that nothing will be guaranteed to him. Williams rejoined the Cowboys on a one-year contract with a base salary of only $1.4M. Obviously, the team has much more invested in the players ahead of him on the roster. To the detriment of the team but also to the benefit of Williams for the time being, the collective pass rush hasn’t done so well. This has allowed Williams to stand out from the rest of the pack. Williams has terrific athleticism relative to the edge rusher position. We have seen him showcase his talents as a gunner and, at times in camp, has looked fairly good in coverage. Sam Williams meets Jaydon Blue in the backfield pic.twitter.com/jIoYArkkLt — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) August 4, 2026 Sam Williams vs Drew Shelton pic.twitter.com/6898cHCJH3 — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) August 4, 2026 Williams and James Houston appear locked into a hotly contested roster battle, and Houston had a solid day Monday as well as picked up a sack in practice. Williams can earn a spot not only by his own merits but also in some part by default if others don’t step it up to keep serve with Williams. Now in his fifth year, if the lights do come on for him, it could be the perfect time for the team and for Williams. Curtis Robinson Curtis Robinson hasn’t played much in the NFL since going undrafted in 2021. He’s mostly maintained his spot in the NFL as a core special teams player. Yet, the Cowboys have given him a little more responsibility. He, along with others, has been entrusted with wearing the defensive green dot to relay defensive signals to the defense. Unlike his other linebacker counterparts like Justin Barron, for example, he has a little more in-game experience on defense and has logged a lot of time on special teams coverage. PICK-6! Curtis Robinson takes it to the 🏠 Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/8P3YGE8sAT — NFL (@NFL) August 24, 2025 That alone has given him a leg up on the competition as he battles for one of the lower spots on the depth chart. There’s still a long way to go, but if Robinson can stay the course and continue to validate the coaches’ faith in his cognitive abilities, he might make it out of camp with a roster spot.

title: Why the Cowboys left tackle battle is over
summary: Tyler Guyton is the left tackle for the Dallas Cowboys. This has always been the hope since he was selected late in the first round of the 2024 NFL draft, and his job security was brought into question after head coach Brian Schottenheimer announced in early June that the position was up for grabs between […]
full_text: Tyler Guyton is the left tackle for the Dallas Cowboys. This has always been the hope since he was selected late in the first round of the 2024 NFL draft, and his job security was brought into question after head coach Brian Schottenheimer announced in early June that the position was up for grabs between Guyton and Nate Thomas. For now, the decision has been made with the former Oklahoma tackle keeping the starting spot. The left tackle position has been a little up in the air for the last couple of months, with lingering factors creating uncertainty. Most of which stems from the availability and progress of Guyton. He’s dealt with injuries in each of his first two seasons in the league, and when he has played, he hasn’t shown enough consistency to give the coaching staff confidence that he is the long-term plan at the position. Thomas’ name was thrown into the hat after a promising debut last season. A seventh-round pick in the same draft as Guyton, Thomas missed his entire rookie season dealing with knee tendinitis, landing him on injured reserve. He returned last year and played all 17 games, including making four starts when Guyton got hurt. He put together a decent rookie campaign, showing good things as a run blocker, but he also struggled in pass protection. He allowed 23 pressures, three sacks, and four penalties. A promising start made this a supposed open battle to start the camp as the coaching staff initially planned to evaluate both tackles in four-day cycles. This evaluation period was short-lived as the team appears to have already made its decision. Thomas showed some nice spurts, but Schottenheimer stated that he wasn’t showing enough consistency. His ongoing struggles with pass protection have created enough separation between him and Guyton, making the choice easy for the coaching staff. It’s not just the fading of Thomas that’s driving this decision. Guyton has looked impressive in camp. The coaches have praised him for his technical growth, and it has shown up in his performance over these first training camp practices. His footwork has looked sharp. He’s popping out quickly, setting well in his stance, and showing a lot more control and balance. He’s putting himself in good spots early and has shown nice leverage on several reps in camp. These improvements are huge for Guyton. His dedication is noted as he returned to the weight room in early February. His hand punching and physical power have been evident as he’s been seen driving defenders back. All the signs are pointing to him finally turning a corner this season. Guyton was selected on Day 1 because of his elite athletic traits accompanying his prototypical frame of an NFL left tackle. The potential has always been there, but he just hasn’t made the right strides in his development to be a player one can count on to protect the blindside of your franchise quarterback. But now these strides are more evident, and things are looking up for the Cowboys’ young offensive tackle. I don't care what anyone says. I believe Tyler Guton will be special this year. Not just good but special. He looks amazing. I see change. Real change. He already had the heart and work ethic!!!! Year 3 blow up coming. pic.twitter.com/vP6k7mDZKJ — Boss *Show Me (@BossCowboySport) August 4, 2026

title: Sean Payton reflects on Mike Shanahan’s legacy, Hall of Fame case
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country! Mike Shanahan is a Hall of Famer. He’s one of the best coaches in the history of the NFL. Whether the former Denver Broncos head coach and member of the Broncos Ring of Fame gets the nod when the committe votes this year for induction next year remains to be seen. […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - OCTOBER 31: Former Head Coach for the Denver Broncos Mike Shanahan stands on the field during halftime against the Washington Football Team at Empower Field at Mile High on October 31, 2021 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country! Mike Shanahan is a Hall of Famer. He’s one of the best coaches in the history of the NFL. Whether the former Denver Broncos head coach and member of the Broncos Ring of Fame gets the nod when the committe votes this year for induction next year remains to be seen. As current Broncos head coach Sean Payton said on Thursday after training camp practice (Shanahan was in attendance) in regards to Shanahan and his Hall of Fame candidacy: “Yes. He’s going to be there … Mike’s going to be there. It’s not if; it’s just what year.” Shanahan’s resume speaks for itself. He’s the winningest coach in Broncos’ history, one of the most successful franchises in the history of the NFL. Shanahan is one of seven coaches to win back-to-back Super Bowls (Chuck Knoll did it twice with the Pittsburgh Steelers). Of those seven, four are in the Hall of Fame, with two as locks when the time comes for Bill Belichick (maybe?) and Andy Reid. From 1996-98, Shanahan oversaw one of the most successful periods in NFL history. Denver won 46 games and two Super Bowls. The Shanahan coaching tree and his offensive mind continue to influence the league in major ways. His time as offensive coordinator with the San Francisco 49ers helping Steve Young win his first Super Bowl as a starting quarterback. If that wasn’t enough, here’s some more tidbits to prove how incredible Shanahan was, especially in Denver. The Broncos led the league in both 1,000-yard rushing seasons (11) and 1,000-yard receiving seasons (18) during Shanahan’s 14 years as Denver’s head coach. “I think, and this is with respect to Mike, there was only one Shanahan offense, and then there were these offshoots and very good offshoots,” Payton said to the media on Thursday. “I think that it really depends on … Each coach has taken his maybe spin on it. The one thing I would say is the commitment to running the ball well. You always felt that with Mike’s teams. A strong commitment to running the ball well, and the boots and the play-actions that come off of it. “Those are the first things that hit my mind. Then obviously the route combinations can vary, but that would be the first thing that I think they did better than anyone. They ran the stretch series, the play-action off of it. It really became problematic for defenses.” Of course when anyone discusses a candidate for the Hall of Fame, it comes back to the impact they had on the NFL. The old, “Can you write the story of the NFL without Mike Shanahan?” For Shanahan, he continues to leave his mark even after long being retired. As Payton said on Thursday: “My first year in the league in 1997 with Philadelphia, Jon Gruden had me, we had Beta then, had me cutting up four offensive teams, one being Denver. There was a game, you guys were too young, but they played Dallas and Mike started getting into these, the (wide receiver) outside Rod Smith to get man-zone reads. It was an empty package. It was like Denver really had a good offensive game that day … it was must-watch. You had to get that game tape. “So Mike, and then the coaching tree, and then the Super Bowls, every element of it fits just like the Broncos and Elway and the many members of that team. There’s a chapter, a number of chapters, that are attributed to that timeframe. So I’m looking at it really more in a microscope relative to what he was doing before anyone else was doing it. “So there are elements to him being the head coach, but then him being a heck of an offensive play caller and a forward thinker relative to how he utilized his personnel, the success they had with the wide-zone scheme, all of the play-action mechanics with. So yes, a very important part of our history.”
author: Ian St. Clair

title: 2026 Denver Broncos Training Camp: Day 6 News and Notes
summary: Day 6 of Denver Broncos training camp is in the books, and it was a less physical practice than the ones they have had in previous days. That was mostly due to them being out of pads, after three straight padded practices, and in shells. The pads go back on likely Saturday when they have […]
full_text: CENTENNIAL , CO - AUGUST 6: Cornerback Jahdae Barron (23) of the Denver Broncos stretches during practice on Thursday, August. 6, 2026, at Broncos Park in Centennial, Colo.(Photo by Timothy Hurst/MediaNews Group/The Denver Post via Getty Images) | Denver Post via Getty Images Day 6 of Denver Broncos training camp is in the books, and it was a less physical practice than the ones they have had in previous days. That was mostly due to them being out of pads, after three straight padded practices, and in shells. The pads go back on likely Saturday when they have a scrimmage and expect the intensity to ramp back up then. The big story coming out of this practice was updates on the Broncos’ injured players. Thankfully, we have good news to report. Star WR Jaylen Waddle should be back in “4 or 5 days”, Nik Bonitto returned to the field on a limited basis, Courtland Sutton is just getting some load management, and Luke Wattenberg didn’t practice, but was once again present for practice. So, while the team might be a tad bit banged up, thankfully, they are just dealing with some minor stuff right now. Stacking days ⚒️ pic.twitter.com/VZdShik9BB — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) August 6, 2026 In today’s camp report, we have second-year wide receiver Pat Bryant thriving while Waddle and Sutton are sidelined, cornerback Jahdae Barron has his best practice of camp, more about Courtland Sutton’s load management, news and notes, injury updates, tweets from camp, quotes and more Pat Bryant thrives while Waddle and Sutton are sidelined With star wide receiver Jaylen Waddle sidelined for “4 to 5 days” and Courtland Sutton going through load management, the Broncos were down their top two wide receivers for today’s practice. This gave a pretty big opportunity for the wide receivers battling for the WR3 job, and according to reports, second-year wide receiver Pat Bryant thrived. Pat Bryant makes plays every damn day. Clear WR3 to me — Ryan Edwards (@redwardsradio) August 6, 2026 He was beginning to stand out late last season and has carried that momentum into the offseason and now into training camp. As Ryan Edwards stated above, Pat Bryant is making plays every damn day and looks like the clear WR3 to him. After practice, cornerback Riley Moss was asked how difficult it has been covering Bryant during training camp so far. He told reporters that Bryant is really good vertically, and he makes his releases look all the same. He added that he is strong at the catch point, he can get up, and he has a big frame. “He’s really good vertically and he makes his releases look all the same, which is tough for a guy like me. When he’s shooting 15 yards deep and then he’ll cut in or he’ll cut out, it all looks the same. He does a great job. Then at the catch point, he’s strong. He can get up. He has a big frame.” From the start, I always believed Bryant was the favorite to be the WR3 for this offense. We saw him elevate his game late last season; he has great hands, gets open, blocks, and simply makes plays. He may not have the speed of Mims or Franklin, but he is the better all-around wide receiver. I would still have him as the favorite, but Mims sure has been making a strong push for snaps and touches as well. Franklin has had a quieter camp thus far, and will need a strong push to enter the conversation, it seems. We are only a week into camp so a lot can and probably will change moving forward. Jahdae Barron has his best day of camp For those anxiously awaiting an update on 2025 first-round pick Jahdae Barron, we have one today. After having a fairly unspectacular start to camp where he hasn’t done anything noteworthy, good or bad, the talented corner had his best practice of camp today. The Denver Post’s Luca Evans tweeted out that Barron had a “really nice day at Broncos Camp”. He added that Barron snuffed out a screen pass to Pat Bryant, nearly lit Bryant up during a play, and just had a PBU. He later tweeted out that Barron won 3 reps in a row when asked if he has won a rep at all during camp. So, not the most exciting update, but still good to see Barron playing well out there when many fans and media were starting to panic about him. The pads were off, which should be noted, but hopefully he can start stacking positive days together and really flip the narrative surrounding him right now. Jahdae Barron’s had a really nice day at #Broncos camp thus far. Snuffed out a screen to Pat Bryant earlier in team, nearly lit up Bryant on a play this period and just had a subsequent PBU — Luca Evans (@bylucaevans) August 6, 2026 After practice, cornerback Riley Moss was asked about Barron, and he told reporters that Barron has become more patient . He noted that he has played dime, nickel, and outside, and the job description for all three are a bit different. He says his eyes have gotten a lot better, he’s athletic, and that it takes time to get used to the outside but that he has been progressing well. I think the talk of Barron pushing Moss and/or McMillian for a starting job is dead for now, especially with the way Moss has been performing thus far. However, the fact he had a good day and seems to be developing and progressing well is good news. He will need to finish camp and the preseason strong to quiet the noise outside the building, but this is a positive first step. Courtland Sutton is healthy despite sitting out practice The mystery around Courtland Sutton’s absence appears to be solved. Over the past two days, veteran wide receiver Courtland Sutton did not participate in practice. He was present, but out of pads and on the sideline. Head Coach Sean Payton has continued to say it was just a rest day for him, but it is typically uncommon to see a player miss back-to-back practices with rest being the reason why. So, some speculated that maybe he was quietly dealing with an injury, but Payton dismissed that and told reporters Sutton would be present at today’s practice. Well, today came and Sutton did indeed participate early on, but spent most of the day on the side field, which reignited the injury talk and even some potential trade talk from some online conspiracists. After practice, Payton once again dismissed the injury talk and continued saying it was based on their protocol. Then we heard from the man himself. Courtland Sutton met with the media and confirmed it’s about “load management”, even though they both don’t want to use that term, and it’s being done to keep Sutton fresh and healthy for an entire 17-game schedule and the playoffs. #Broncos WR Courtland Sutton makes clear: he is “indubitably” healthy. Says repeatedly he is trying to be a “good solider” with accepting team’s vet-rest plan, whether he likes it or not. pic.twitter.com/Lc4o6CCUr9 — Luca Evans (@bylucaevans) August 6, 2026 Sutton told reporters that he is “indubitably healthy” and being a “good soldier” with the Broncos’ rest plan for him, whether he likes it or not. When asked if he understands the benefits of these rest days, Sutton told the media that he is just being a good teammate and will do what’s best for the team. “I feel like ‘load management’ is like that basketball term. That’s what they talk about with basketball and everyone is like… I wouldn’t [call it] that, I think it’s just being a good teammate and being a good player in terms of player-coach relationship. I try to do the best that I possibly can to put myself in the best position. If they come to me and say that’s what they need from me, whether it’s… You guys have been around it for a long time. I’ve been able to talk to you guys for a long time and I love to work. Whenever I get the opportunity to, I do. If they come to me and say, ‘Hey look, based on what we’ve seen in terms of the numbers that you’ve put out on catapult, we need you to do this,’ I’ll say, ‘Alright, let’s do that.’ That’s what you guys ask of me and that’s what I’m going to do. I appreciate them being transparent with me in what they see because I don’t go in…

title: Troy Franklin feels more comfortable in third season with Broncos
summary: One of the most intriguing storylines unfolding at Denver Broncos training camp is the competition at wide receiver. Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton are slated to be the top tandem in the Broncos’ aerial attack this season. Yet the continued development of their young receiving corps will also be critical for the offense to ascend […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - NOVEMBER 16: Troy Franklin #11 of the Denver Broncos reacts after catching a pass during the third quarter against the Kansas City Chiefs at Empower Field at Mile High on November 16, 2025 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images One of the most intriguing storylines unfolding at Denver Broncos training camp is the competition at wide receiver. Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton are slated to be the top tandem in the Broncos’ aerial attack this season. Yet the continued development of their young receiving corps will also be critical for the offense to ascend to new heights in 2026. Entering his third season with the franchise, Troy Franklin is coming off the best season of his career. After a relatively quiet rookie campaign , Franklin took flight in 2025 and was the Broncos’ second leading receiver. He trailed only Sutton in target share and production. He finished his second season with 65 catches for 709 yards and 6 touchdowns. It’s unlikely that Franklin will see as much volume in year three compared to last year. Nevertheless, he figures to play an important role in Denver’s passing game. Yesterday, Head Coach Sean Payton took time to discuss Franklin’s progression to date and what he has improved upon since his rookie season in 2024. “His understanding of the formations, the details. Maybe in a different offense where he’s lining up outside right, now all of the sudden he’s getting used to the different roles that he’s playing and the alignments on the field,” stated Payton. “He has really good burst. That would be the one thing: he’s comfortable within the framework. It’s so much different than the system he had in college.” It usually takes several seasons for wide receivers coming out of the collegiate ranks to finally hit their stride as pros. Last season, we saw tremendous growth from the former Oregon standout. While there were some issues with drops and downfield tracking, he made a lot of big plays that helped Denver earn several key victories. After yesterday’s practice, Franklin noted he is better prepared this training camp compared to his first two years with the team. His knowledge of the offense is far more immense. Moreover, his chemistry with quarterback Bo Nix continues to get better each and every day. “I would say a lot. It’s my third year in it, so I’m comfortable. I don’t really have to think anymore, so I can just go and play,” stated Franklin. With Sutton and Waddle poised to earn the most looks in Denver’s passing endeavors, how the rest of the target share winds up being divided up remains a mystery. Franklin is competing alongside Marvin Mims Jr. and Pat Bryant for playing time during training camp. With no clear leader in the competition thus far, how Payton and Offensive Coordinator Davis Webb choose to attack opposing defenses on a weekly basis will be fascinating to watch. Their bevy of talented receivers has a lot of potential. If they can live up to it and be more consistent in ‘26 compared to ‘25, Denver certainly has the ability to be one of the best offenses in the NFL.

title: Eyioma Uwazurike hype hits fever pitch early on at Broncos training camp
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country. To win and play at a high level in the National Football League, you have to hold your own at the line of scrimmage. Over the past several seasons, the Denver Broncos have performed outstanding in the trenches. It’s a key reason why they are championship caliber team. The Broncos are […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 7: Eyioma Uwazurike #96 of the Denver Broncos stands on the sidelines during the nation anthem prior to an NFL football game against the Tennessee Titans at Empower Field at Mile High on September 7, 2025 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country. To win and play at a high level in the National Football League, you have to hold your own at the line of scrimmage. Over the past several seasons, the Denver Broncos have performed outstanding in the trenches. It’s a key reason why they are championship caliber team. The Broncos are set to return virtually every player on their offensive and defensive fronts with the exception of John Franklin-Myers. Those are some big shoes to fill, but thankfully, Zach Allen, D.J. Jones, and Malcolm Roach are the incumbent top three at the position. However, the competition for the next spot in the rotation is ramping up. Several players on rookie contracts are in a heated battle for increased playing time in 2026. Earlier in the offseason, some had pegged fourth-year defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike as a potential breakout player for the Broncos’ defense. While it’s still very early on in camp, Uwazurike is starting to make some noise. Yesterday, Head Coach Sean Payton spoke highly of his career arc and progression to date. “I’m proud of him because, you guys know this, in our sport, any sport really to just be out for a year can be difficult. He’s really come back, developed,” stated Paton. “He’s strong, he’s big and he’s having a real good start to camp. I think you have to look at it as one less year than what’s listed because of the year out. He’s doing really well.” Uwazurike played in eight games as a rookie before missing his entire second season due to violating league policy on gambling. After a relatively quiet year back in 2024, the former Iowa State standout earned a lot of playing time last year. He finished the 2025 season with a career high 39 tackles, 5 tackles for loss and 3.5 sacks. While Payton lauded his unteachable physical traits, veteran defensive tackle D.J. Jones spoke to what he has seen up close and personal as key reasons why Uwazurike performed well last year, and why he is ready to take his game to the next level in ‘26. “His hands and his eyes. This game is fast. It’s physical, which he has. But if you don’t have good eyes on the defensive line, then you’ll be lost. The leap he’s taking right now is pretty scary. He can play every position, very physical and his eyes are 10 out of 10 now,” remarked Jones. Replacing Franklin-Myers’ production won’t be easy, but if we can trust Payton and Jones, Uwazurike appears poised to be huge part of the Broncos’ defensive plans this season. title: Denver Broncos: Notes from the quotes — August 5th 2026
summary: Any time you listen to a player or a coach give an interview in the NFL, you have to not only listen to what they say, but also what they DON’T say. Along with head coach, Sean Payton, wide receiver, Troy Franklin, and interior defensive lineman, D.J. Jones, gave interviews. Sean Payton offers several important […]
full_text: CENTENNIAL , CO - JUNE 4: Troy Franklin (11) of the Denver Broncos stretches during OTAs at the Broncos Park in Centennial, Colorado on Thursday, June 4, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images Any time you listen to a player or a coach give an interview in the NFL, you have to not only listen to what they say, but also what they DON’T say. Along with head coach, Sean Payton, wide receiver, Troy Franklin, and interior defensive lineman, D.J. Jones, gave interviews. Sean Payton offers several important updates Injury updates are always a critical point of interest during questions with Sean Payton and Wednesday was not exception. Coach Payton mentioned that Drew Sanders is fully healthy, there were questions about whether he would be playing inside or outside and he said that Drew’s position “will sort itself out. It always does. That’s a lot better question than, ‘Who’s going to take the three reps?’ It’s an important position in this defense. Those edge positions, they’re hard to find. It’s a big reason why we’re staying with the positions these guys played a year ago. I think it’s one of the strong suits of our front.” So it would appear that Sanders will be mostly used at OLB in a crowded and highly talented group that includes Nik Bonitto, Jonathan Cooper, Jonah Elliss, Dondrea Tillman, and Que Robinson. With the lack of depth at ILB, and ability to play some snaps at ILB, which Elliss or Sanders could do, could be critical to making the 53-man roster. Additionally “the special teams stuff” will be critical. “Those guys are going to play a lot of snaps if they’re not playing snaps on defense. So all of that will factor in.” Que Robinson has been a pleasant surprise so far in camp and Sean Payton offered him some praise. Payton mentioned “he’s a real good technician, and he’s one of those guys that we know has been coached hard. We felt coming into this defense from what he was playing in, there were some similarities to what we were going to ask him to do.” The continued development of Que could make one of the other edge guys, like Cooper, a tradeable asset. Payton mentioned that Que is “competing for those reps in the line of scrimmage. I think it’s going really well, and again, we’ve had pads on for two days now.” The Broncos can never have too many good edge guys. Discussion of the WR room There were some interesting tidbits about the WR room offered yesterday both from Troy Franklin and Sean Payton. Payton offered high praise for the continued progress of Pat Bryant who he calls “one of those congested ball catchers.” The ability to go over the middle and catch the ball will be critical for the continued development of Bo Nix who did use the middle of the field very much last season. Having Jaylen Waddle who is “fine” as he just had some muscle tightness yesterday. Payton mentioned that Troy Franklin has made some progress during the offseason in terms of understanding the formations and the details of what is going on with the rest of the offense on a given play. “Now all of the sudden he’s getting used to the different roles that he’s playing and the alignments on the field. He’s comfortable within the framework. It’s so much different than the system he had in college.” A familiarity with the offense and with the Bo Nix can only help to improve the production from Troy Franklin who has “really good burst” according to Sean Payton. In Troy’s own words “I don’t really have to think anymore, so I can just go and play.” Coming down with more of his targets in 2026 will be critical for Troy. He was generally getting deep targets (ADOT, average depth of target, was 12.7 yards with was 27th highest in the NFL), but his catch rate of 53 percent leaves plenty of room for improvement. For comparison, Jaxson Smith-Njigba had an ADOT of 11.2 last season and a catch rate of 73 percent while Christian Watson had an ADOT of 17.8 and a catch rate of 64%. Lil’Jordan Humphrey also received praise from San Payton as one of the guys who does all of the little things to help the team win. He plays special teams at a high level, he blocks, and he doesn’t complain if he isn’t getting targetted, he is a big target, and he is extremely smart according to Sean Payton. He also mentioned that LJH has lost some weight relative to last season and he is moving better. “We do all the metrics and they wear the chips, but his weight’s down. His movement on the field, acceleration, top-end speed is higher last season and now than it was when he was here earlier.” Troy Franklin also sang the praises of new WR coach, Ronald Curry, who “has been great for us. I think he’s bringing a lot of new options on how we can get open. He’s taking a really good time in meeting rooms and making sure we know everything we need to do [with] our spots. Same thing with ‘Johnny Mo’ (Offensive Pass Game Coordinator John Morton), too. All those guys are helping us—[Offensive Quality Control Coach] Willie Snead [IV]. They’ve been a great addition for sure.” I’m excited about the WR room for this season. Marvin Mims will be playing for a free agent contract, which is usually when guys have career years. Pat Bryant, if he can stay healthy, is the possession guy that can thrive with all the attention Courtland Sutton and Jaylen Waddle will draw. Troy Franklin and LJH can both contribute in significant ways, so at least on paper, the Broncos have a really strong WR group. Discussion of the defense DJ Jones mentioned the progress that Eyioma Uwazurike has made during the past year. “His hands and his eyes. This game is fast. It’s physical, which he has. But if you don’t have good eyes on the [defensive] line, then you’ll be lost. The leap he’s taking right now is pretty scary. Like I said, he can play every position, very physical and his eyes are 10 out of 10 now.” Having EU as a dominant force on the DL, even if it is just in run-stuffing, will be critical since he is the largest IDL player that the Broncos have and much of the group relies more of quickness than mass. At the team roster site, he is listed as 320, which is the second heaviest player on the team. Only Tyler Miller, 6-9 335 lbs, is heavier. Sometimes on the DL, you just need that mass to stand up against double teams from the OL. Our next heaviest IDL guy is Jordan Miller at 307. DJ also mentioned how the return of almost every starting defender from last season will help the 2026 defense. While familiarity with the guys playing next to you and their abilities is not as critical as it is on the OL (since the OL plays every snap and the DL rotates), it is a plus for any defense.
author: Joe Mahoney

title: Detroit Lions give Jahmyr Gibbs record-breaking contract extension
summary: The hold-in is over. Just two days after Bijan Robinson became the highest-paid running back in NFL history, the Detroit Lions and Jahmyr Gibbs have agreed upon an extension that will one-up the three-year, $66.75 million deal Robinson got. The initial terms of the extension are a three-year $67.5 million deal that could be worth […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 27: Jahmyr Gibbs #0 of the Detroit Lions plays plays against the Green Bay Packers at Ford Field on November 27, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The hold-in is over. Just two days after Bijan Robinson became the highest-paid running back in NFL history, the Detroit Lions and Jahmyr Gibbs have agreed upon an extension that will one-up the three-year, $66.75 million deal Robinson got. The initial terms of the extension are a three-year $67.5 million deal that could be worth up to $75.75 million, including $51.5 million in guarantees . Be aware that initial numbers are often inflated. Regardless, this contract now makes Gibbs the highest-paid running back in NFL history. Gibbs was the Lions’ 12th overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft, and he’s the second player from that Lions draft class to already earn a second contract with the team. Earlier this offseason, Detroit handed linebacker Jack Campbell a four-year, $81 million deal to place him among the highest-paid linebackers. As for Gibbs, he has already become an essential part of this offense. In his three seasons thus far, he’s averaged 1,745 scrimmage yards per season, scored a total of 49 touchdowns, and averaged a whopping 5.3 yards per carry. Since entering the league in 2023, here’s where Gibbs ranks among his peers (min. 200 carries): 3,580 rushing yards — 7th 5,029 yards from scrimmage — 3rd 5.3 yards per carry — 2nd 39 rushing touchdowns — 2nd 49 total touchdowns — 1st It’s worth noting that Gibbs accomplished all of this while splitting the load with David Montgomery. But with Montgomery now with the Texans, the plan is to increase Gibbs’ workload, because they feel there’s nothing he can’t do. “He’s going to be our bell cow now,” coach Dan Campbell said in June. “He really became more of that last year, but we’re going to hang our hat on him quite a bit. We’re going to do a lot of things we feel like he does well. “Now, I’ve mentioned this before. He can run everything that we’ve got. He can run every scheme that anybody’s ever run. He’s not just an outside runner. He is not just a space runner. He can create his own space in the middle. And some of his biggest runs have been gap scheme right down the pipe, where he’s had patience, and found it, and guys blocked it up well. So, we’re going to ask a lot of him.” With Gibbs and Jack Campbell both now locked up, the attention shifts to two other players from that 2023 draft class: tight end Sam LaPorta and safety Brian Branch. Lions general manager Brad Holmes has already publicly expressed an interest in giving both players new contracts, although Dan Campbell did say that they may need to see Branch’s recovery from his torn Achilles before they opt to extend him. “I think you always want to know that your guys are healthy and this is truly healed,” Campbell said. “You are always going to kind of want to lean that way knowing the investment that would go into that.”

title: Lions training camp observations: Several reserves make most of promotions
summary: It was a pretty unique day at Allen Park for Day 7 of Detroit Lions training camp. Not only was it one of the longer practices of training camp—just short of 2.5 hours—but with the humidity seemingly around 130% and the sun bearing down, there were a lot of absences or early exits from players. […]
full_text: Aug 2, 2026; Allen Park, MI, USA; Detroit Lions quarterback Luke Altmyer (2) throws a pass during Detroit Lions training camp at Meijer Performance Center. Mandatory Credit: Paul Barnick-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It was a pretty unique day at Allen Park for Day 7 of Detroit Lions training camp. Not only was it one of the longer practices of training camp—just short of 2.5 hours—but with the humidity seemingly around 130% and the sun bearing down, there were a lot of absences or early exits from players. So much so that the Lions pushed an injury alert to media that several of those absences were cramping/heat related. [Note: see the full injury report for Thursday here ] The Lions responded with heavy rotations and low pitch counts from a lot of their starting lineup. As a result, a bunch of reserves had big opportunities, and several ran with it. Let’s break it all down in our Day 7 observations. Several promotions in midst of injuries/absences Luke Atlmyer shows good command as QB2 With Teddy Bridgewater sidelined, Luke Altmyer essentially got double his normal reps, quarterbacking the second and third-team offenses. I continue to be impressed with his arm speed and accuracy. Twice on Thursday, he was able to fire the ball between two defensive backs in a zone, and I don’t think he’s thrown more than one or two interceptions all camp. Beyond that, he’s also got way more poise than I would expect from an undrafted rookie. While sometimes his progressions are taking significant time, I’ve already seen improvement in that category. And when running a two-minute drill toward the end of practice, he showed impressive command—leading to a win* (more on that later) for the offense. Running back reserves continue strong camp With no Jahmyr Gibbs, Isiah Pacheco, or Sione Vaki involved in team drill, Jacob Saylors and Jabari Small even shared first-team reps at running back. Saylors continues to impress with his speed and one-cut style of running. Meanwhile, I thought Small ran with impressive strength, particularly between the tackles during red zone drills. Admittedly, they both benefitted from strong run blocking today (though it was Tate Ratledge’s best day of camp). Skyler Gill-Howard, Ahmed Hassanein make most of early reps With very limited roles for Tyler Lacy and Mekhi Wingo on Thursday, Ahmed Hassanein and Skyler Gill-Howard both got some significant work with the first team. It was yet another impressive day for Hassanein, as he continues to live up to the fan hype. With the twos, I had him down for two tackles for loss and two sacks. The second sack came during the final situational drill, where he stunted with Gill-Howard, then he completely okey-doked Mason Miller for a free run at Altmyer. Hassanein was a bit out of control, though, and actually bumped into the rookie quarterback—a no-no in camp. While most of his production came against the second team, he did get a big win during one-on-ones against Blake Miller, beating him with a speed move around the edge. Gill-Howard was pretty disruptive in team drills, notching at least one pass breakup and sack, but it’s worth noting he did struggle during one-on-ons, going 0-for-3 in the three matchups I saw. Devin White, Trevor Nowaske get call-up to first-teamers Nowaske got a ton of first-team work with Barnes pretty severely limited on the day. It’s worth noting Barnes looked a little shook up during Tuesday’s practice and told media it was just a minor knee injury that he finished practice with. It was a quiet day for Nowaske, but he’ll certainly benefit from the first-team reps. White, on the other hand, got a ton of work in replacing Malcolm Rodriguez as the WILL linebacker in three-linebacker sets, and made a few plays throughout the day. He tallied a beautiful pass breakup on Kye Robichaux during 7-on-7s, and played with good anticipation in the run game. Nick Whiteside’s early camp gets rewarded With no D.J. Reed on the day, Whiteside got a ton of work opposite Rock Ya-Sin with the first team defense. Detroit was in nickel for a large portion of the day, and I would say the majority of those first-team reps went to Ennis Rakestraw. Although Rakestraw did get some outside work in replacement of Whiteside, with Christian Izien sliding into first-team nickel, as well. Whiteside’s day wasn’t as flashy as previous camp appearances. Isaac TeSlaa got the better of him in on-one-ones in both of their matchups, but the promotion still shows Detroit has appreciated the work he’s put in. Flags flying everywhere Officials were on hand for the first time in training camp, and they were busy on Thursday. As expected, the flags were flying during the WR/DB one-on-ones. Keith Abney was the guilty party on each of his first two reps (vs. Tom Kennedy and Tarik Black). But the flags continued all day. The offense was guilty of a few false starts, one offsides, and at least two illegal formations. Meanwhile, the defense got tagged with an illegal contact, a defensive holding, and at least one offsides penalty during team drills. It’s not all that uncommon for things to be this sloppy early in camp, but I’m guessing the coaching staff won’t be very happy with the high number of procedural mistakes. Isaac TeSlaa redemption I mentioned it earlier, but it’s worth breaking down TeSlaa’s day, particularly during one-on-ones. A few days after going 0-for-4 during these drills, he won both of his matchups on Thursday, both against Whiteside. On the first, he used his size to high-point a back-shoulder throw on the sidelines. The second, he cleanly won on a comeback route for a modest gain. Now, I’d like to see him do those against the likes for Reed and Ya-Sin—two extremely physical cornerbacks who have given him a hard time to date—but it was still a nice confidence boost for the second-year receiver. Situational end… with just the second-teamers The Lions ran an interesting situational drill, but only used the second-team offense and defense to end practice. The scenario: down 14-13, 3:32 left, 2 timeouts for both teams, starting on own 8-yard line The second-team offense really struggled out of the gate. After Greg Dortch (6 yards) and Cedrick Wilson (5 yards) picked up short gains to move the chains, the offense completely stuttered. Two penalties (false start on Miles Frazier and illegal formation) set them back, and the aforementioned Hassanein sack ended the drive quickly. But Detroit ended up just re-setting the ball with a fresh set of downs, and the offense quickly found life. A great turkey-hole shot to tight end Thomas Gordon plus a medium gain to Tom Kennedy quickly put them in field goal range, and Bates drilled a 41-yard field goal as time expired. Miscellaneous notes: I thought this was Jackson Meeks’ best day of camp. He sealed a few rushing lanes on the day, and his biggest highlight was a red-zone catch in which he delivered a vicious stiff-arm to Khalil Dorsey to turn a 5-yard curl into a 15-yard gain. Jake Bates had a pretty typical day. Makes: 38, 39, 41, 43, 44, 49 Misses: 39, 48 Just because he doesn’t get mentioned much, I thought Jared Goff was lethal today, espeically during 1-on-1s. He dropped a few deep shots into tiny windows. Despite eating the aforementioned stiff-arm, it was a good day for Khalil Dorsey, mostly working with the twos. He tallied a pass breakup on Tom Kennedy, an interception during 1-on-1s (vs. Wilson), and he was dominant on both the gunner and jammer drills on special teams. Jameson Williams had the catch of practice on a red zone fade pass from Goff. Williams high pointed the ball and battled through contract from Ya-Sin for the score.

title: Detroit Lions training camp injury report: Gibbs, Conklin back
summary: After a day off, the Detroit Lions were back on the field Thursday for Day 7 of training camp. It was a very hot and balmy day at Allen Park, and it forced a lot of players to either be limited or miss practice entirely. The Lions even offered the following update regarding players after […]
full_text: ALLEN PARK, MICHIGAN - JUNE 17: Jahmyr Gibbs #0 of the Detroit Lions works out at mandatory minicamp at Detroit Lions Meijer Performance Center on June 17, 2026 in Allen Park, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images After a day off, the Detroit Lions were back on the field Thursday for Day 7 of training camp. It was a very hot and balmy day at Allen Park, and it forced a lot of players to either be limited or miss practice entirely. The Lions even offered the following update regarding players after practice: “Several player absences/limited time related to the heat/cramping etc. Won’t have official updates on those.” So as you see some of the unexpected absences, early departures or limited playing times of the players below, keep in mind some of them may not be injury related. Return to practice: RB Jahmyr Gibbs (hold-in, back) TE Tyler Conklin (calf) G Ben Bartch (undisclosed) Gibbs was back on the field with a helmet, going through walkthroughs with his teammates for the first time. But when the team broke for positional and team drills, he split from the group and worked with a trainer. He stayed on the field for the entire practice, but did no team work after walkthroughs. Conklin officially came off the PUP list and did some walkthrough and individual drills on Thursday. He was not cleared for team drills yet, though. That left Jackson Meeks and Thomas Gordon to get most of the TE3-4 reps for the day. After solely working with trainers for the past couple of days, Bartch was back on individual drills, but he has still yet to participate in any team drills this training camp. For someone expected to contend for the starting left guard job, he needs to get out there soon. Out, but working with trainers: S Brian Branch (PUP, Achilles) Branch spent a significant amount of time working with a trainer on Thursday. I would estimate he did about an hour of work, up from about the 15 minutes he did earlier in the week. He stayed on the field all day and hung out with his teammates, but he remains on PUP, with the last estimate on his return being late August, early September. Appeared to be limited: LB Derrick Barnes (undisclosed) Barnes appeared to be on a bit of a pitch count on Thursday, leaving Trevor Nowaske to get the majority of the first-team SAM linebacker reps when Detroit was in base defense. Not practicing: QB Teddy Bridgewater (undisclosed) RB Isiah Pacheco (undisclosed) RB Sione Vaki (eye, broken nose) OT Giovanni Manu (NFI) G Juice Scruggs (undisclosed) EDGE Derrick Moore (groin) EDGE Payton Turner (back) LB Malcolm Rodriguez (ankle) LB Jimmy Rolder (leg) CB D.J. Reed (undisclosed) S Kerby Joseph (PUP, knee) Bridgewater was nowhere to be seen on Thursday, leaving undrafted rookie quarterback Luke Atlmyer to take all of the second and third-team reps. He got a ton of work in Thursday, which is obviously good for his development. He did not look out of place, either. Some reporters believe they saw Pacheco during warmups (I hadn’t started attendance yet), but he was not present for the rest of practice. With Pacheco, Vaki, and Gibbs not participating in team drills, the first-team reps were split pretty evenly between Jacob Saylors and Jabari Small. No word on why Juice Scruggs was out. But with him out and Bartch still limited, Christian Mahogany took all of the starting left guard reps that I saw. Michael Niese stepped in for Scruggs as the backup center, as well. With Reed out for undisclosed reasons, it was primarily Rock Ya-Sin and Nick Whiteside as the starting cornerbacks, with a heavy day of nickel reps for Ennis Rakestraw. Left practice early EDGE Tyler Lacy (undisclosed) DT Mekhi Wingo (groin) CB De’Shawn Rucker (ankle) We did not get an update on Lacy, suggesting his early exit was heat related. In his place as the starting big end, Detroit utilized both Ahmed Hassanein and some Levi Onwuzurike with the ones. But with a lot of nickel looks on Thursday, DJ Wonnum got a significant workload opposite Aidan Hutchinson. With Wingo out, rookie Skyler Gill-Howard got the bump up at three-tech, playing with both the first and second-team defenses. Onwuzurike also took some of those reps. Rucker appeared to suffer an injury during 7-on-7 red zone drills.

title: Jahmyr Gibbs returns to practice; contract extension could ‘get done this week’
summary: Detroit Lions superstar Jahmyr Gibbs has returned to training camp practices, according to Pride of Detroit’s Jeremy Reisman. Gibbs reported for Lions training camp last week, and while he has been participating in meetings and with his teammates, he had yet to practice while he waits for a new deal to arrive. On Thursday, he […]
full_text: Sep 14, 2025; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs (0) looks on during warmups prior to the game against the Chicago Bears at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Detroit Lions superstar Jahmyr Gibbs has returned to training camp practices, according to Pride of Detroit’s Jeremy Reisman. Gibbs reported for Lions training camp last week, and while he has been participating in meetings and with his teammates, he had yet to practice while he waits for a new deal to arrive. On Thursday, he was in full uniform and participated in warm-ups, but when the team shifted to individual drills, he stepped off to the side to work with a trainer, suggesting he is going through an acclimation process. Gibbs is not going through individual drills with the team. Currently working to the side with a trainer. — Jeremy Reisman (@DetroitOnLion) August 6, 2026 This return to the field for Gibbs is another optimistic sign that he could be nearing a contract extension with the Lions, which lines up with a recent report from The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones. Before Thursday’s practice, Jones expressed optimism surrounding a new deal, based on conversations with sources, and reported that a deal could “get done this week for Gibbs.” Gibbs has not formally met with the media in camp, and while reporters—Pride of Detroit included—have attempted to ask him about his situation, he’s kept things very close to the vest. When asked when he plans to rejoin his teammates on the practice field, he simply responded: “Time will tell.” On Tuesday, coach Dan Campbell was asked how other NFL running backs getting extensions could help facilitate the process of getting a deal done with Gibbs; he noted how it could help and that he was excited to get the star running back on the field. “I think it certainly’s not going to hurt,” Campbell said. “It’s not going to hurt, but we’ll see. I’m anxious to get Gibbs back out there. Every day that goes by, that’s another day that you feel like you miss with him and getting him out there with the guys and him doing his part. But, there again, it’ll get done when it gets done.” On Wednesday, general manager Brad Holmes was also asked for his thoughts on the situation by SiriusXM radio hosts Pat Kirwan and Jacob Hester, and Holmes noted that the two sides remain in communication. “Look, obviously we love Jahmyr,” Holmes said. “Me and Dan (Campbell) have always been believers in that one-two punch. I just think that’s how this league is going now. But, you know, we’re having dialogue. We’ll see where it goes.“ Will continue to update this situation as it progresses.

title: Discussion: What’s the proper concern level for Jahmyr Gibbs’ hold-in?
summary: Jahmyr Gibbs’ hold-in for a new contract officially enters Week 2 on Thursday, as the Detroit Lions will participate in their seventh training camp practice this offseason. Thus far, there have been no tangible signs of progress between the Lions and Gibbs, but there haven’t been any reports of stagnation or sticking points with negotiations, […]
full_text: Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs (0) on field after practice during training camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Monday, August 3, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Jahmyr Gibbs’ hold-in for a new contract officially enters Week 2 on Thursday, as the Detroit Lions will participate in their seventh training camp practice this offseason. Thus far, there have been no tangible signs of progress between the Lions and Gibbs, but there haven’t been any reports of stagnation or sticking points with negotiations, either. Really, all the evidence we have about negotiations are the scant details we’re getting from the team itself. Both Lions coach Dan Campbell and general manager Brad Holmes have expressed public interest in getting a deal done, and on Wednesday, Holmes said they are engaged in talks. So this isn’t a situation in which the Lions are refusing to pay Gibbs or closed to any talks. However, there have been a few signs that are relatively discouraging. A week ago, Campbell said he “wasn’t sweating” Gibbs’ hold-in, but he also admitted he was surprised the contract hasn’t been finalized yet. “I thought we’d have been done by now,” Campbell said. On Wednesday, Holmes told SiriusXM they’re “having dialogue” with Gibbs , but his body language did not scream optimistic, and when reassured by the radio host that it’ll get done, his response was an uninspiring “that’s the hope.” So today’s Question of the Day is: What’s your concern level regarding Jahmyr Gibbs’ hold-in? My answer: I’m still pretty low. Let’s call it a 2/10 total. Admittedly, we’re entering uncharted territory with the Lions. Any time they’ve publicly expressed an interest in extending a player, they’ve been able to do so in a very timely manner. So, on the surface, it’s a bit concerning that’s not how negotiations are going this time around. Additionally, I figured as soon as Bijan Robinson signed his three-year extension with the Atlanta Falcons, that Gibbs’ deal would come about almost immediately. It’s been around 48 hours since, and all has been quiet. That all being said, I’m still not that concerned. We’re still very early in training camp, and while I’d certainly like Gibbs to be out there in a new offense with a new offensive line, there is more than enough time for him to enter the picture and be ready by Week 1. I trust that Gibbs’ appearance at practices is a sign of good faith and no ill-will, and I do expect the Robinson deal to move things along relatively quickly. And with Campbell’s mostly-optimistic comments on the situation, I’m assuming things will be just fine. Simply put, if Campbell isn’t sweating it, there’s no reason I should be. That said, if we’re beyond the first preseason game and Gibbs is still sidelined, that’s when the worry starts to creep up into the 4-6 range, and if we’re nearing the end of preseason, that’s when I’d jump to a 8-10. But, for now, it’s early. It’s okay to be patient here. What is your concern level for the Jahmyr Gibbs contract negotiations? full_text: ASHWAUBENON, WISCONSIN - JULY 31: MarShawn Lloyd #32 of the Green Bay Packers works out during the Green Bay Packers training camp at Ray Nitschke Field on July 31, 2026 in Ashwaubenon, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Thursday, the Green Bay Packers had their final practice leading up to Friday’s Family Night practice at Lambeau Field. It was closed to the public, but the media were able to attend the practice. Want some good news? There was confirmation today that the Packers will be streaming Family Night on Packers.com for a second straight year, which means that even out-of-market fans will be able to get a look at the team with their own eyes before the preseason starts. If you want an extended look at the starting offense and defense, this is probably going to be your best shot, considering how conservative the Packers have been with their starters in preseasons past. For perspective, starting running back Josh Jacobs got all of two snaps in the 2025 preseason. Be sure to join us during the Family Night practice tomorrow, as we’ll have a watch thread where we’ll be discussing what’s going on the field. Here’s what happened in practice today. Injuries There have been no changes to the Packers’ reserve/injured lists, as running back Chris Brooks (hamstring) remains on the non-football injury list (he was hurt outside of the facility) and tight end Luke Musgrave (neck), defensive lineman Javon Hargrave (knee), defensive lineman Jordon Riley (Achilles), edge rusher Micah Parsons (knee) and long snapper Matt Orzech (calf) are still on the physically unable to perform list. The Packers described Orzech’s and Hargrave’s injuries as short-term injuries in the past, and head coach Matt LaFleur stated today that he’s hoping that Brooks returns to the field “sooner rather than later,” a sign that it’s not a major injury. Musgrave’s neck appears to be the only major injury that Green Bay’s roster has suffered outside of the holdover recoveries from 2025 (Micah Parsons and Jordon Riley). Running back Josh Jacobs (groin) and cornerback Carrington Valentine (hamstring) both missed practice on Thursday with what were described as short-term injuries. The only other DNP on Thursday was safety/slot defender Johnathan Baldwin, who is dealing with a knee issue. So far, we have no info on how serious Baldwin’s injury is. For what it’s worth, Baldwin was the team’s backup slot defender in camp thus far, despite the fact that the third-string role (behind Javon Bullard and cap casualty Nate Hobbs) was filled by Kitan Oladapo in 2025. Offense Love high for Golden on first play with the ones. Starters: Love Lloyd Dabney – Whyle Golden – Watson Morgan – Burton – Rhyan – Monk – Belton Sorrell – Brooks – McClellan – Brinson – LVN Zaire – Coop Cisse – Nixon Williams – X — Andy Herman (@AndyHermanNFL) August 6, 2026 With Aaron Banks and Zach Bako-Bewele still out of the lineup in team drills, the Packers have used injury replacement starters at left guard and right tackle throughout camp. Generally, those reps usually go to Jacob Monk (left guard) and Darian Kinnard (right tackle), but today there was a heavy dose of Anthony Belton (who usually plays right guard) at right tackle. That opened up another spot at guard on the line, which rookie Jager Burton stepped into. Donovan Jennings also got some reps at guard with the first-team offense today, too. If you’re trying to keep tabs on a 53-man roster projection right now, I’d say that the sixth through ninth offensive linemen right now are likely Kinnard, Monk, Burton and Jennings, in some order. The Packers will likely keep 10 offensive linemen (and they roster 11 more times than they roster 9). That leaves one spot up for grabs, depending on how entrenched Jennings is right now. John Williams having to move from snapping sign twos to immediately playing left tackle with threes is one of the more impressive things I’ve seen from an O-lineman on the reserve units — weston hodkiewicz (@WesHod) August 6, 2026 One option for the final offensive lineman on the 53-man roster is second-year draft pick John Williams, who missed his entire rookie season with a back injury. Right now, Williams is playing every position on the offensive line. Here’s the thing: If that’s the Packers’ backup line, the only “true tackle” beyond the starters is Kinnard, as Monk, Burton, Jennings and Williams are primarily interior offensive linemen. That is likely one reason why Belton is getting some reps at tackle right now while Bako-Bewele is out. If the group ever faced two injuries at the tackle position (any combo of two of Jordan Morgan, Bako-Bewele and Kinnard), Belton is probably the next man up at the position. No idea if he stays healthy, but MarShawn Lloyd is very, very fast. — Ryan Wood (@ByRyanWood) August 6, 2026 MarShawn Lloyd just did a backflip after catching a TD wide open during 11-on-11. — Matt Schneidman (@mattschneidman) August 6, 2026 There’s some momentum building for running back MarShawn Lloyd, who has dealt with a series of injuries going into Year 3 of his NFL career. Lloyd, who has only played 10 regular-season snaps after being taken in the third round, made several plays in camp today and got the majority of the snaps with the starting offense while Jacobs was sidelined. At the moment, Lloyd projects to be the Packers’ number two ball-carrier in 2026, only behind Jacobs. Defense Mama there goes that man. Anthony Campbell with a would be sack on Tyrod Taylor. — Andy Herman (@AndyHermanNFL) August 6, 2026 Defensive lineman Anthony Campbell continues to make plays. While Hargrave and Devonte Wyatt (practicing but not in team drills) have been sidelined, Campbell has been pushed into working with the second-team defense. He’s recorded several pass breakups in camp and has “sacked” quarterback Tyrod Taylor several times. Keep an eye out for Campbell on Family Night and in the preseason, as he has a chance to push Nazir Stackhouse for the sixth (and likely last) roster spot on the defensive line. At the moment, Hargrave, Wyatt, rookie third-round pick Chris McClellan, second-year draft pick Warren Brinson and Karl Brooks are considered roster locks. Javon Bullard took out Josh Whyle low on a swing pass. Adam Stenavich was *not* happy. After the period, Bullard came to the offense’s sideline and apologized to Whyle. — Matt Schneidman (@mattschneidman) August 6, 2026 It was a little chippy today, as Bullard popped tight end Josh Whyle pretty good in practice. Green Bay is already very thin at the tight end position, so it’s understandable why the offense would be mad that Bullard didn’t protect his teammate. Still, Bullard apologized and didn’t let it escalate further. So far, no fights in camp. Special Teams Kick returners: Melton Moore Sturdivant Strong Sheppard Nixon Savion is not with the returners and scanning the field multiple times I don’t currently see him out practicing. Will keep you posted. — Andy Herman (@AndyHermanNFL) August 6, 2026 General manager Brian Gutekunst had big praise for receiver/returner Skyy Moore on Thursday in his pre-practice press conference, stating that he “expects” Moore to help the team in 2026. Adjust your 53-man roster projections accordingly. In practice today, the team worked on kick returns in their special teams period. The returners were receivers Bo Melton, J. Michael Sturdivant, Will Sheppard and Moore and running backs Pierre Strong Jr. and Jaden Nixon. Savion Williams was not involved in that period, as he was getting checked by the medical staff, but later returned to practice. Williams was the Packers’ preferred kick returner in the regular season last year, though Jacobs and cornerback Keisean Nixon handled those duties in the postseason. For what it’s worth, Jacobs and Nixon generally worked on kickoff returns in camp, even if they didn’t do it in the regular season last year. Don’t expect the team to flip the switch and send those two…

title: Green Bay Packers news: Brandon Cisse making the most of early opportunities in camp
summary: I think it’s pretty obvious that the Packers drafted Brandon Cisse expecting him to compete for playing time sooner rather than later. And just a couple of weeks into training camp, he’s already getting that chance. Carrington Valentine has been sidelined with a hamstring injury, forcing Green Bay to shuffle its cornerback rotation and creating […]
full_text: Green Bay Packers cornerback Brandon Cisse (2) is shown at training camp Friday, July 31, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co I think it’s pretty obvious that the Packers drafted Brandon Cisse expecting him to compete for playing time sooner rather than later. And just a couple of weeks into training camp, he’s already getting that chance. Carrington Valentine has been sidelined with a hamstring injury, forcing Green Bay to shuffle its cornerback rotation and creating additional first-team reps for Cisse. The second-round rookie hasn’t looked out of place. SI’s Bill Huber reports that Cisse has been one of Green Bay’s more encouraging first-year performers, highlighting a steady climb up the depth chart throughout camp. He hasn’t simply flashed athletic traits, he’s been around the football and continued to earn opportunities with the starters. Our own Justis Mosqueda also noted Cisse as getting plenty of looks with the ones. Camp stories don’t always translate to the regular season, but the truth is the Packers have questions at cornerback. Keisean Nixon remains locked in as a veteran leader, but several jobs behind him are up in the air. If Cisse keeps stacking success, it may not be long before Green Bay trusts him with meaningful game snaps. To be clear, cornerback is one of the NFL’s toughest positions, and consistency usually comes with experience. TL;DR: there will be growing pains. But so far, Cisse seems to be doing exactly what the Packers hoped for through the opening stretch of camp. Packers rookie report: update on all 17 and who’s rising (and falling) on depth chart With six draft picks and 11 undrafted free agents, the Packers have 17 rookies on their roster. Here is where they stand after one week of training camp. title: Jordan Love, Josh Jacobs poised to make big moves on Packers all-time leaderboards
summary: If all goes well, the Packers’ offense should put up some big numbers this year. That will, of course, mean good things for the team as a whole, but it also will mean significant leaps up the all-time statistical leaderboards for a few notable names on the Packers. Here’s how the Packers could rewrite the […]
full_text: Jordan Love, number 10 of the Green Bay Packers, throws a football during training camp at Ray Nitschke Field in Ashwaubenon, Wisconsin, on August 2, 2026. (Photo by Ross Harried/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images If all goes well, the Packers’ offense should put up some big numbers this year. That will, of course, mean good things for the team as a whole, but it also will mean significant leaps up the all-time statistical leaderboards for a few notable names on the Packers. Here’s how the Packers could rewrite the record books in 2026. Passing stats Jordan Love stands to make the most meaningful mark on the Packers’ record books this year. He’s currently tied with Tobin Rote for fifth all time in passing yards with 11,535. It will take him multiple seasons to catch Lynn Dickey for fourth all time, but he’ll overtake Rote with his first completion of 2026. Let’s go ahead and knock that out on the first play of the first game. With 83 passing touchdowns to his name, Love needs just seven touchdowns to pass Rote (89) for fifth all time in passing touchdowns. If he threw 51, he’d leap past Dickey for the fourth spot. That’s not impossible, but it’d take some doing — he’d only have to throw more touchdowns than any Packers player has ever thrown in a season to make it happen. A guy can dream! Rushing stats Josh Jacobs ranks 18th in Packers history with 2,258 rushing yards. The first name on his overtake list is A.J. Dillon; Jacobs needs just 171 yards to pass the former Packers’ second round pick. How high can Jacobs climb? 1,000 yards would get him past Donny Anderson for 14th all-time, and that’s probably about the upper limit. He’d need more than 1,500 yards to jump Paul Hornung (3,711) and get into the top 10, and Aaron Rodgers currently sits at 11th with 3,466. Both are probably safe this year. However, he can make some serious noise on the all-time rushing touchdowns list. His 28 touchdowns already have him tied with Dorsey Levens and Elijah Pitts for 11th, and two scores puts him past John Brockington and Tobin Rote (29 apiece) for sole possession of ninth place. And Jacobs only climbs from there. Eight touchdowns gets him past Ted Fritsch (31), Aaron Rodgers (35), and Clark Hinkle (35) for sixth all-time, and if he can get to 10 rushing touchdowns this year, he’ll pass the great Verne Lewellen for fifth all-time. More on Jacobs and his scoring abilities later. Receiving stats Christian Watson enters 2026 as the Packers’ active leader in receiving yards, ranking 30th all time. If he notches his first 1,000 yard season, he’d pass a whole host of notable names in Packers history, including Bubba Franks, Ed West, William Henderson, Romeo Doubs, Javon Walker, Ahman Green, Jermichael Finley, and Bill Schroeder, who’s currently in possession of 18th place all time with 3,435 receiving yards. I want to call out Watson’s relationship to Doubs (at least statistically) here. Watson needs 70 catches to pass Doubs’ career total of 202 in Green Bay, but just 161 yards to surpass Doubs’ 2.424. It just goes to show the difference in what the two players offer. As a bonus, Watson’s 20 receiving touchdowns currently have him tied with Bill Schroeder and Jermichael Finley for 20th in Packers history. Three touchdowns this season not only breaks that tie, but puts him past Romeo Doubs (21), Gary Knafelc (21), and Javon Walker (22) for 20th in Packers history. Nine touchdowns has him leaping Johnny Blood (28) for 18th on the big board. Elsewhere in the world of pass catching, Tucker Kraft’s 15 touchdowns has him tied with Jayden Reed and Ron Kramer for 33rd all time. Just three more scores has him leaping notable tight ends Kramer (15), Robert Tonyan (17), Donald Lee (17), and Mark Chmura (17). Six could get him past Jermichael Finley’s career total of 20. Speaking of Finley, it’s possible that Kraft could pass Finley on both the career yardage and touchdowns leaderboards this year. He’d need a bit more than 1,200 yards to do it, but he was on pace for 1,139 last year and I’d never put it past Kraft to smash through anything. He probably won’t catch Finley’s reception total of 223 this season (he’d need 111 to do it), but again…why bet against Tucker Kraft? Sooner or later, he’s going to be the Packer’s most statistically productive tight end of all time. Why not sooner? To cap off the receiving section, Matthew Golden ranks 144th in Packers’ history with just 361 receiving yards. If he manages just 500 this year, he’ll climb all the way to 82nd. Progress! Scoring stats Scoring is much less of an important metric now than it was in earlier NFL history, but the Packers have had some notable scorers during their more than century of history, so it bears mentioning. Trey Smack is off to a shaky start so far, but he’ll make something resembling history if he makes it into the regular season. If he converts just one kick, he’ll become just the 43rd in recorded Packers history to do so, or at least history as recorded by Pro Football Reference. Two made field goals makes him a top-35 kicker in Packers history. See? The bar is low! (Please improve, Trey.) Up toward the top of the leaderboard, Josh Jacobs’ 180 career points are pretty solid for two seasons, but put him in a tie for 42nd in Packers history. However, he doesn’t need to do that much to pass some notable names. He realistically won’t get anywhere near the top 10 (Jordy Nelson is 10th with 416 points, so good luck), but he’s within striking distance of Tony Canadeo (186), Aaron Rodgers (216), and Johnny Blood (224). And if you’re scoring more than Johnny Blood? Well, that’s saying something.

summary: One of the Houston Texans’ most underappreciated defensive contributors is staying put. NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reported Thursday morning that linebacker Henry To’oTo’o has agreed to a two-year, $16 million contract extension, keeping him in Houston through the 2028 season. The deal includes a $1M incentive option based on performance. The former fifth-round pick was […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TX - JANUARY 04: Linebacker Henry To'oto'o #39 of the Houston Texans runs through smoke as he is announced as a defensive starter before the NFL game between Houston Texans and Indianapolis Colts on January 4, 2026, at NRG Stadium in Houston, TX. (Photo by David Buono/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images One of the Houston Texans’ most underappreciated defensive contributors is staying put. NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reported Thursday morning that linebacker Henry To’oTo’o has agreed to a two-year, $16 million contract extension, keeping him in Houston through the 2028 season. The deal includes a $1M incentive option based on performance. From Inside Training Camp on @nflnetwork : #Texans LB Henry To’oTo’o gets a two-year, $16 million contract extension while I practice my glottal stop to make my @gmfb colleague Manti Te’o proud. pic.twitter.com/zDqVauTJkS — Mike Garafolo (@MikeGarafolo) August 6, 2026 The former fifth-round pick was an afterthought on the roster when he was initially drafted in 2023. Stuck behind veterans, To’oTo’o slowly worked his way up the depth chart and earned a starting role the past two seasons. He posted 200 tackles and four sacks over the past two seasons. While he does receive criticism for his coverage woes, he has been extremely reliable against the run and a sure tackler in open space. The short deal keeps To’oTo’o in Houston through 2028. This contract is fairly team-friendly and maintains continuity in a linebacker room quickly overrun with injuries. For context, this deal makes him the 30th highest-paid linebacker in the NFL. A great deal for the Texans given his production and health. Compare that to Azeez Al-Shaair’s contract that’s fourth highest in the league and pays him $44.6M over the next two seasons. With the new deal, General Manager Nick Caserio has inked the entire starting defense through the 2027 season. That is an incredible financial feat given the quantity of elite talent on the roster. The only notable free agent on defense will be DT Tommy Togiai.
