title: Patriots 2026 scouting report for TE Hunter Henry
summary: The New England Patriots’ 2021 free agency class was one for the ages, but five years later only one of the high-profile signings remains with the team. And for good reason: Hunter Henry has been a model citizen since coming to Foxborough (and before that as well), and will go down as one of the […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - JANUARY 25: Hunter Henry #85 of the New England Patriots celebrates a touchdown during the AFC Championship Playoff game between the New England Patriots and the Denver Broncos at Empower Field At Mile High on January 25, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Kara Durrette/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New England Patriots’ 2021 free agency class was one for the ages, but five years later only one of the high-profile signings remains with the team. And for good reason: Hunter Henry has been a model citizen since coming to Foxborough (and before that as well), and will go down as one of the better tight ends in franchise history. Heading into his sixth season with the Patriots, there is nothing to suggest that he won’t again be an imporant piece of the club’s offensive puzzle. Hard facts Name: Hunter Henry Position: Tight end Jersey number: 85 Opening day age: 31 (12/7/1994) Measurements : 6’4 7/8”, 249 lbs, 9 1/4” hand size, 32 3/4” arm length, 78” wingspan, 4.68s 40-yard dash, 7.16s 3-cone drill, 4.41 short shuttle, 31 1/2” vertical jump, 9’5” broad jump, 13 bench press reps, 6.28 Relative Athletic Score Experience NFL: San Diego/Los Angeles Chargers (2016-20), New England Patriots (2021-) | College: Arkansas (2013-15) Henry drew considerable interest as a four-star college recruit out of Pulaski Academy in Little Rock, AR, but he decided to stay in his home state and joined the University of Arkansas in 2013. He was named All-SEC in all three of his seasons as a Razorback (first team 2014, 2015; second team 2013) and also was named an unanimous All-American as well as the winner of the. John Mackey Award as the nation’s top tight end in 2015. After catching a combined 116 passes for 1,661 yards and nine touchdowns his first three seasons, Henry decided to forgo his final year of eligibility to enter the NFL. He was a highly-regarded prospect and ended up as the first tight end off the board: the Chargers brought him to San Diego as the 35th overall selection in 2016. Henry made an impact on the Chargers offense from his rookie season on, and together with veteran Antonio Gates formed one of the league’s better tight end duos during his first two seasons with the organization. While a torn ACL limited him to just one game in 2018 — a divisional playoff loss to the eventual Super Bowl champion Patriots — he still managed to appear in 56 games with 50 starts during his five-year career in San Diego and Los Angeles. After receiving the franchise tag in 2020, however, he left the organization the following spring: the Patriots signed him to a three-year, $37.5 million free agency pact, and he quickly picked up where he left off. Setting a new career high in touchdowns (9), he was one of quarterback Mac Jones’ favorite targets and therefore instrumental to New England qualifying for the postseason. The next few years were more challenging from a team success perspective, but Henry nonetheless was one of the top performers and most reliable players on New England’s roster — a status that did not change with the arrivals of new starting QB Drake Maye in 2024 and head coach Mike Vrabel in 2025. As a consequence, Henry has now played 86 games with 72 starts for the club and been on the receiving end of 269 total passes for 3,115 yards and 27 touchdowns. Scouting report Strengths: Standing at 6-foot-5, 249 pounds, Henry has the size and length NFL teams are looking for in an inline/Y-tight end. He uses his size and naturally soft hands to haul in passes at a high rate and make receptions outside of his frame or in a contested manner. He readjusts his body well in the air, and has a good feel for not committing too early to incoming plays. In general, his football IQ is immense and he is able to find soft spots in zone defense or maneuver through traffic effectively; he also knows how to stay alive on scramble drills. Henry also is a very good route runner, especially in the short and intermediate parts of the field. He moves efficiently without any wasted lower-body movement and quickly gets into his patterns. He also possesses the short-area quickness to make hard cuts and shake defenders in man-to-man coverage. A quarterback’s best friend, he has handled a volume role well as a receiver and also has been competitive as a blocker on the edge; he identifies his targets well and knows how to position himself to maximize his chances of coming away victoriously. In addition, leadership has been a key part of Henry’s presence ever since he arrived in New England. The 2025 season was his third being voted a captain by his peers, and his teammates regularly praise him for his demeanor on and off the field. Weaknesses: Henry is a crafty blocker more so than a talented one. He carries out his assignments but is not a game-changer at the point of attack; he lacks the core strength and leg drive to consistently free up the edge in the run game and can get mispositioned against speed and power. In general, his consistency has been on and off since joining the Patriots: especially late in seasons, there has been a drop-off in his ability to maintain his typical high level of play. As a receiver, Henry lacks the explosiveness to be a consistent deep threat. He also won’t break many tackles, despite overall being a solid if unspectacular run-after-the-catch producer. 2025 review Stats : 21 games (21 starts) | 1,067 offensive snaps (78.6%), 11 special teams snaps (2.0%) | 98 targets, 69 catches (70.4%), 880 receiving yards (12.8/catch), 8 TDs, 6 drops | 4 QB pressures surrendered (2 sacks, 2 hurries) | 3 penalties (incl. 0 declined/offsetting) Season recap: Even though the Patriots offense as a whole struggled in 2024, Henry produced a career year in terms of catches (66) and receiving yards (674). Naturally, there was plenty of optimism when the team under new head coach Mike Vrabel hired Josh McDaniels to call the offense: Henry had looked good during their lone season together, and there was little to suggest that their second go-around would be any different. And indeed, it was not. Henry was once again one of New England’s top performers on the offensive side of the ball and a safety blanket for quarterback Drake Maye. As a consequence, he was on the field for more than three quarters of offensive snaps, ranking first among the Patriots’ skill position players. He also managed to set new career marks in games against the Steelers and Bengals. The first contest saw him tie his personal best with eight catches and two touchdowns, while the latter ended with him reeling in seven passes for a career-high 115 yards as well as another score. All in all, Henry was once again a pivotal part of the Patriots’ offensive operation. He finished the season ranked second on the team in targets (98), receptions (69) and receiving yards (880) — all eclipsing his 2024 numbers — while ranking first in touchdowns (7). One of those TDs came during New England’s wild card playoff win over his former team, the Chargers. THIS IS GORGEOUS 🎯 @DrakeMaye2 | @Hunter_Henry84 📺 NBC pic.twitter.com/7TYUczWj3q — New England Patriots (@Patriots) January 12, 2026 The base-line statistics tell only part of the story, though. Henry’s season was much more nuanced than “career high after career high” en route to his first Super Bowl appearance. While, yes, he also posted his best yards after the catch (5.4) and yards per route run (1.54) since joining the Patriots, and moved the chains on half of his 32 third- and fourth-down targets, he also dropped a career worst six passes and was uneven as a run blocker. In general, he was again not able to sustain what had been a strong start to the season. In the postseason especially, he failed to elevate his game against the top defenses the Patriots faced. While solid in that aforementioned game against the Chargers, he only had six receptions for 48 yards in the final three playoff games combined. So, was Henry’s 2025 season a success or…

Rechsteiner played three years at Jacksonville State, where he logged 629 receiving yards and […]
full_text: METAIRIE, LOUISIANA - JUNE 17: Brock Rechsteiner #89 of the New Orleans Saints takes part in drills during mandatory mini camp at Ochsner Sports Performance Center on June 17, 2026 in Metairie, Louisiana. (Photo by Tyler Kaufman/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL has suspended rookie wide receiver Brock Rechsteiner for the first six games of the season, per Ari Meirov. #Saints WR Brock Rechsteiner, the son of WWE Hall Of Famer Scott Steiner, has been suspended 6 games by the NFL. pic.twitter.com/Khs3zLJq2m — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) August 6, 2026 Rechsteiner, the son of WWE Hall of Famer Scott Steiner, signed with the Saints as an undrafted free agent in May. Rechsteiner played three years at Jacksonville State, where he logged 629 receiving yards and 7 touchdowns. Rechsteiner’s suspension is unfortunate for the rookie wideout, as the wide receiver room is quite crowded, and there was already a slim spot for him. With standout performances from Barion Brown in training camp and now his suspension, Rechsteiner will have a hard time making the roster. Despite his suspension, the 6-foot-2 wideout will be allowed to continue participating in training camp and during the team’s three preseason games. Rechsteiner’s suspension won’t take place until the conclusion of their preseason week three matchup with the Dallas Cowboys on August 28th. Rechsteiner will miss the first six weeks of the regular season. The reason for Rechsteiner’s suspension has yet to be disclosed.

full_text: The closest thing we get to actual NFL football has arrived with the annual Hall of Fame Game in Canton, Ohio. The Hall of Fame Game will kick off the Hall of Fame weekend festivities which will culminate with the 2026 Pro Football Hall of Fame enshrinement ceremony on Saturday. Drew Brees, the greatest quarterback in New Orleans Saints history, will be the headliner of this year’s class, but the Saints themselves will not be playing in this game. Former Cardinals WR Larry Fitzgerald and former Panthers LB Luke Kuechly stands among Brees’ fellow inductees this year, so the Cardinals and Panthers faithful should be in the stands for this exhibition game. It will be nice to see something that resembles NFL football after months of waiting. It may not be much, but we’ll take what we can get at this point. Here are the details for tonight’s exhibition: 2026 Hall of Fame Game Carolina Panthers vs. Arizona Cardinals Location – Tom Benson Hall of Fame Stadium – Canton, Ohio Weather – 63º – Partly Cloudy Game Time – 5:00pm PST / 7:00pm CST / 8:00pm EST Network – NBC Announcers – Mike Tirico and Cris Collinsworth Online and Mobile – peacocktv.com The first step toward the 2026 NFL Season is finally here!

title: Barion Brown could be the unsung hero of the WR room
summary: Of course, it’s important to temper expectations whenever going off of training camp performances, but I think we can all agree how exciting it’s been to see Barion Brown so far. Every day since pads were put on the players, Brown has been making play after play, and his ability to get separation is incredible. […]
full_text: METAIRIE, LOUISIANA - AUGUST 03: Barion Brown #19 of the New Orleans Saints reacts during training camp at Ochsner Sports Performance Center on August 03, 2026 in Metairie, Louisiana. (Photo by Morgan Simmons/Getty Images) | Getty Images Of course, it’s important to temper expectations whenever going off of training camp performances, but I think we can all agree how exciting it’s been to see Barion Brown so far. Every day since pads were put on the players, Brown has been making play after play, and his ability to get separation is incredible. When Brown was drafted by the Saints in the 6th round, his contribution on the roster was believed to be one on special teams. He is a dangerous returner that would be a massive upgrade for this special teams unit, but it seems like the Saints viewed him as a real contributor on offense. Yesterday, after yet another excellent performance in practice, Kellen Moore spoke on what the team saw from Brown in college and made sure to mention his impact on offense. "We watched a lot of evidence of (Barion Brown) playing receiver and playing impactful plays in the SEC … You're really fired up to have this guy. He's doing a great job." Coach Moore on Barion Brown pic.twitter.com/j4Vtd4K3ir — New Orleans Saints (@Saints) August 5, 2026 The Saints have had some tough decisions to make recently because rookies/young players have outperformed expectations. For 2026, it already seems like that’s going to be Brown. When he was drafted, he was put behind 4 other guys in the WR depth chart: Chris Olave, Jordyn Tyson, Devaughn Vele, and Bryce Lance. Also, before Ja’Lynn Polk retired, it was believed that he was going to be WR4, so Brown would be all the way down at the last spot. But now, there’s no way that’s going to happen. With the consistency he’s shown in practice and the major impact he’s making, there’s a good chance Brown begins the season in the 4th WR spot, and it may not take long for him to overtake Vele. Becoming the third WR is a bit more of a long shot without injuries happening, but now it’s not out of the question. Even if he stays in that fourth spot, Brown’s ability to make big plays could make him one of the most important players on offense. He may not be able to be that consistent nearly double-digit receiving yards per game guy, but I can see a more Rashid Shaheed role for him.

title: QB Jaxson Dart: Giants’ offense is ‘taking steps each day’
summary: WHITE SULPHUR SPRINGS, W.Va. — The New York Giants’ time in the “football paradise” of The Greenbrier Sports Performance Center in West Virginia is rapidly drawing to a close. It might be a sleepy area without the bright lights he and many of his teammates are accustomed to, but quarterback Jaxson Dart sounded on Thursday […]
full_text: Jaxson Dart | Getty Images WHITE SULPHUR SPRINGS, W.Va. — The New York Giants’ time in the “football paradise” of The Greenbrier Sports Performance Center in West Virginia is rapidly drawing to a close. It might be a sleepy area without the bright lights he and many of his teammates are accustomed to, but quarterback Jaxson Dart sounded on Thursday like he will miss the place. “This is like a football paradise,” Dart said. “I think that anytime that you watch any of the movies, the training camps where you’re able to see, those guys go on little getaways, I think that this is kind of that feel and it’s been a joy. “I think that what’s really good about being here is that football is the main thing, and that’s how it should be in training camp. So, I really love being here. I know the guys have too because not only has it made us better on the field, but at the same time it’s allowed us to make stronger connections off the field. So, just the more time we’ve been able to spend with one another I’ve loved, and I know all the other guys have felt the same way.” Has paradise been kind to the Giants as they learn a new offense under coordinator Matt Nagy? Dart and his cohorts have had a rough go against the team’s defense, although things did improve during the last couple of padded practices this week. “This is like a football paradise.” Jaxson Dart on West Virginia “I think that we’re taking steps each day,” Dart said. “Obviously, there’s things that you go out there and maybe it’s our first time running something or whatever, and you kind of have things you talk through. But a lot of times we have the opportunity the next day to have a chance to fix it and go at it again. “So, I think the really good thing that I’m seeing right now with the offense is our communication after practices being able to fix adjustments for the next day, and that’s really encouraging to see. And I think that if we just continue to do this process we’ll be in a good spot.”Defenses are generally ahead of offenses in these early stages. A big part of that is because there is much more to install and master when it comes to offense. Dart admitted that part of the struggle against a defense providing a variety of looks and pressure packages is the newness of what the Giants are running each day. “There’s still more things that we have to put in. There’s still a lot more things that we have to do,” the second-year quarterback said. “But I think at the same time, there’s a good amount that’s in for us and it requires us to be really locked in each and every day because it’s just NFL football. You’re getting a big install each and every day. “So, you just continue to learn, continue to get reps at things and have a lot of really valuable communication.” Dart believes dealing with Dennard Wilson’s defense, which may at times be throwing complicated looks the offense isn’t quite ready for yet, can be a benefit. “I’m happy that we’re able to see exotic looks from Dennard’s defense. I think that they do a really good job,” Dart said. “While we’re installing plays, a lot of times it’s to exotic looks. And so, it’s good for us to have that communication and it’s good for us to make those adjustments and have those conversations so by the time we get into the season, we feel like we’ve seen a lot already, which I’m really happy about just as a communication standpoint.”

title: NY Giants suffer their first worrisome injury of training camp
summary: WHITE SULPHUR SPRINGS, W.Va. — When starting slot cornerback Dru Phillips left practice early on Wednesday after getting tangled up with wide receiver Xavier Gipson, head coach John Harbaugh was hopeful Phillips would be able to return to practice on Thursday. That wasn’t the case. Phillips sat out practice on Thursday with what Harbaugh called […]
full_text: Dru Phillips | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co WHITE SULPHUR SPRINGS, W.Va. — When starting slot cornerback Dru Phillips left practice early on Wednesday after getting tangled up with wide receiver Xavier Gipson, head coach John Harbaugh was hopeful Phillips would be able to return to practice on Thursday. That wasn’t the case. Phillips sat out practice on Thursday with what Harbaugh called “a mild knee sprain.” “He came out of it pretty well,” Harbaugh said. “It’s going to be a little bit. He won’t be back tomorrow. But the good news is he’s going to be okay.” Phillips’ knee sprain is, thus far, the most significant injury the Giants have suffered during training camp. Phillips, a 2024 third-round pick, has played in 31 games over two seasons with the Giants as the team’s primary nickel cornerback. Phillips has three interceptions and a 92.3 passer rating against in two seasons. His run support was not up to par last season, but he showed in 2024 that he can be an asset against the run. Ar’Darius Washington , a versatile defensive back signed as a free agent from the Baltimore Ravens during the offseason, is likely to step in for Phillips. Another injured cornerback Jarrick Bernard-Converse has been out of practice most of the week. “Bernard’s dealing with an ongoing knee issue,” Harbaugh said. “I think he’s been dealing with that here before. So, that flared up on him.”

There was really nothing noteworthy from the slow-paced practice, except that for some unexplained reason cornerback Nic Jones and wide receiver Xavier Gipson squared […]
full_text: WHITE SULPHUR SPRINGS, W.Va. — The New York Giants held a walk-through of roughly two hours and 15 minutes on Thursday, a light day of work after three consecutive padded practices. There was really nothing noteworthy from the slow-paced practice, except that for some unexplained reason cornerback Nic Jones and wide receiver Xavier Gipson squared off at the end of practice. That happened out of my vantage point, but was seen by a couple of reporters stationed at the opposite end of the practice field. No winners and losers today as there wasn’t enough happening. If there was a “loser,” it would have to be the fans who traveled to The Greenbrier Sports Performance Center for a practice during which nothing worth watching happened. Injury updates The only player held out of practice, as far as I could tell, was cornerback Dru Phillips . He was in attendance, but did not work after leaving practice early on Wednesday. Brian Burns, Malachi Fields, and Beau Brade all worked. Malik Nabers even participated in team periods during the non-contact walk-through. Roster move I have been asked a number of times if the Giants had a backup fullback. Well, now they do after signing undrafted rookie free agent fullback/defensive tackle Grant Finley. Patrick Ricard, the Giants fullback who has made six Pro Bowls in nine seasons, followed that path as a fullback/defensive tackle when he entered the NFL. Maybe John Harbaugh thinks Finley can be next. Remaining Greenbrier practice schedule Friday, August 7 — 1:30-4 p.m. (Open to the public) Saturday, August 8 — 10 a.m. – 12:30 p.m.

title: Giants sign FB/DL Grant Finley, waive TE Tyler Moore
summary: Fullback enjoyers rejoice. The New York Giants announced that they’ve signed fullback / defensive lineman Grant Finley. Finley is an undrafted free agent out of Missouri Western who played both sides of the ball over his three years. He has solid measurables for both fullback and defensive line, standing 6-foot-4, 281 pounds and is a […]
full_text: Fullback enjoyers rejoice. The New York Giants announced that they’ve signed fullback / defensive lineman Grant Finley . Finley is an undrafted free agent out of Missouri Western who played both sides of the ball over his three years. He has solid measurables for both fullback and defensive line, standing 6-foot-4, 281 pounds and is a solid athlete for either position. He turned a 4.88-second 40-yard dash, with a 32-inch vertical and 9-foot-11 broad jump, at the Missouri Western Pro Day. Finley previously worked out for the Giants at their rookie minicamp in May. Head coach John Harbaugh has committed to a power run game, bringing in run game guru Greg Roman as well as All-Pro and Pro Bowl fullback Patrick Ricard. Adding a second fullback is an oddity in the modern NFL, but it does allow the Giants to practice their 21-Personnel plays while keeping reps off of the 32-year old Ricard. The Giants could also view Finley as a developmental player who could take over for Ricard in the future. He does also have some upside on the defensive side of the ball as well. He has 16 tackles for a loss, 7.5 sacks, and six passes defensed over the last three years at Missouri Western. The Giants waived tight end Tyler Moore , who was signed shortly before the start of training camp, in a corresponding roster move.

You readers know exactly what the dog days of August signify: It’s time to get serious about fantasy football prep for redraft leagues. Lots of news and noise emerges from NFL training […]
full_text: The Giants’ offense survived the loss of the electric Nabers | Getty Images NFL training camps are underway, and the start of the 2026-27 NFL season is less than six weeks away. Can you believe it? You readers know exactly what the dog days of August signify: It’s time to get serious about fantasy football prep for redraft leagues. Lots of news and noise emerges from NFL training camps. There will be some stories and developments that matter, and plenty that don’t. Let’s put that aside for now, since we don’t know what we might hear over the next month or so. As training camps get underway, here are the stories I’m paying the most attention to, for fantasy purposes. You can find all of my preseason fantasy content, including preliminary rankings and tiers, at this link . All fantasy rankings shown are for Half-point PPR, on a points per game basis, and exclude the final week of the season. Average Draft Position (ADP) shown is also for Half-Point PPR, as of August 3. Alvin Kamara didn’t retire — Now what? How much Kamara eats into Travis Etienne’s workload is an important question. We may not get much of an answer to this before the season starts, but lots of people expected Kamara to retire, and he didn’t. He’s coming back for at least one more season, on a restructured deal. Is he dust at this point, or can he still be a factor in the passing game and at the goal line? He used to excel at both, and those high-leverage touches are what could be the difference between Top-10 numbers or something a lot lower for Etienne. I’m in on Kellen Moore’s offense in year two, but would have been a lot happier using an early pick on Etienne if Kamara wasn’t hanging around. 2. It’s only August 4, and the 49ers are already banged up. Shocker, right? Are they cursed? Is it the substation? Ricky Pearsall (PCL) is lost for the season. A guy who didn’t miss a single college game in five seasons because of injury will miss 31 across his first three NFL seasons. It doesn’t end there, though. George Kittle (achilles) opened camp on PUP, as expected, newly added Christian Kirk has a calf injury, new addition and future hall of famer Mike Evans has a quad strain, and second round rookie D’Zhaun Stribling has a hamstring issue. Even Kyle Shanahan is injured, after a bad car accident. The team just brought back Deebo Samuel, Sr. , but he hasn’t exceeded 75 catches or 1,000 yards since 2021 (and that was his only season hitting those marks).Evans will be 33 on August 21 and missed 12 games with injuries over the last two seasons. Evans isn’t the only old guy. Kittle will be 33 in October, Samuel is 30, Kirk is 29, and Christian McCaffrey is 30. Yikes. And yet, this is an offense that scores and scores… 3. Will Malik Nabers be ready Week 1, and at what strength? This has been one of the most significant fantasy stories all off-season. After months of discouraging news about his recovery from a major knee injury suffered in Week 4 of the 2025 season, which included a clean-up procedure, Nabers didn’t open camp on PUP, and now there’s speculation that he’ll be ready to go Week 1. He’s still at a major discount right now, at an ADP of overall player 39 (WR19). More positive news from camp will continue to push him up. Even if he’s ready to go Week 1, the question will be how close he is to his full strength. It’s often the year AFTER the year after an ACL tear that players get their explosiveness back. Still, Nabers is an elite talent and is already a proven producer at age 23, and if he’s a go to start the season, his ADP should climb and end up no lower than the 2-3 turn. Obviously, a healthy Nabers would be huge for second year QB Jaxson Dart . 4. Are the Cardinals going to trade James Conner or Trey Benson ? I’m asking for a friend. Actually, I’m asking for a lot of friends: The entire fantasy community. Overall #3 pick Jeremiyah Love and newcomer Tyler Allgeier should both play a lot of snaps for the Cardinals this season. But what of Conner and Benson? Both are trade candidates, and a running back injury on another team could expedite a move. Love’s ADP is a little rich for me at 31 (RB14). Arizona has the league’s toughest schedule and they’re projected to score one of the lowest point totals for the season. Plus, they had the fewest running back carries in the league last season. The big crowd in the RB room only makes it worse. 5. Will Josh Jacobs suffer any league discipline (or face legal charges)? For now, neither Rashee Rice nor Jacobs is facing a suspension relating to his off-field incidents. The Fantasy community has been watching closely for developments. Rice appears to be in the clear for this season, but the police investigation is still open on Jacobs, and it’s possible he could face a suspension at some point this season. His ADP (RB17, 37 overall) reflects that uncertainty. He finished as the RB6 and the RB9 in 2024 and 2025. 6. Where (if anywhere) will Brandon Aiyuk and/or Keenan Allen sign? Deebo is back with the 49ers as discussed above, and it sounds like Tyreek Hill’s injury recovery timeline won’t allow him to play this year. Stefon Diggs just signed a one-year deal with the Commanders. That leaves the duo above as the biggest names who remain unsigned. Teams that could be in the market: Kansas City, Baltimore, New Orleans, Indianapolis, and Buffalo, among others. 7. The progress of players returning from season-ending injuries is always important to monitor as the season approaches. The next six weeks won’t reveal how much Patrick Mahomes or Daniel Jones will use his legs this season, but it should tell us if they’re ready to go Week 1. I’ll be keeping an eye for injury recovery news related to those two, plus Nabers and Kittle who I already discussed, and Zach Charbonnet , Tucker Kraft , Alec Pierce , Michael Penix , Jr. , and others who are returning from injuries and surgeries that happened since the start of last season. That’s it for today. Keep it here for more preseason fantasy content. Coming later this month: Sleepers, and players to target and avoid at ADP.
author: David Hartman

title: Giants news: Patriots hosting former Giants guard Greg Van Roten
summary: The New England Patriots are hosting former New York Giants guard Greg Van Roten for a workout, per a report from Ian Rapoport. Van Roten, 36, spent the last two years as the Giants’ right guard, joining Jermaine Eluemunor in coming to New York from the Las Vegas Raiders. While certainly not an elite guard, […]
full_text: Greg Van Roten | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New England Patriots are hosting former New York Giants guard Greg Van Roten for a workout, per a report from Ian Rapoport . Van Roten, 36, spent the last two years as the Giants’ right guard, joining Jermaine Eluemunor in coming to New York from the Las Vegas Raiders. While certainly not an elite guard, Van Roten comported himself well once he became established in 2024 and carried that into 2025. And despite being an older lineman, Van Roten was a steady presence for the Giants and started all 34 games for them over the last two years. The Giants opted to move on from Van Roten after the 2025 season, adding Daniel Faalele as well as retaining Evan Neal and Joshua Ezeudu in free agency. There was some thought that the trio could compete to fill the right guard spot next to Eluemunor, or at least there was until Dexter Lawrence demanded his trade and the Cincinnati Bengals sent the 10th overall pick to New York. That pick turned into Sisi Mauigoa, who is in line to lock down the right guard spot and hopefully upgrade the position. It remains to be seen whether the Patriots will sign Van Roten, but he should still at least be able to be a good depth piece at guard and center.

title: NY Giants Odell Beckham feeling ‘a lot of love’ from fans, and making them dream
summary: WHITE SULPHUR SPRINGS, W.Va. — For the past couple of days, Odell Beckham Jr. has made New York Giants fans dare to dream that he can actually complete an unlikely comeback. Beckham, 33, will never again be the superstar he was for a few years after the Giants selected him in the first round of […]
full_text: Odell Beckham | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect WHITE SULPHUR SPRINGS, W.Va. — For the past couple of days, Odell Beckham Jr. has made New York Giants fans dare to dream that he can actually complete an unlikely comeback. Beckham, 33, will never again be the superstar he was for a few years after the Giants selected him in the first round of the 2014 NFL Draft. Age and several leg injuries guarantee that. Can he, though, be productive after not playing in 2025 and playing sparingly in 2024? Maybe. Don’t get caught up in the “oh my God, Odell is taking first-team reps” hype. Yes, Beckham has taken reps with starting quarterback Jaxson Dart in the past two practices. So, too, have Jalin Hyatt and Xavier Gipson. Malik Nabers is not taking team reps. Malachi Fields has only done individual drills for the past couple of days. Darius Slayton is ramping up after double sports hernia surgeries during the offseason. JuJu Smith-Schuster missed a practice this week. The story isn’t, or shouldn’t be, that Beckham is getting a handful of training camp reps with the starters. That feels like missing the forest for the trees. The story is that Beckham has practiced every day thus far. The story is, or should be, that after the injuries and time away, Beckham is still a good player. He can still run. He still has strong, sure hands. He is still a good route runner. He doesn’t have the explosive athleticism of his youth, but he can still get open. Wednesday was Beckham’s best day. He caught passes from Dart, Jameis Winston and Brandon Allen at all three levels of the field. “I feel like I’m getting better,” Beckham said after Wednesday’s practice. “I feel like with repetition, with mistakes, unfortunately I’m one of those people who has to touch the stove to know that it’s hot and to not touch it again, so I learn from a mistake, and it’s like, all right, that’s something that I corrected. “So, I definitely feel like I’m getting better. There’s definitely been more opportunities. It’s just a combination of both. But kind of just fizzle all that out, and I’m just like – I’m just locked in the moment. I’m truly grateful for being where my feet are at and just trying to enjoy that each and every day and bring the best energy that I can.” Defensive back Ar’Darius Washington played with Beckham in 2023 with the Ravens. “He almost looks better (than 2023),” Washington said. “As far as his physical abilities and things like that, he’s still rolling. Sometimes he gets in his head, and he doesn’t make those plays. He just wants it so bad, I’ll just tell him, just relax. Be yourself. It’s going to come to you. “He’s still got the juice in the tank. Hundred percent.” Cornerback Paulson Adebo has also been impressed. “He’s been great. I think every time we line up against him, he looks good,” Adebo said. “I grew up watching him as a youngin’, so it’s definitely cool to be able to go up against him, but yeah, he definitely looks like he looks ready.” When fans are in attendance at training camp practices, every Beckham catch is greeted by a louder, more excited crowd reaction than any other player receives. Clearly, they want Beckham to make this team and help the Giants win. Beckham, who said he gets “a lot of juice” from the fans, also wants that. “It’s a lot of love,” Beckham said. “Most people don’t get a chance to double back, and this is a place that made me into a man, made me into who I am. I have so much love for this organization, this city. I’ve got New York tatted on my back; you know what I mean? And I’m from New Orleans. “So, all I ever wanted to do was win a championship for the New York Giants and just having an opportunity right now to – the end goal in mind, but stack those days, that’s all I want to do for this city, this organization, is bring one home.” Beckham did not have to put himself through this. He has fame. He has money. He has nearly 600 catches and 8,000 receiving yards. He was, during his first tenure with the Giants, arguably, the game’s best receiver. He chose this, in an effort to leave the game on his own terms. “I feel like if this comes off selfish, sorry, but this is like – this is for me. This is [to] prove to myself. It’s never really been to prove it to others, but it’s always fun when you can prove it to others,” Beckham said. “But this is for me, this is for my son, this is like – in our household, we never give up, you know what I’m saying? No matter what it is, you’re going to finish what you started. And that’s kind of all this is to me. “I take it as if God’s giving me one year, then it is what it is, but who knows what it’s going to be. I’m just trying to be present each and every day, and prove to myself that I am who I know I am.” Part of the reason head coach John Harbaugh hesitated to give Beckham this opportunity. This is what Harbaugh said after the Giants did sign Beckham to a contract: “I told him, you just can’t be okay. You’re Odell Beckham,” Harbaugh said. “You’ve got to come out here, and you’ve got to be performing at a high, high level in a workout. You’ve got to be performing at a high level in practice. “You’ve got to be a guy that’s capable that we can see would have a chance to make a difference in NFL games. You’ve got to be that kind of a player. Who knows better what that kind of a player is than Odell Beckham?” Beckham isn’t worried about that. He isn’t worried about facing the indignity of Harbaugh, a coach with whom he has a close relationship, perhaps being forced to cut him. “This is the conversation I had with Coach. Before I ever came here, he’s like, ‘You know, I’ve got a really good relationship with you, I don’t want you (to) come here, and then something happens, and you can’t make the team.’ I’m like, ‘I can live with me getting up, leaving my home, coming here and giving my best effort, and if it doesn’t work out, it doesn’t work out,’ ” Beckham said. “I couldn’t live with me feeling like I gave up on myself and I never (saw) through my dream that I’ve been chasing since I was four years old. I just couldn’t live with that. “So, it is what it is. I’m all for competition. I’ve always been like that. I feel like I rise to the occasion. And right now, I’m just trying to stay in the bag, you know what I mean? I’m trying to get better each and every day, know exactly what I’ve got to do, get open, catch the ball, score, get back to the game that I truly love.” Giants fans might remember the Victor Cruz comeback. After a year away from the game, Cruz caught 39 passes for 586 yards for New York in 2016, averaging 15.0 yards per catch. Those weren’t the numbers of his glory days, but he was productive. What sort of numbers can Beckham produce, if he can make the team? “People like to talk, ‘What are the stats?’ And all these things, and I’m like, the last time I played at the Ravens, I had 35 catches and 600-plus yards and four touchdowns. If you double that, that’s 70 catches, 1,200 yards, it’s a great season,” Beckham said. “So, it’s about how many opportunities you get, knowing that I may not be getting 10, 12 targets, what am I going to do with the five or six that I get? How can I help all the other receivers and the running backs, and how can I help this team? What can I bring? “I’m not so much caught up in what numbers are going to be, I just want to be the best me that I can be. I want to get open and create separation, catch the ball, hopefully score a lot, and have fun. That’s really all it is for me.” I wrote in the spring that the Giants should pass on a reunion with Beckham . I was wrong. He will never be the Beckham of old. He also, though, is not the old Beckham. He’s older. More mature. Mellower. A dad. He doesn’t seem like the young player who proposed to a kicking net and pretended to pee like a dog on the field after scoring a touchdown against the Eagles in Philadelphia. There are snaps to be had at the Giants’ wide receiver position. Malik Nabers is working back slowly from knee…

title: Geno Smith doesn’t get much love in Mike Sando’s quarterback rankings
summary: Every year Mike Sando of The Athletic polls NFL executives and coaches about the league’s quarterbacks. The votes rank the relevant quarterbacks in the NFL and place them into tiers. It probably doesn’t come as a major surprise, but coming off a rough 2025 season Geno Smith did not rate highly. Smith was in Tier […]
full_text: FLORHAM PARK, NEW JERSEY - JULY 29: Geno Smith #7 of the New York Jets throws during training camp at Atlantic Health Jets Training Center on July 29, 2026 in Florham Park, New Jersey. (Photo by Adam Hunger/Getty Images) | Getty Images Every year Mike Sando of The Athletic polls NFL executives and coaches about the league’s quarterbacks. The votes rank the relevant quarterbacks in the NFL and place them into tiers . It probably doesn’t come as a major surprise, but coming off a rough 2025 season Geno Smith did not rate highly. Smith was in Tier 4, which is defined as: Veteran who ideally would not be a full-season starter Unproven player; not enough information to classify Smith came in at 30th of the 35 passers who were part of the ranking. Smith suffered the largest year-over-year decline of any quarterback, falling from a career-best 2.90 average to 3.70. His 11-spot drop in the rankings tied Stroud’s for the largest. “He looked terrible on the film we saw,” a defensive coordinator said. The Raiders did Smith no favors. “He got sacked 10 times in a game (against Cleveland),” a defensive coach said. “Once you get hit and keep getting hit and hit and hit, how good are you going to be? They had no identity on offense. Geno got a bad rap. He was getting murdered out there.” Seven current GMs placed Smith in Tier 4. The eighth had him in Tier 5. Coaches liked Smith more than execs did. “It’s hard to tell because last year wasn’t fair, and before that he was a 3,” an offensive coach said. “I’m going to give him the benefit of the doubt and say he’s a 3 till proven otherwise.” The five quarterbacks to rank lower than Geno were Deshaun Watson, Michael Penix, Jr. Jacoby Brissett, JJ McCarthy, and Shedeur Sanders. Smith has his work cut out for him to revitalize his career. A happy Jets season will require the type of performance that lands him much higher on the 2027 quarterback ranking.

summary: Good morning Gang Green Nation! Sometimes you just have to chuckle at the absurd level of hype training camp provides. full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - DECEMBER 07: Jaylen Waddle #17 of the Miami Dolphins catches a pass for a touchdown during the NFL 2025 game against Brandon Stephens #21 of the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on December 07, 2025 in East Rutherford, New Jersey."" (Photo by Kenneth Richmond/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning Gang Green Nation! Sometimes you just have to chuckle at the absurd level of hype training camp provides. If you scroll down to the last link in today’s Flight Connections you come to an article titled “Brandon Stephens is quickly giving Jets fans a reason to forget about Sauce Gardner.” Ummm … what?! Brandon Stephens is a 28 year old journeyman who probably shouldn’t be starting in the NFL. For his career Stephens has allowed a 105+ passer rating in coverage. No quarterback in the history of the NFL has a 105+ career passer rating. Which means throwing at Stephens essentially turns the average NFL quarterback into the best quarterback of all time. Last year Stephens allowed an ungodly 134+ passer rating, the worst of his NFL career, so it’s not like he’s on the upswing in his career. Sauce Gardner is a two time All Pro. He has allowed a passer rating of 76.7 for his career. Last season the 32nd ranked NFL passer was Joe Flacco, with a 79.2 passer rating. Throwing at Gardner essentially turns the average NFL starting quarterback into worse than the worst starting quarterback in the NFL. So here’s what we have. Throw at Stephens, get results better than the best QB in NFL history. Throw at Sauce, get results worse than the worst starting quarterback in the NFL. But sure, a few decent Stephens practices in August no doubt will make Jets fans forget about their former two time All Pro cornerback. Makes perfect sense when you really think about it. The irony here is that even the author of that article doesn’t believe his own headline. Read past the headline and you see he doesn’t even try to make the case his headline implies. He knows better than that. He just wanted to put up a clickbait headline full of absurd hype, because clicks are apparently more important than not misleading your audience. Sigh. Here are your links to the New York Jets this glorious Thursday in August. title: Eagles training camp: 17 winners, 8 losers, and 5 IDKs from the first week
summary: Philadelphia Eagles training camp began just over a week ago. Let’s take a look at the most notable winners, losers, and I don’t knows from the first six practices down at the Jefferson Health Training Complex. Obligatory disclaimer: The Eagles only held one fully padded practice and it’s obviously early in camp. There’s still plenty […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - JUNE 9: Dontayvion Wicks #13 of the Philadelphia Eagles runs with the ball during mandatory minicamp at Jefferson Health Training Complex on June 9, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Philadelphia Eagles training camp began just over a week ago. Let’s take a look at the most notable winners, losers, and I don’t knows from the first six practices down at the Jefferson Health Training Complex. Obligatory disclaimer: The Eagles only held one fully padded practice and it’s obviously early in camp. There’s still plenty of time for players to change their outlook — for better or worse — over the next few weeks. For historical context, here’s a look at the W-L-IDKs from this time last year . WINNERS JALEN HURTS By no means has Hurts and the offense been perfect. They’ve had some rough days where they’ve been dominated by Vic Fangio’s defense. But Hurts has also been missing Lane Johnson, DeVonta Smith, and Makai Lemon for multiple practices. Despite this, the slimmed-down signal caller has turned in some sharp sessions where he looks totally in control on offense. Hurts seems to be fully embracing Sean Mannion’s new offensive direction. It feels like the arrow is pointing up here as he enters a pivotal season. JALEN CARTER Carter signed a record-breaking contract extension before training camp began. The early returns on that massive investment are looking good. Carter has dominated the Eagles’ offensive line. He seems to be buying into the messaging about how he was paid for what he’s going to do next, not his past accomplishments. Carter should be expected to have the best season of his career in 2026. JALYX HUNT Hunt made a big leap from Year 1 to Year 2 to lead the 2025 Eagles in sacks … and interceptions! The 25-year-old looks poised to take another significant step forward this season. Hunt has been living in the backfield. He absolutely feasted on Fred Johnson at right tackle in one practice. And that was after he gave Jordan Mailata trouble on the other side of the line the previous day. I’d advise buying all the Hunt stock you can possibly afford. No one should be surprised if — no, WHEN — he produces double-digit sacks this season. DONTAYVION WICKS Wicks has been Hurts’ top target with both Smith and Lemon missing time due to hamstring injuries. The former Green Bay Packers wideout looks ready to take on the WR2 role in Philly. He’s done a nice job of getting open and he’s made some tough contested catches as well. Wicks has had some struggles with drops in the past (nine in 2024) but that hasn’t been an issue for him so far in camp (knock on wood). “For now [Dontayvion Wicks] is really developing nicely. People around the Eagles are really excited about that player.” @JFowlerESPN reports on the Philadelphia Eagles' new offense during training camp 👀 pic.twitter.com/3FS5ORwcMW — NFL on ESPN (@ESPNNFL) August 5, 2026 DARIUS COOPER As the original identifier of Darius Cooper’s greatness, I’m admittedly biased here. But don’t just take my word for it. Look at what Hurts said about DC, unprompted : MIKE GARAFOLO: How about this receiver room? We know DeVonta Smith, what he’s done over the course of his career, we know he’s going to produce. Everybody’s saying, ‘Who’s the number two?’ And I don’t even know if you look at it that way. Maybe it’s two, three, four, and that’s all one kind of cluster to you. But you’ve got some veterans who have been around, [Dontayvion] Wicks has got the cheat code because he’s been in this offense before. Who’s really emerged and opened your eyes there? JALEN HURTS: I think Darius Cooper has done a really good job. I think Darius Cooper has done a really good job. He’s always been a big body, physical, strong hands guy. But just to see how he’s transitioned going into Year 2, definitely excited for him. Along with the rest of them. Cooper rotates in with the first-team offense and gets a lot of looks that result in good outcomes for the offense. At this point in time, I’d be surprised if the Eagles actually make him one of their top three receivers. But he’s building a compelling case to be more involved in the offense than he was as a rookie last year. ELIJAH MOORE On one hand, it shouldn’t be surprising that Moore is flashing. The 2021 second-round pick (No. 34 overall) has generated some excitement in the past. But this is also a player who got cut by the wide receiver-needy Buffalo Bills last season … and finished the 2025 campaign on the Denver Broncos’ practice squad. So, it’s not like it was a given that Moore would make the most of his opportunities in Philly. That’s exactly what he’s done, though, as he’s rotated in with the first-team offense. While Moore clearly has some juice to offer on offense, I do wonder if his lack of special teams experience could hurt him when it comes to roster cuts. If I had to rank the Eagles’ receivers solely based on what I’ve seen from them in training camp, I’d go: DeVonta Smith Dontayvion Wicks Darius Cooper Elijah Moore Hollywood Brown Johnny Wilson Britain Covey Danny Gray Quez Watkins Makai Lemon Erik Ezukanma Samori Toure Brandon Hayes TANK BIGSBY As we’ve noted , Bigsby looks simply too good to not be involved more on offense this season. An encouraging sign on that front: he’s gotten a decent amount of work with the starters. Of course, part of that is probably about managing Saquon Barkley’s practice workload. Still, Bigsby has shown a lot of juice as both a runner and a pass-catcher. He’s clearly RB2 and I have to imagine he would be RB1 on a number of teams. ANDREW MUKUBA Mukuba had made some nice plays and I can’t recall him losing many reps or being caught out of position. I have reason to believe he’s at least going to be a quality starter, if not more. The safety position as a whole seems to be in good hands. I know Eagles fans have been worrying about this spot but Mukuba, Marucs Epps, and Michael Carter II have all had some positive moments. I’m not really concerned about this group. MARKEL BELL Lane Johnson’s excused absence has benefited Bell, who’s been able to log more first-team reps than he would be getting otherwise. The rookie third-round pick has seen more starting action than veteran Fred Johnson. He might actually take over as the Eagles’ swing tackle … or at least be the primary backup at one of the two tackle positions. DREW KENDALL Kendall has repped at both center and guard, which speaks to the Eagles preparing him for last year’s Brett Toth role as the top backup interior option. Kendall saw some first-team left guard action earlier this week with Landon Dickerson getting a rest day. He doesn’t look like he doesn’t belong when he’s out there. ANDY DALTON I wouldn’t say Dalton has been great. But he’s been much better than he was in the spring (low bar). He looks like a veteran backup who knows what he’s doing in this offense. So, he’s meeting realistic expectations. Dalton is ahead of McKee so far. Still time for that to change as we see them perform in practice and preseason games over the next few weeks. COLE PAYTON Payton is not a lock to make the roster just because the Eagles used a fifth-round pick on him. Just look at Kyle McCord last year, who was waived despite being selected at No. 181 overall. And consider that Payton was taken at No. 178 overall in the 2026 NFL Draft. The difference here is that Payton is showing more intriguing potential. Yes, he’s been guilty of throwing interceptions. But I would call them good mistakes because he was being aggressive. The Eagles will probably want to reign him in a bit but, to me, it’s good that he’s erring on the side of fearlessness rather than looking too scared to let it rip. The team shouldn’t risk losing Payton to waivers, especially since Hurts is their only other quarterback under contract beyond 2026. JEREMIAH TROTTER JR. Fangio talked up Trot Jr. on Wednesday morning: Trot’s had a very good camp. Trot,…

full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 16: Jalen Hurts #1 and Darius Cooper #80 look on against the Detroit Lions at Lincoln Financial Field on November 16, 2025 in Philadelphia, United States. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Jalen Hurts interview with Mike Garafolo and Brian Baldinger – NFL Network MIKE GARAFOLO: How about this receiver room? We know DeVonta Smith, what he’s done over the course of his career, we know he’s going to produce. Everybody’s saying, ‘Who’s the number two?’ And I don’t even know if you look at it that way. Maybe it’s two, three, four, and that’s all one kind of cluster to you. But you’ve got some veterans who have been around, [Dontayvion] Wicks has got the cheat code because he’s been in this offense before. Who’s really emerged and opened your eyes there? … JALEN HURTS: I think Darius Cooper has done a really good job. I think Darius Cooper has done a really good job. He’s always been a big body, physical, strong hands guy. But just to see how he’s transitioned going into Year 2, definitely excited for him. Along with the rest of them. Eagles Training Camp Practice Notes: Jalen Hurts looked sharp – BGN JALEN HURTS UPDATE: Hurts looked pretty sharp today! QB1 completed all of his attempts in 7-on-7 … save for one dropped pass by E.J. Jenkins that hit the tight end in his hands. Hurts connected with Dallas Goedert over the middle with a ball that was placed just over the flyswatter dummy that’s designed to simulate a leaping defensive lineman. Hurts threw a perfect pass with anticipation into a tight window along the left sideline down the field to Dontayvion Wicks. Unlike earlier in his career, Hurts also doesn’t really take off running in 7-on-7, which is refreshing to see since that’s a useless thing to do in a pure passing drill. 7 standout players from NFL training camp so far – SB Nation Jalyx Hunt, EDGE — Philadelphia Eagles. The Eagles have so much defensive talent, and while Jalyx Hunt made a strong impression in limited time during the 2025 season, he’s really asserting himself now as a player to watch. Hunt has been blowing past the Eagles’ stout offensive line in practice and looking every bit of a double-digit sack guy, which is huge after Philly lost Jaelan Phillips in free agency. Seven takeaways from Vic Fangio’s Wednesday training camp press conference – PhillyVoice Vic likes what he has seen from Andrew Mukuba mentally so far. “It’s just experience, knowledge and know-how of the defense, Fangio said of the difference between Mukuba this year and last year. “You might look and say, ‘Man, he looks quicker. He’s in better shape. This, that.’ I think it’s just the thought process [speeding] up, comfortability with the defense and what he has to do. He’s in a little bit better shape too.” #JimmySays: I haven’t often seen Mukuba beaten through the first six practices. He is having a sneaky-good camp, in sort of a quiet way. How Eli Stowers is dealing with a slow start in his first NFL training camp – NBCSP One of the most important skills for a young rookie trying to find his way in the NFL is dealing with frustration. Dealing with disappointment. Dealing with the rough days that inevitably occur. For Eli Stowers, it’s all a part of football. “It’s always a challenge when something bad goes down, and you just have to continuously learn how to get back up, not worry about the last play and continue on to the next play,” Stowers said after practice Wednesday. I’m just out here trying to learn, continuously learn every single day. And I’m really appreciative of my coaches so far just trying to help me get going at this level and I’m super excited for what’s going to come.” Eagles training camp: Markel Bell works through ‘growing pains’ filling in for Lane Johnson – The Athletic The third-round rookie’s progress appears to be back on track. Bell initially filled in at right tackle during OTAs for Lane Johnson, who regularly misses the voluntary workouts to train on his own. Fred Johnson’s Saturday spot “start” suggested Bell still needed to improve. Bell said Lane Johnson told him “the other week” that there would be “growing pains” in learning the system and playing right tackle. Bell had only played left tackle in college. He acknowledged “it’s a whole different ballgame over there” and that he’s had to adjust against a defense that has ranked in the top nine in terms of EPA in both years under coordinator Vic Fangio. More than a week into Eagles training camp, Jalen Hurts and the new-look offense are ‘calibrating’ – Inquirer The new-look offense under first-year coordinator Sean Mannion is still in the early days of installation. While it got the best of Vic Fangio’s defense Monday, the defense has the upper hand so far through six days of practice. Wednesday’s practice was a run-heavy day, and it was a shorter practice compared to Tuesday’s session that ran nearly two hours. For Hurts, Wednesday was another chance to “continue to take strides.” It isn’t supposed to be easy to install a new offense against one of the best defenses in the NFL. “I like to think of the term calibrating,” Hurts said. “This is a time where we’re kind of putting it together and finding out who we are. We’ve got a lot of new pieces, an entirely new approach and MO, philosophy, to our offense. Being able to put that together and make it our own, I’m excited about where we are.” Spadaro: Marcus Epps takes Andrew Mukuba under his wing – PhiladelphiaEagles.com There has always been, in many instances, a big brother/little brother element in the Eagles’ locker room, a key to the team’s success through the years. When the veterans on the team care enough and are selfless enough to show younger players the way, transitions happen, careers are grown, seamless production takes place. Zach Ertz to Dallas Goedert … Jason Kelce to Cam Jurgens … Fletcher Cox to Jordan Davis and Jalen Carter … Darius Slay to Quinyon Mitchell and Cooper DeJean. The list goes on and on, and it is a huge reason why the Eagles have been a championship contender for so many seasons. There are similar stories happening now, and one of them is Marcus Epps and Andrew Mukuba. Epps is the eight-year veteran whose career has never been on a linear path – a sixth-round draft pick in Minnesota in 2019 who was released midway through his rookie season, picked up by the Eagles and a contributing player on the defense through the 2022 campaign, another move to Las Vegas for 2023 and 2024 before suffering a torn ACL, signed in New England for five months in early 2025, added to the Eagles’ practice squad last season, promoted to the 53-man roster in late September … A lot of moves. Nothing given. Everything earned. Lane Johnson misses fourth straight Eagles practice – PFT The Eagles are practicing without right tackle Lane Johnson for the fourth straight day on Wednesday. Johnson has been excused from practice for what is described as a non-injury related reason. There’s been no word from the team about when Johnson will be back, but Jeff McLane of the Philadelphia Inquirer reports that he is expected to return soon. 2026 NFL season: Future Hall of Famers from all 32 teams – ESPN Keep it up: QB Jalen Hurts, CB Quinyon Mitchell. I thought the Prescott Hall of Fame discussion was going to be tough. Hurts has obviously had rough points at times over the past few years, but he has also done two things the Hall of Fame loves: play quarterback and win a lot of games. Hurts is 57-25 as a starter and has two trips to the Super Bowl, winning the game’s MVP award when the Eagles blew out the Chiefs. He also finished second in regular-season MVP balloting to Patrick Mahomes in 2022, with a late-season shoulder injury costing Hurts a chance at taking home the hardware. Later in practice, it was running back Lew Nichols and D’Shawn Jamison in a scuffle on the ground who had to be separated. After all of the fighting […]
full_text: Aug 03, 2026; Latrobe, PA, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers (8) throws a pass during a practice session at Training camp at Saint Vincent College. Mandatory Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect LATROBE – It was a chippy day of practice on Thursday as we saw receiver Ben Skowronek get into it with linebackers Payton Wilson and Patrick Queen. Later in practice, it was running back Lew Nichols and D’Shawn Jamison in a scuffle on the ground who had to be separated. After all of the fighting and play on the field, it’s time for our daily look at who performed well and who had a rough go on an eventful seventh day of training camp practice. Stock Up QB Aaron Rodgers Rodgers was operating on a different level today. What was most impressive were the layered throws over defenders in the middle of the field. Rodgers was peppering DK Metcalf and Roman Wilson with targets all practice long. The veteran was feeling himself today, and could be seen hitting some of his signature fist pump emotes after some throws. EDGE Jack Sawyer We had not seen a lot from Sawyer up to this point, but he certainly put together a strong practice today. Sawyer had some wins on reps during run plays and seemed to be getting into the backfield at a solid rate today. He capped it off with what would have been a sack in a game situation in which Sawyer came screaming off the edge and had Mason Rudolph dead to rights. Sawyer seems like someone who will only get better with increased opportunities, and we saw some of that today. DL Derrick Harmon It was a big day for the defensive line, and Harmon is a big reason for that. The Steelers’ run defense was significantly better when Harmon was healthy last season, and today was another glaring example of why. Harmon was wrecking the first-team offense when they were trying to run the ball today. Whether they ran to the inside or outside, the defensive lineman always seemed to be the first one there making contact. Harmon is a seriously gifted run defender who has a chance to become a household name this season. Stock Down QB Drew Allar It was not a day to remember for the Steelers’ third-round quarterback. The accuracy on short throws was very spotty, and the timing seemed to be off over the middle. Allar led the lone two-minute drill at the end of practice, and his only completion was called back for offensive pass interference. However, the blame can’t fall solely on his shoulders, as he hit Kaden Wetjen twice in the hands and he wasn’t able to bring it in. This type of practice is exactly what the Steelers knew they were getting into when selecting Allar. He is a work in progress that can make otherworldly throws and plays, but needs serious polishing on the simple stuff and mechanics. S Jaquan Brisker Brisker is someone who I cannot wait to see play this season. He should form one of the better safety duos in the entire league with DeShon Elliott. However, this now marks the third practice in which Brisker has dropped what should have been an easy interception. As good as Rodgers was today, he got a bit wild throwing a cross-body post route to Roman Wilson, which was thrown well short. Brisker was the defender that should have had the interception, but it just bounced off his hands. Stuff like this happens, but it is worth noting that this is the third day in a row in which the safety has not been able to come down with an interception after being in prime position for one. It’s no reason to be overly concerned, in fact, you can look at it as a good thing that he is so often around the ball in favorable positions that by the time the season rolls around, fans can count on him for a splash play or two when the defense needs it. title: Steelers training camp: Defense dominates a chippy practice
summary: LATROBE – The Pittsburgh Steelers returned to the practice field on Thursday for what would end up being their longest – and chippiest – practice of training camp thus far. There were also multiple players that left with injuries on a day that was dominated by the defense. Let’s dive in. Multiple scuffles take place […]
full_text: Aug 03, 2026; Latrobe, PA, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers linebacker Cole Holcomb (55) and defensive end Gabriel Rubio (96) look to tackle running back Lew Nichols (35) during a practice session at Training camp at Saint Vincent College. Mandatory Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect LATROBE – The Pittsburgh Steelers returned to the practice field on Thursday for what would end up being their longest – and chippiest – practice of training camp thus far. There were also multiple players that left with injuries on a day that was dominated by the defense. Let’s dive in. Multiple scuffles take place It appears the Steelers saved their aggression specifically for today. After a week of clean practices with little to no fights, a handful of altercations took place Thursday. During an 11-on-11 team period, Ben Skowronek and Payton Wilson exchanged words and open-hand punches were thrown. “He just grabbed me from the back,” Skowronek told me after practice . “Grabbed my jersey. I was blocking PQ, we got into it… we’re just competitive. When you’re out here 11-on-11 a bunch of days in a row, we’re all competitive, we all wanna win. Sometimes some extra curriculars happen after the play. But at the end of the day we’re teammates and we’ll be out there in a handful of weeks on Sundays going against the other guys.” Lew Nichols and D’Shawn Jamison also got into a skirmish, this one a bit more physical. Nichols blocked Jamison, who was coming for the quarterback. The two went to the ground and had to be pulled apart. They continued to chirp at one another on the sideline after the play. There were other close calls in which players nearly came to blows. DeShon Elliott lowered a shoulder into DK Metcalf as he was running out of bounds. Metcalf hit the ground and multiple offensive players came over to Elliott, though he immediately helped Metcalf up, recognizing his mistake. Asante Samuel Jr. also tripped Pat Freiermuth during team period. Like Elliott, he immediately got up and patted himself on the chest as a way of admitting fault. For a camp that features no live tackling, Thursday was very physical. Injuries hit multiple contributors The Steelers had a great week with limited injuries, but the bug finally bit on Thursday. First-round pick Max Iheanachor left practice with an injury, as did cornerback Brandin Echols. The severity of both is yet to be known. Additionally, running back/wide receiver Eli Heidenreich and defensive lineman Logan Lee were both held out of practice with undisclosed injuries. Defense wins the day After a very successful week for the offense, it was the defense who won the day on Thursday. Derrick Harmon and T.J. Watt both batted down passes at the line of scrimmage, and Sebastian Joseph-Day got enough of one pass that prevented a completion to Rico Dowdle. Jaquan Brisker had a great play in coverage, breaking in on a one-on-one deep ball from Mason Rudolph to DK Metcalf to prevent a completion. Nick Herbig blew up a run play for what would have been a three-yard loss. They capped off the day with a win in the two-minute drill. An overall very nice day from the defense. Other notes The Steelers continue to toy with looks that involve T.J. Watt, Alex Highsmith, and Nick Herbig all on the field. There were looks where all three lined up on the ball, as well as Herbig playing off-ball. Doneiko Slaughter had another nice day. After Brandin Echols went out, he ran with the first-team and had what would have been a tackle for loss on a swing pass to Jaylen Warren. Jack Sawyer had a great rep against Broderick Jones. Gets outside leverage and would have been a sack in-game. Aaron Rodgers hit Roman Wilson for a long touchdown in team period. It gets called back due to a penalty on DK Metcalf away from the play, but Wilson continues to light up training camp. Writing may be on the wall for Kaleb Johnson. Travis Homer and Lew Nichols continue to get the second and third-team reps at the same rate, or at an even higher rate, than No. 20. I truly don’t see a spot for him on the roster. Pittsburgh may need to go get one more receiver. Kaden Wetjen is not a good pass-catcher. Drew Allar looked his way on consecutive plays during the two-minute drill, both of which Wetjen dropped. No matter how terrific a returner he was in college – and may be in the NFL – he isn’t an NFL receiver. Let us know what you think in the comments . title: Steelers’ Joey Porter ranked outside top 25 NFL cornerbacks
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers continue to view Joey Porter Jr. as a potential cornerstone of their defense, but a new set of rankings suggests not everyone is as high on the former second-round pick. Bleacher Report’s NFL Scouting Department ranked Porter as the 27th-best cornerback in the NFL entering the 2026 season, placing him between Minnesota Vikings corner Byron Murphy […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PA - NOVEMBER 02: Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. (24) looks on during the NFL football game between the Indianapolis Colts and Pittsburgh Steelers on November 02, 2025 at Acrisure Stadium in Pittsburgh, PA. (Photo by Mark Alberti/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers continue to view Joey Porter Jr. as a potential cornerstone of their defense, but a new set of rankings suggests not everyone is as high on the former second-round pick. Bleacher Report’s NFL Scouting Department ranked Porter as the 27th-best cornerback in the NFL entering the 2026 season, placing him between Minnesota Vikings corner Byron Murphy Jr. at No. 26 and Philadelphia Eagles defensive back Riq Woolen at No. 28. The list is topped by Denver Broncos star Patrick Surtain II, widely regarded as one of the league’s premier shutdown corners. The ranking is likely to spark debate among Steelers fans, many of whom believe Porter has already established himself as one of the AFC’s better young cover corners. Since entering the league in 2023, Porter has consistently drawn difficult assignments against opposing No. 1 receivers while developing into a physical press-man defender capable of limiting explosive plays. While Porter has not always produced eye-catching interception totals, his ability to stay attached in coverage and challenge receivers at the line of scrimmage has made him one of Pittsburgh’s most trusted defensive backs. Given that reputation, a ranking outside the league’s top 25 cornerbacks may come as a surprise. The timing is also noteworthy as Porter continues to await a long-term contract extension from the Steelers. With several young cornerbacks around the league signing lucrative new deals, Pittsburgh faces increasing pressure to secure one of its defensive building blocks before his price climbs even higher. Every evaluation — whether favorable or critical — adds another layer to the discussion surrounding what Porter could ultimately command on his next contract. Whether Bleacher Report’s evaluation proves accurate or serves as added motivation, Porter will have an opportunity to change the narrative this season. A standout 2026 campaign against the NFL’s top receivers could quickly move him up future rankings while strengthening his case for one of the league’s richest contracts at the position. I asked McCarthy about what the progression he’s seen in Drew Allar from rookie minicamp up through the first week of training camp, to which the Steelers’ head coach said the rookie is making daily throws that raise eyebrows. “He’s doing what you want from a young player,” McCarthy said . “These are tough practices because you’re not just repeating concepts… there hasn’t been a day where he hasn’t made a throw that makes you say, ‘Okay, that’s a young man taking a step.‘” Allar was listed as QB4 on the Steelers’ first depth chart behind Mason Rudolph and Will Howard who were listed at QB2 and QB3, respectively. He had a pair of throws o the first day of camp that had everyone in attendance talking – two rips over the middle of the field, one of which was a touchdown to Robert Tonyan to close practice. He also threw a long touchdown to Cole Burgess among several other throws where he has showcased his timing on throws over the middle. Allar will take the field as a Steeler for the first time next Thursday when the Steelers host the Green Bay Packers in the preseason opener. Let us know what you think in the comments . full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA - MAY 27: Brock Lampe #46 of the New England Patriots during New England Patriots OTA on May 27, 2026, at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts. Sportswire) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks announced one signing on Thursday afternoon, adding fullback Brock Lampe, who went undrafted out of Northern Illinois last year. To make room, tight end Lance Mason was waived. Mason, who also went undrafted, signed with Seattle in May and participated in rookie minicamp, organized team activites (OTA’s) as well as the first week of training camp. Lampe played his entire collegiate career with the Huskies, spending three season under then head coach Thomas Hammock, who joined the Seahawks as a senior offensive assistant/running backs coach in the offseason. He began his college careeer as a linebacker, before switching to fullback ahead of his sophomore season in 2022. Standing in at 6’1, 249lbs, he profiles as a traditional physical blocker, who helped anchor a rushing attack that averaged an outlandish 203.8 rushing yards per game in his senior season. After going undrafted, Lampe signed with the New England Patriots, but missed his entire rookie campaign while on injured reserve, after suffering a leg injury in training camp. He returned for OTA’s, but was waived by the team on July 22. Robbie Ouzts, who ended last season with a neck injury sustained in the NFC Divisional Round against the San Francisco 49ers, has missed the last several practices and his injury status remains uncertain. Mike Macdonald does not have any updates regarding his health and he has not disclosed the injury.
