title: Jahmyr Gibbs' Lions extension: Answering all the key questions
summary: Answering all the key questions about Gibbs' record contract extension, who's next for the Lions, fantasy impact and more.
full_text:
DETROIT -- Cha-ching! Detroit Lions star Jahmyr Gibbs is now the NFL's highest-paid running back .

 Few players in league history have had a better start to their NFL career than the 24-year-old Gibbs, who has earned three straight Pro Bowl nods and is an early betting favorite to be the 2026 Offensive Player of the Year.

 Gibbs is clearly the man in Detroit. He will now have the keys to the offense under first-year Lions offensive coordinator Drew Petzing, while handling the bulk of the carries.

 

 Despite a 9-8 finish in which Detroit missed the postseason last season, Gibbs accounted for 1,839 scrimmage yards (fifth most in the NFL) and 18 touchdowns (second most) in 2025.

 His 3,580 rushing yards are also the 22nd most for a player's first three seasons since yardage statistics were first recorded in 1932, according to ESPN Research.

 Still, he's not satisfied, and says he thinks fans haven't seen the best version of him yet.

 Now with his extension in hand, he'll probably reach that peak form in a Lions uniform.

 "Nah. I don't think so," Gibbs told ESPN when asked if he's played his best football yet. "Me personally, I could've done a lot of stuff throughout the year to get us out of some holes."

 ESPN Lions reporter Eric Woodyard, NFL insider Ben Solak, analytics writer Seth Walder and senior fantasy football writer Mike Clay break down what the new deal means.

 

 

 Why did the Lions extend Gibbs now? 

 It's a no-brainer. Gibbs is one of the most exciting and explosive players in the league and the Lions have secured him for his prime years, which is crucial for a running back since they typically decline at a faster rate compared to other positions because of the workload. So, why not now?

 This new deal also ended a hold-in situation in which Gibbs sat out six consecutive practices at training camp while the new deal was being negotiated. It comes after the Falcons and RB Bijan Robinson agreed to a three-year extension Tuesday morning that includes $51 million guaranteed, setting the stage for Gibbs' new deal.

 Furthering Gibbs' case, he's off to a historic start in his NFL career, scoring the most touchdowns (49) of any player in their first three seasons. He is expected to take on a larger workload in 2026 after the Lions traded his backfield mate David Montgomery to the Houston Texans this offseason. His production as a versatile threat is much deserving as a foundational, long-term part of the organization. -- Woodyard 

 

 What does this mean for other Lions eligible for extensions, such as TE Sam LaPorta and DB  Brian Branch ? 

 Not much. Gibbs' record-setting contract extension is no surprise to anyone. He earned it and the organization had prepared for it.

 

 The Lions didn't splurge on any free agent signings this offseason. General manager Brad Holmes said the team was fully aware of its financial constraints, with looming extensions already being put in place for not only Gibbs, but for LaPorta and Branch as well -- two more players they hope to retain.

 With Gibbs' deal done, the question now is who's next. Detroit swears by its draft-and-develop approach under Holmes and head coach Dan Campbell, and plans to keep as many of its key drafted players around for as long as possible. This, the team hopes, will keep its Super Bowl window open for the foreseeable future. -- Woodyard 

 

 Is it risky to invest so much financially into Gibbs, given running backs' short careers and early peaks? 

 Every top-of-market contract has some inherent risk to it. What if the player gets hurt? What if he doesn't dominate the position, instead remaining one of the five or 10 best, failing to outperform players who are on lesser deals? But specific to the running back position, it's hard to get overly concerned about Gibbs' current state.

 Gibbs has at least 300 touches in each of the past two seasons but never more than 250 carries, which minimizes the amount of big contact he's taking between the tackles. He was not heavily used in college (under 500 total touches) and entered the league as a 21-year-old rookie. With three more years attached to his remaining two seasons, this extension will take him to the age of 28. The Lions have every reason to believe Gibbs will be an elite back for the next several years, and they have paid him as such. -- Solak 

 

 Is Gibbs actually worth paying more than Bijan Robinson? 

 Paying top-of-the-market price on a deal for Gibbs works for the same three reasons it does for Robinson:

 
 He's a legitimately elite running back 
 He's particularly dangerous as a receiver, which is what matters most 
 He's only 24 years old 
 
 Gibbs' numbers last season weren't quite as good as Robinson's (168 rush yards over expected to Robinson's 249 and 126 receiving yards over expected to Robinson's 201, per NFL Next Gen Stats) but I feel these are the best two running backs in the NFL. Though this is top-of-the-market money for a running back today, it's cheaper than what running backs were paid in the past. For example, in 2015, Adrian Peterson and Marshawn Lynch signed deals that were worth the equivalent of $29.4 million and $25.2 million per year, respectively, in 2026's cap environment. -- Walder 

 

 What should we expect from Gibbs in fantasy this season? 

 Clay's 2026 projection: 283 carries, 1,374 yards, 15 TDs; 86 targets, 68 receptions, 547 yards, 3 TDs

 Gibbs has finished in the top 10 among running backs in yards per carry, routes, targets, receptions, touchdowns and fantasy points in each of his first three seasons. In fact, his 38 touchdowns over the past two seasons are four more than any other player. Though Gibbs has finished as a top-three fantasy back in each of the past two years, he has yet to finish a season higher than seventh in touches. That very well could change this season with Montgomery no longer in the mix. Gibbs is one of the NFL's top playmakers in one of its best offenses. He's a strong option with the first pick of fantasy drafts. -- Clay

title: Why Packers are connecting with DC Gannon's 'turnt up' vibe
summary: The former Cardinals head coach is bringing a different approach to the defense, and players are buying in.
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- There are two Jonathan Gannons on the Green Bay Packers  coaching staff. There's the one underneath the floppy hat and behind the sunglasses who strolls onto the practice field like he doesn't have a care in the world. And the one his players describe.

 And more than one used the same word to do so.

 "He [is] a little crazy, you know," safety Javon Bullard said.

 "He's got like a crazy little energy," safety Evan Williams said.

 

 Other players have offered similar descriptions.

 "Oh yeah, J.G., man, he just turnt up, man," linebacker Zaire Franklin said.

 It sounds like he's nothing like the guy in the infamous, cringeworthy video from a team meeting early in his tenure as head coach of the Arizona Cardinals , during which he asked players whether they drove to the facility or took the bus, seemingly leaving them uninspired.

 "The 'crazy' things ... I don't know who said that, but [I know what] they're probably alluding to," Gannon said. "I do believe that words paint pictures, so there's certain things in the install or certain things when we're going over a tape review, I'm probably using an example that's non-football-related that hopefully hits their brain and they can understand it a little bit better or it kinda cements it in: This has to get done. And I sometimes will use some examples that are probably a little bit out there, so maybe that's what they're talking about."

 

 Whatever the method, Gannon seems to be striking a chord with his new players, many of whom had close relationships with Gannon's popular predecessor, Jeff Hafley. Seemingly no one was more universally liked and respected in the locker room than Hafley, who is now the head coach of the Miami Dolphins .

 So while there has been much talk about how Gannon's scheme (a 3-4 base) differs from Hafley (who used a 4-3), it may be just as important to Gannon to connect with his players like Hafley did.

 Star edge rusher Micah Parsons  spoke glowingly about Hafley after last season, saying, "He's another guy I can't wait to have another year with."

 This was before Hafley got the job in Miami. And when presented with the notion that Hafley could leave for a head coaching job, it was as if Parsons was trying to speak it into non-existence.

 "Nah, Haf ain't going nowhere," Parsons said at the time.

 To be sure, coaches aren't employed to win popularity contests, and being known as a player's coach doesn't always ring true with players.

 "Anytime I need to get cussed out or need a chewing, he's going to be on me," cornerback Brandon Cisse said.

 

 Gannon has been especially popular in the safety room. So far in camp, he has shown a willingness to use three safeties -- usually Bullard, Xavier McKinney and Williams -- on the field together. While Hafley did that with Bullard in the nickel, Gannon appears to have taken it a step further by giving all three safeties more responsibilities and more freedom.

 "I'd probably say the biggest thing right now, obviously we got this three-safety look going on, which we love it right now," McKinney said early in camp. "I think we're gonna continue to love it. I think it's gonna progress and get better as we learn different spots. We're all able to move around and do different things."

 Only Franklin and defensive tackle Javon Hargrave had any previous experience with Gannon. Franklin was on the Colts when Gannon served as their defensive backs coach from 2018 to 2020. Hargrave and Gannon were together in Philadelphia when Gannon was the defensive coordinator in 2021 and 2022.

 Franklin predicted early on that his fellow defenders like McKinney, Parsons and linebacker Edgerrin Cooper would quickly discover what he likes about Gannon.

 "He's gonna bring that fire, he's gonna bring that energy." Franklin said. "I think he recognizes who we have in that room, and he wants the players to play. And I think that's just special.

 "Some guys want to put themselves in that position, and they want their name in the media. Whereas J.G. understands, 'Look, let the players play' -- let us get in the best position, let Cooper and let 'X' be him, let Zaire be him, let Micah be Micah. So that's what's special about it, and you know he's gonna bring that energy for sure. He's gonna make sure we turnt up for sure."

 So even if Gannon seems a little monotonous in public, his players insist that's not what he's like behind the scenes.

 "I feel like you need that as a D coordinator; you need to be a little on edge," Williams said. "If you're a D coordinator, and you're fully stable and emotionally flatlined, I don't need that."

full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Green Bay Packers ' camp is taking place in Green Bay, Wisconsin, and Packers reporter Rob Demovsky has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Packers camp. We will update this file often. Will the revamped WR corps help QB Jordan Love and the offense take another step? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news out of Packers' camp 
 
 Micah Parsons: Playing vs. Cowboys in Week 6 'realistic' 
 Packers RT changes last name to Bako-Bewele to honor heritage 
 Packers star TE Tucker Kraft activated off PUP after ACL recovery 
 Better, worse or the same: Packers defense 
 Packers CEO: Team needs financial bump to stay competitive 
 

 

 Thursday, Aug. 6 

 It would be hard to blame running back  MarShawn Lloyd for getting excited after he scored a touchdown in practice on Thursday.

 
And it would be hard to blame coach Matt LaFleur for telling his oft-injured running back to find a different way to celebrate it.

 
After he caught a touchdown pass from  Jordan Love , Lloyd celebrated with a backflip in the end zone.

 
When the period ended, LaFleur walked over to Lloyd on the sideline.

 
"He said it was cool," Lloyd said. "But he said let's not do that."

 
Receiver Christian Watson has used the same move to celebrate.

 
"And he told him the same thing: Stop doing them," Lloyd said.

 
Lloyd, a third-round pick in 2024, has already made it further into camp than he did last season, when a recurring hamstring injury kept him out the entire season. Previously, he had hip and ankle injuries along with appendicitis that limited him to 10 snaps as a rookie.

 
"Got a long way to go, but when he's out there, he's making plays and he's turning heads," GM Brian Gutekunst said before Thursday's practice. "He always kind of has done that since he's been here, when he's been able to be out there. So yeah, excited for where he's going."

 More observations: 

 
 It's looking more and more like Skyy Moore will have a spot on the opening-day, 53-man roster. And not just as a return specialist. The Packers have liked what they've seen in him as a receiver. The Packers gave Moore a $1 million signing bonus in free agency, but they've cut players with similar bonuses before; kicker Brandon McManus was released this offseason only weeks after he was paid a $1 million roster bonus. "I think Skyy's going to help us as a returner and as a receiver," Gutekunst said. "I expect him to be part of our squad moving forward." 
 Speaking of backup receivers, Isaiah Neyor made an impressive touchdown catch from backup QB Kyle McCord . Neyor fought off tight coverage from safety Kitan Oladapo and spun in the air to bring in the ball. Neyor, who was on the practice squad last season, and undrafted rookie J. Michael Sturdivant could be fighting for the last receiver spot on the roster. Studivant also has been impressive. 
 The coaches want to take a long look at offensive lineman Jacob Monk . With left guard Aaron Banks (knee) still not doing any team drills, Monk has been with the starters. He had been mostly at left guard but moved over to right guard Thursday, which meant Anthony Belton bounced out to right tackle, where regular starter Zach Bako-Bewele (knee) is also not doing team drills. "I love Monk's playstyle," offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich said. "He's got the right mindset. He tries to get after people and plays the game the right way. So I've been happy with how he's played so far this camp." 
 Running back Josh Jacobs (groin) missed his first practice of camp. However, the injury is not expected to be a long-term concern. 
 The Packers closed Thursday's practice to fans but are expected to have nearly 60,000 in Lambeau Field for Friday's annual Family Night practice. 
 J.J. Watt was a visitor at practice. The Milwaukee-area native never got the chance to play for his home-state team, although he was reportedly interested in doing so before he signed with the Cardinals in 2021. Watt is expected to be part of the CBS broadcast crew for the Week 1 game against the Vikings. 
 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 

 While much has been made about rookie kicker Trey Smack 's early struggles in training camp (see Monday's camp report), special teams coordinator Cam Achord explained why those practice kicks are only a small part of the evaluation.

 
Some of that has to do with the wind. Smack kicked in one especially windy day on Ray Nitschke Field, and Achord -- who is new to town -- was surprised at the difference in the wind on the practice field compared to inside Lambeau Field.

 
"We go in there and it's like, wow, you don't feel anything," Achord said. "So I don't put as much stock on the practice stuff as I will in the stadium stuff."

 
Lambeau Field has tricky winds of its own, but Achord said he believes gusts of 25 miles per hour outside "really feels like a light breeze almost inside. Whereas at practice you're out there and you're looking at the flags and it's moving. You're like, whoa, it's a tough day to kick."

 
Add into the mix that regular long snapper Matt Orzech has been unavailable because of a calf injury and holder Daniel Whelan is getting used to putting the ball down the way Smack likes it, which coach Matt LaFleur said is different than how previous kicker Brandon McManus wanted it held.

 
Achord was asked to explain the nuances of holding and didn't just explain it, he demonstrated it in the Packers' media auditorium. That demonstration can be seen here:

 

 Achord, defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon and offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich spoke to reporters on Wednesday, when the players were off.

 More observations: 

 
 Achord might be the only Packers coach ever to wear cleats to practice. He said he started wearing them in 2018, when he joined the Patriots' staff because he likes to get hands on with his players: "I got tired of getting thrown on the ground doing gunner releases with Matt Slater," he said. " Justin Bethel broke my nose. ... I'm 165 pounds and they're athletes, and I tell them like, quit pulling me like you're gonna pull a coach. I was like, pull me like you're gonna pull the freaking vise, yank. So they started yanking and broke my nose, fell down. So after that, I started wearing cleats just for better grip." 
 LaFleur has rarely played veteran starters during the preseason but with a new defensive coordinator in Gannon, might LaFleur want his players to get some exhibition game reps? Said Gannon: "I'll probably punt that one to Matt what we're going to do. How do I say this the right way to you guys? I think that our players have earned the right to play our stuff and get really good at it and go play." 
 Gannon on his plans for Micah Parsons when he returns from his ACL rehab: "We were talking the other day, he could see himself in a bunch of different spots in different calls, so that's kinda cool. Then it will be our job to make sure he gets his touches, which he will." 
 Six practices in, and MarShawn Lloyd is still healthy. That's an accomplishment for the third-year pro, who has played in exactly one NFL game and missed all of last season after getting injured on the first day of padded practices last summer. Asked whether his confidence in Lloyd has grown, offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich said: "Every day he's out there and doing it, I have a little bit more. ... But I think this preseason's going to be a huge telling point of what…

title: Texans' Ryans uses Artemis II space launch to set expectations
summary: Houston's coach used NASA's trip around the moon as inspiration to rally his team.
full_text:
HOUSTON -- Before training camp began, DeMeco Ryans set the tone for his team with a different approach.

 The Houston Texans  coach delivered a speech with a picture of Artemis II towering over him in bold letters. The names from NASA's crew of Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover (pilot), Christina Koch and Jeremy Hansen sat beneath Ryans as he talked about the launch on April 1 and flight around the moon, marking the first time since Apollo 17 in 1972.

 Ryans used the 10-day mission to fly around the moon before returning safely to Earth as an example of how the crew "went further" than anyone else. But he also highlighted how they laid the groundwork for years to make that moment possible.

 He compared the takeoff to what Houston could do this upcoming season. How this team could reach heights that it never has. Not only reaching the AFC Championship Game for the first time in franchise history, but winning the Super Bowl. 

 

 "The preparation that it took for Artemis II to launch, it took three years for that mission to take place, and that's the beauty of it," Ryans said. 

 Owner Cal McNair has been on record saying Houston wants to play "in the very last game," and All-Pro defensive end  Will Anderson Jr . called the Texans a "Super Bowl team" this offseason.

 "When you guys asked me about expectations, the only thing I know is high expectations," Ryans said. "That's why we do what we do to achieve the ultimate goal."

 But with the Texans' lofty goals comes the mentality of daily submission to the process.

 "The expectation is to take it one day at a time, one play at a time," quarterback C.J. Stroud said. "And then see where we are at the end of camp."

 The roster has the necessary pieces on both sides of the ball to reach the heights the franchise has failed to capture in years prior.

 Houston has a capable quarterback who has played at a Pro Bowl level at times. The running game has a lead back in David Montgomery , a more physical offensive line with the addition of first-round pick Keylan Rutledge  (center), offensive tackle Braden Smith and former All-Pro guard Wyatt Teller . Wideout Nico Collins is a multiple time Pro Bowler.

 

 The defense is highly decorated with three All-Pros in cornerback Derek Stingley Jr ., Danielle Hunter  and Anderson. There are three other Pro Bowlers in linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair , cornerback Kamari Lassiter and safety Calen Bullock . Each level has difference-makers, which helped them allow the fewest yards (277.2 per game) and second-fewest points (17.4) in the NFL last season.

 But the coaches and players have left those achievements in the past, shifting their focus toward a Super Bowl while putting a massive emphasis on the daily process.

 "You just have to realize that it's a marathon," Lassiter said. "It's a long season. Training camp is the beginning, but every day you want to get better. If we have a common goal, and we're all trying to reach that goal, you take each and every day with a sense of gratitude and you attack it like you don't have the next one."

 The push for goals never met is what's fueling this season, but they won't rush through the importance of the process.

 "You want to do things, you want to go places you've never been before, there's a lot of preparation in the background to prepare to launch," Ryans said. "We don't launch tomorrow. You don't just get there just by talking about it. You got to put the work in, and that's the main message."

 Thursday, Aug. 6 

 Starting quarterback Daniel Jones had one of his best days in Thursday's evening practice, connecting on a number of aggressive, downfield throws. But the same could not be said of the quarterbacks behind him on the depth chart.

 Anthony Richardson Sr . and Riley Leonard , locked in a battle for the backup job, have yet to establish the consistency that coach Shane Steichen is seeking.  "The guy that's most consistent is going to win that job," Steichen said. "Those guys are battling. It's back and forth right now." He added, "There's been flashes, but yeah, there's work to done for sure."

 
 The Colts' kicking battle continues, with Spencer Shrader and Blake Grupe each kicking extensively in Thursday's practice. Both had a pair of misses, from 57 and 61 yards in full-team action. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 One week into camp and perhaps the biggest question is not a question at all.

 Quarterback Daniel Jones has not missed a single snap with the first-team offense and has not taken any days off from practice. This comes in spite of him only recently being fully cleared to practice in full-team drills following his Achilles tendon tear in December. If there were any uncertainties entering this camp, Jones has put them to rest.

 "I've felt good through the whole camp so far," Jones said. "I knew I would. You try to push yourself in the rehab in preparation for camp, knowing what to expect. I felt really good and I stay on the recovery part of it to make sure I'm available and out here every day."

 The Colts are five practices in and there are no known plans to pull back on Jones' workload.

 
 Play of the day: Tight end Tyler Warren hauled in a leaping catch on a deep ball from Jones, taking the ball away from safety Cam Bynum . 
 Cornerback Sauce Gardner missed Tuesday's practice with an illness, according to a team spokesman. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 Cornerbacks Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward have been making life difficult for the team's wide receivers so far in camp, much to the Colts' contentment.

 Gardner and Ward are expected to be among the best cornerback combos in the league this season if they can both remain on the field. That was not the case last season, when they spent just one full game on the field together because of respective injuries.

 The length of both players has been especially challenging for the receivers, a group that is trying to find its way with the No. 3 spot still up for grabs.

 "When you can go up against two of the best in the league in practice every day, it's going to make everybody better," coach Shane Steichen said.

 

 
 Steichen said he still does not have any clarity on when No. 1 receiver Alec Pierce might return to the lineup after offseason ankle surgery. Pierce, according to GM Chris Ballard, will spend "a week or two" on the physically unable to perform list. But it's not clear that he's closer even as the Colts begin their second week of camp. 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 The Colts spent most of Saturday's workout focused on red zone play, with the offense and defense more or less playing to a draw in terms of success. Among the highlights was tight end Tyler Warren 's leaping catch in the end zone for a touchdown from quarterback Daniel Jones . Another impressive completion came when Jones delivered a strike to receiver Josh Downs in the corner of the end zone.

 But the defense held its own, too, forcing Jones and quarterback Anthony Richardson Sr . to scramble out of the pocket multiple times in 7-on-7 and in full-team periods.

 Additionally, cornerback Sauce Gardner had an athletic pass deflection against Downs to stop a red zone threat.

 More observations: 

 
 Coach Shane Steichen missed practice with an undisclosed personal matter. 
 WR Nick Westbrook-Ikhine emphasized his intent to be a reliable blocker for running back Jonathan Taylor , a quality he said he learned early in his career while blocking for Derrick Henry during their time together with the Tennessee Titans . "That's something you've definitely got to take pride in," he said. 
 

 

 Friday, July 31 

 Owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon spoke to reporters for the first time in several months and revealed the details of her address to the team this week. On the heels of last season's massive collapse -- a seven-game losing streak to end the Colts' season -- Irsay-Gordon emphasized the need to finish.

 "As we reflected on last season, this one phrase just kept coming to my mind," she said. "And that was 'Find a way.' So that was the mantra that we settled on for this season. And we came to 'find a way' because we thought about what are the qualities that successful people have? And those qualities are consistency, those qualities are resilience."

 The Colts lost quarterback Daniel Jones and players such as  Sauce Gardner and DeForest Buckner down the stretch last season. But Irsay-Gordon emphasized that injuries would not be a cop-out this season, when general manager Chris Ballard and coach Shane Steichen are considered to be on the hot seat.

 More observations from the day: 

 
 Rookie middle linebacker CJ Allen returned to the lineup after sustaining a calf tweak during his preparation for camp last week. He spent the first two days of camp on the physically unable to perform list but immediately stepped into the starting lineup on Friday. 
 The Colts endured underwhelming quarterback play on Friday from Jones, Anthony Richardson Sr . and Riley Leonard with errant throws, bobbled snaps and questionable decisions ruling the day. 
 

 

 Thursday, July 30 

 Cornerback Charvarius Ward has had a strong start to camp, something that is especially notable given where he was just seven months ago: On the verge of retirement.

 Ward previously addressed his change of heart, deciding to return after the 2024 death of his infant daughter and a series of concussions in 2025 nearly pushed him to step away from the NFL. He now says he was "probably 85% sure I was going to retire. But I found a different why, a different purpose. Doing it for Junior [his son], doing it for Amani, my daughter. They bring me joy. They bring a smile to my face."

 Ward, 30, added, "I feel good, I've got a lot of energy. I feel like I still belong out here."

 More observations: 

 
 The Colts are taking a closer look at second-year safety Hunter Wohler , who sustained a season-ending injury in camp as a rookie last year. He's in a competition with rookie A.J. Haulcy , who was impressive in the spring and looked to have the edge at strong safety. This will be a position battle to watch. 
 The Colts have a legitimate kicking competition between Spencer Shrader , who had a season-ending knee injury last season, and former…

title: Can Colts recapture '25 magic? Taylor deal reflects optimism
summary: The Colts believe they can recapture their early-season success from 2025, but they couldn't do it without Jonathan Taylor.
full_text:
WESTFIELD, Ind. -- If you want to know about an NFL team's priorities, it can be instructive to simply examine where it spends its money.

 For the Indianapolis Colts , their 2026 offseason spending was directed toward the pieces of their roster that represent their biggest reasons for optimism.

 In the spring, Indianapolis signed receiver and deep threat extraordinaire Alec Pierce to a four-year, $116 million deal. Days later, the Colts agreed to a new contract with rejuvenated quarterback Daniel Jones at two years for $88 million.

 And, on Thursday, the Colts locked up another critical offensive piece, with big-play running back Jonathan Taylor agreeing to terms on a two-year extension worth $44 million. The contract is the third-largest deal for a running back in NFL history.

 Their philosophy isn't difficult to decipher.

 In Weeks 1 through 10 of 2025, the Colts were 8-2 and playing at a level rarely seen even when Hall of Fame quarterback Peyton Manning starred for the team. Indianapolis led the NFL in offensive expected points added (103.8), points per game (32.1), yards per game (396.9) and yards per play (6.4) before falling off a proverbial cliff late in the season.

 

 They had seemingly perfected a formula with proven success in the NFL: Running an efficient passing game with Jones at the controls, mixing in explosive deep shots to Pierce, who led the NFL in yards per catch, then allowing Taylor to bludgeon defenders until they inevitably yielded one of his breakaway runs.

 Likewise, the Colts were running away from opponents, posting a league-high 11.5-point margin per game.

 But a seven-game losing streak to end the season represented a stunning unraveling fueled by a season-ending injury to Jones and the loss of key defensive players.

 The Colts, however, are holding out hope they can recapture who they were before that collapse. And in their estimation, they will do that by doubling down on their offensive stars.

 "What we saw in that first half is we were, in a record way, dominating offensively," principal owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon said after the season.

 That formula likely would not have worked had any of those pieces been missing. That is why, even amid a season that is seen as make-or-break for the Colts -- with coach Shane Steichen and general manager Chris Ballard considered to be on the hot seat and several veteran players facing uncertain futures -- locking up Taylor proved to be a priority.

 Without Taylor in the backfield, Jones' play-action passing would be much less potent. Without Taylor, defenses would be more comfortable dropping defenders into coverage to safeguard themselves against Pierce's speed. Without Taylor, linebackers might've been more likely to focus on rookie tight end Tyler Warren , who was dominating the middle of the field.

 So much could have been different if not for Taylor, already the second-leading rusher in Colts history behind Hall of Fame back Edgerrin James. Even in an era when running backs are often taken for granted, Taylor is the piece that made it all come together.

 

 His ability to turn 3-yard rushes into 5-yard gains, and to make mere chunk plays into game-breaking runs that broke opponents proved to be the Colts' secret sauce.

 When Taylor got bottled up on an inside run against the Atlanta Falcons last season in Week 10, then somehow bounced outside for an 83-yard touchdown, it left even his teammates in awe. The play was all Taylor.

 "He's our home run hitter," former Colts linebacker Zaire Franklin marveled afterward. "He's our knockout punch. He's the best weapon in the league."

 Taylor is among a group of backs who believe they are changing perceptions of the position as a collective afterthought. Derrick Henry , Saquon Barkley , Bijan Robinson , Jahmyr Gibbs and others are making the NFL rethink its attitudes toward running backs.

 For the Colts, there is no attitude adjustment necessary. They demonstrated Thursday just how important Taylor is to their offensive formula.

 Jaguars' Travis Hunter feeling faster after 10-pound weight gain 
 
 

 Thursday, Aug. 6 
 Talks between the Jaguars and receiver  Parker Washington 's camp on a contract extension remain active, but the fourth-year player out of Penn State isn't focusing on when a deal could get done and isn't upset that an agreement hasn't yet been reached.

 "It's there and it's a conversation, but my focus is just coming out here and I need to make plays for Trevor [Lawrence] ," Washington said Thursday. "So that's my mindset and that's how I'm going to attack it. I'm not going to step on my agent's toes. They can have those conversations. I'm going to come out here and do my job."

 Jaguars general manager James Gladstone said early in the offseason the team was working on extensions with Washington and tight end Brenton Strange . They reached a deal with Strange, signing him to a three-year extension worth up to $48 million in June but have yet to finalize anything with Washington.

 Washington was asked about his reaction to the four-year, $140 million extension  with $108 million guaranteed that receiver Zay Flowers agreed to with Baltimore and said he was happy for Flowers, who was the 22nd overall pick in 2023.

 "The receiver market is a little crazy and you see guys getting their opportunities and getting paid, I mean, that's cool," said Washington, whom the Jaguars drafted in the sixth round in 2023. "But like I said, for me, I just want to go out here and be my best self and just attack it."

 

 More observations: 

 
 OL Emmanuel Pregnon was injured during 11-on-11 and received treatment off to the side. He remained at practice but did not participate in any more team work. 
 S Preston Hodge intercepted QB Joey Aguilar and LB Ventrell Miller punched the ball away from RB Ameer Abdullah and recovered the fumble in 11-on-11 work. 
 The Jaguars will have a mock game on Friday morning at the team's practice facility. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 Very good day for the defense on Tuesday in the Jaguars' second day in full pads.

 Safeties Antonio Johnson and Eric Murray and cornerback Jarrian Jones intercepted passes, Jones broke up another in the end zone, and linebacker Branson Combs broke up a pass on the goal line. Cornerback Jabbar Muhammad also had tight coverage on Travis Hunter on a throw into the end zone and forced an incompletion.

 Johnson's interception came off Trevor Lawrence while Murray and Jones picked off Nick Mullens .

 More observations: 

 
 Hunter had 17 snaps (10 defense, 7 offense) in 11-on-11 work. He has totaled 86 snaps (51 defense, 35 offense) through six practices. 
 LB Jared Bartlett was taken off the field after suffering a leg injury, which leaves the team down two linebackers ( Jack Kiser suffered a right knee injury on the first day of camp). The team is also limiting  Foyesade Oluokun 's snaps in team work, so the Jaguars could be looking to add at that spot. 
 RB Chris Rodriguez Jr . did not participate in Tuesday's practice as part of the team's plan to ramp up his participation. Rodriguez, who missed almost all of the spring with a left foot injury, did participate in Monday's practice. 
 DE Arik Armstead had a veteran day off on Tuesday, his second of camp. 
 

 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 Anton Harrison , who has started 48 games at right tackle since being drafted 27th overall in 2023, has spent the past three practices working at left tackle as part of the Jaguars' philosophy of cross-training offensive linemen.

 Coach Liam Coen didn't rule out that being a permanent change, though.

 "If that ends up sticking, then hopefully that's a good thing for us," Coen said after Monday's practice. "And I think he's put together five good practices so far that you're pleased with seeing the consistency."

 Monday's practice was the first in full pads and Harrison won all four of his one-on-one pass rush reps, including two against defensive end Josh Hines-Allen , the franchise's sack leader (61).

 Cole Van Lanen was the team's starting left tackle at the end of the 2025 season and the Jaguars signed him to three-year, $51 million extension in January. However, he has yet to practice because he's still recovering from a knee injury he suffered in the regular-season finale. He is expected to return at some point in camp.

 Walker Little  -- who lost the starting job at left tackle to Van Lanen last season -- had been the left tackle for the first two camp practices and is now working at right tackle.

 

 More observations: 

 
 WR Brian Thomas Jr . has followed up his impressive spring with a good start to camp. He had the play of the day on Monday with a one-handed catch down the sideline in 11-on-11. CB Montaric Brown had sticky coverage but Thomas grabbed Trevor Lawrence 's throw with his right arm while fending off Brown with his left. 
 Relatively quiet day for CB/WR Travis Hunter . He had 13 snaps in 11-on-11 (seven on defense and six on offense). He was targeted once by QB Nick Mullens , but there was a miscommunication on the route. Hunter cut the route short while Mullens threw long. 
 

 

 

 Sunday, Aug. 2 
 Travis Hunter had one of the most impressive training camp practices of his career on Sunday, making two catches on offense and intercepting a pass on defense.

 His first catch came on a deep over route on a throw from Trevor Lawrence . He had a step on cornerback Jarrian Jones when he caught the ball and accelerated down the sideline for what would have been a big gain.

 He made his second catch, also from Lawrence, over his left shoulder down the right sideline with a defensive back on his back.

 "The deep reception was awesome to see," offensive coordinator Grant Udinski said. "He's continued to progress from a route technique fundamental standpoint, but also a knowledge of the offense and just the system in general.

 "When he has the ball in his hands, he can create something special. He can make guys miss. He has a great awareness of defenders and space out there on the field, but he also has great ball skills. So those things kind of pop off the tape."

 Hunter intercepted Nick Mullens ' pass to tight end Quintin Morris , jumping in front of the throw and returning the ball for what would have been a touchdown.

 More observations from the day: 

 
 RB Chris Rodriguez Jr . participated in 11-on-11 work for the first time in camp. His snaps were limited but he did get two carries as part of a gradual ramp-up of participating that coach Liam Coen said would be the plan. Rodriguez missed the spring after undergoing surgery on his left foot. 
 WR Parker Washington had one of the plays of the day when he made a sliding catch in the end zone on a deep throw from Lawrence during an 11-on-11 move-the-ball period. 
 The Jaguars will be in full pads for the first time on Monday. 
 

 

 Friday, July 31 
 Cornerback Jarrian Jones had the best performance of any defensive player so far in camp with a pair of interceptions and a pass breakup on Friday. Jones intercepted quarterback  Trevor Lawrence 's sideline pass to…

title: 2026 Kansas City Chiefs training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Chiefs training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Kansas City Chiefs ' camp is taking place at Missouri Western State University in St. Joseph, Missouri, and Chiefs reporter Nate Taylor has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Chiefs camp. We will update this file often. Can coach Andy Reid get the Chiefs back into the playoffs? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive into all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Chiefs camp 
 
 Rookie wideout Cyrus Allen an early star of Chiefs training camp 
 Chiefs' Reid: Eric Bieniemy's wife out of ICU, 'doing great' 
 Chiefs' Mahomes fully cleared for camp, feeling 'amazing' 
 As training camp opens, Chiefs point to brighter future in 2026 
 
 
 Thursday, Aug. 6 

 The Chiefs had a light practice Thursday, the first such on-field work after three consecutive days in pads. The most significant change was that backup quarterback Justin Fields had his first 11-on-11 reps with the first-team offense, an indication that he might be the starter when the Chiefs have their preseason opener next Saturday against the Los Angeles Rams .

 "I've been learning a lot since I've been here and I'm excited to learn more, especially [coach Andy Reid] and [quarterback Patrick Mahomes ]," Fields said. "They definitely taught me a lot."

 Reid has yet to share if Mahomes, who has surgery in December to repair the torn ACL and LCL in his left knee, will be held out of the preseason, which would be a first in his 10-year career. During Thursday's practice, Fields spent time completing passes to running back Kenneth Walker III and receivers Rashee Rice , Tyquan Thornton and Andrew Armstrong .

 "I'm ready to get back on the field and in game mode, to be honest," Fields said. "It should be fun for the guys that are going to get out there and especially the rookies."

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 
 Rashee Rice , the Chiefs' No. 1 receiver, participated in 11-on-11 repetitions, a positive sign that his acclimation process is going well. In May, Rice underwent surgery on his right knee to remove loose debris that was causing inflammation. Since camp began, the Chiefs have been cautious with Rice's participation.

 Most of Rice's work was during the red zone period, where he had several short receptions, including a bubble screen on the perimeter and a touchdown in the back of the end zone. When Mahomes targeted Rice in the back corner of the end zone, Rice couldn't make a leaping, contested catch against cornerback Nohl Williams .

 It's clear Rice will need time to get into true football shape, as he showed fatigue before the long-drive drill, the final 11-on-11 repetitions. During that period, Rice was held out of the first-team offense's 12 repetitions.

 "He got a lot of good reps today, which is important," Reid said of Rice. "We've just got to ease him back in and just keep working. We know he's a good player. He actually got better as the practice went on, so that was a good thing."

 Other observations:  

 
 Linebacker Drue Tranquill missed his first practice of camp with lower back spasms. During the second half of Wednesday's work, Tranquill did some light strength work off the side with the training staff. 
 The other players who missed Wednesday's on-field session were cornerback Kristian Fulton (hip), linebacker Jeffrey Bassa (strained groin), defensive end Ashton Gillotte (strained right hamstring), defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (right knee) and receivers Cyrus Allen (left shin) and Xavier Worthy (sprained right shoulder). 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 

 For the second consecutive day in pads, Kahlil Benson , the undrafted rookie right tackle from Indiana, performed well, even better than Monday, after once again receiving all of the repetitions with the first-team offense.

 In the first 11-on-11 period, Benson showed strong run-blocking skills by executing a double-team to move defensive tackle Khyiris Tonga back. The repetition finished with Benson also blocking linebacker Nick Bolton , which created more space on the right side of the field for running back Kenneth Walker III . A few minutes later, Benson blocked defensive end Felix Anudike-Uzomah in pass protection for quarterback Patrick Mahomes to connect with receiver Tyquan Thornton for a completion for more than 30 yards.

 "He's done great," Walker said of Benson. "We've got pads on now and you get to see how well he's doing out there. He's going to have a great impact on this team."

 Benson's work, on the field and in meetings, has pushed him to have true competition with Jaylon Moore , the five-year veteran, for the starting right tackle role.

 In the final 11-on-11 period, Benson didn't lose any of the five repetitions with the first-team offense. His matchups included Anudike-Uzomah, pass rusher Chris Jones and rookie defensive end R Mason Thomas .

 "We'll give you a chance here to learn, but if you start making [mistakes] consistently, then we've got a problem," Reid said Monday of Benson. "But he's been doing a good job. There's a hiccup here or there, but he fixes them normally."

 More observations: 

 
 The players who missed Tuesday's practice were cornerback Kristian Fulton (hip), defensive end Ashton Gillotte (strained right hamstring), defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (right knee) and receivers Cyrus Allen (left shin) and Xavier Worthy (sprained right shoulder). 
 Receiver Rashee Rice (right knee) participated in 7-on-7 repetitions for the second straight day, this time catching a short pass from Mahomes against zone coverage. For the first time in camp, cornerback  L'Jarius Sneed , a six-year veteran, participated in 1-on-1 drills and 7-on-7 repetitions. 
 Joe Bleymaier said he has talked with offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy the past few days. For more than a week, Bleymaier, the pass game coordinator, has taken over Bieniemy's duties as offensive coordinator during his absence. He left the Chiefs after his wife, Mia Bieniemy, 57, was hospitalized in stable condition last week after being allegedly shot by the couple's son, Elijah Zion Bieniemy, 27, at the family's home in Virginia. "We miss EB, obviously," Bleymaier said. "It was great to hear from him, just on a personal standpoint. You're so devastated for him. He's been reaching out more and more lately with some of the football stuff, so that's kind of brought a little sense of normalcy back. As far as the [acting] offensive coordinator, calling in the plays and just making sure some of the administration stuff is handled has been the biggest thing." 
 One of Mahomes' best repetitions was during the first 11-on-11 period, when he, under center Creed Humphrey , rolled to the right on a play-action pass, completing an intermediate throw to Thornton while on the move. "We're not going to put any limitations on what Patrick can do rather than maybe emphasizing what we're going to try to do more," Bleymaier said of Mahomes, who had surgery in December to repair the torn ACL and LCL in his left knee. "We're really trying to eliminate holding him back -- or 'Let's not put him in this situation.' Everything is open. -- under center, rolling left or right, the whole playbook." 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 

 Among young players, the biggest winner from the Chiefs' first padded practice was rookie defensive tackle Peter Woods , the second of the Chiefs' first-round picks.

 In the 1-on-1 period, Woods had highlight repetitions, winning quickly in both of his matchups against backup guard Hunter Nourzad , a…

title: 2026 Los Angeles Chargers training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Chargers training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Los Angeles Chargers camp is taking place at The Bolt in El Segundo, California, and Chargers reporter Kris Rhim has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Chargers camp. We will update this file often. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 
 Latest from Chargers camp 
 
 Players with the most at stake during Chargers' training camp 
 Tracking 2026 NFL hold-ins: Tuipulotu 
 

 

 Thursday, Aug. 6 
 The Chargers' five-man race for guard continued Thursday with a new twist, as second-year lineman Branson Taylor took all the reps with quarterback Justin Herbert 's group at left guard. Before Thursday, two players had rotated at left guard, but Taylor got all of the reps with the first group in the team's first true padded practice.

 Taylor, a sixth-round pick in last year's draft who didn't make the 2025 53-man roster, was mainly a practice squad player last season. One year later, it seems that he has impressed the staff enough to have a legitimate shot at starting. On Thursday, Taylor fared well, creating running lanes and protecting Herbert throughout, a much-improved version of the player at camp last year.

 Coach Jim Harbaugh said on Wednesday that veteran Kayode Awosika was leading the race to start, and that Taylor, Pipkins, Trevor Penning and rookie Jake Slaughter were in the mix.

 Other observations:  

 
 OLB  Tuli Tuipulotu participated in team drills during Wednesday's padded practice, his second day in a row after not participating in team drills for the first six days of training camp. Harbaugh originally said that Tuipulotu's absence was being "handled internally," then later said it was a "ramp up." Neither Tuipulotu, his representatives, or the Chargers have acknowledged a contract-related absence, but his return to the field signals that whatever matter was being handled internally is resolved. 
 Rookie S  Genesis Smith intercepted Justin Herbert after a pass went through Charlie Kolar's hands. 
 CB  Donte Jackson had an impressive diving pass breakup on a pass by QB  Trey Lance during 7-on-7 that led to an interception by safety Elijah Molden . 
 DT  Justin Eboigbe continued his strong camp, consistently generating interior pressure 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 

 Outside linebacker Tuli Tuipulotu , who has been a limited participant in practice this training camp amid ongoing contract negotiations, was a full participant in Wednesday's practice. The caveat is that the practice was a walkthrough, so Tuipulotu and the other Chargers players were going at half speed. He still has yet to participate in a non-walkthrough practice 11-on-11 period, but his participation on Wednesday could be a sign that things could be headed toward a resolution.

 Other observations:  

 
 After an injury scare Tuesday scare to the same left leg in which he sustained a season-ending patellar tendon rupture last year, left tackle Rashawn Slater was a full participant in practice Wednesday without any limitations. 
 Branson Taylor and Trevor Penning rotated at left guard, continuing the five man race for this starting job. Rookie Jake Slaughter continues to play center with the second group. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 

 The Chargers had their first major injury scare Tuesday as left tackle Rashawn Slater appeared to sustain an injury to his left leg at practice. Slater went to the medical tent with a trainer and then did some on-field testing but didn't return to practice. Branson Taylor and Trey Pipkins III rotated at tackle in his absence.

 Slater ruptured the patella tendon in his left knee during last year's training camp, which forced him to miss the entire season. He appeared in good spirits after practice, walking around and taking pictures with his family.

 Quarterback Justin Herbert said that Slater told him he was healthy enough to return to the field.

 "He said he wanted to be out there, so I think that's okay," Herbert said.

 Other observations: 

 
 OLB Tuli Tuipulotu participated in one 7-on-7 rep but did not take part in the remainder of team drills, marking his sixth straight practice with limited participation as his contract situation remains unresolved. 
 Coach Jim Harbaugh said that Kayode Awosika is leading the competition to start at left guard, but added that Pipkins, Jake Slaughter and Taylor are all in the mix. Harbaugh said that he'd like to name a starter after the next ten practices. 
 The offense came out sharp, with Herbert completing his first eight passes before safety RJ Mickens broke up a pass. From there, the offense and defense traded wins throughout the rest of practice. 
 S Kendall Williamson intercepted Herbert on a pass that was intended for wide receiver Ladd McConkey . "That was nice. He snagged it," Derwin James Jr . said. 
 OLB  Nadame Tucker  had one of his best practices of camp, consistently generating pressure and recording three would-be sacks. 
 DT Teair Tart was disruptive throughout, including what likely would have been at least one sack. The Chargers' interior defensive line generated pressure throughout the day. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 Monday's practice was one of the better days for the defense, as they were constantly disruptive throughout. Undrafted cornerbacks Rodney Shelley and Avery Smith were among the stars. Smith continued his strong start to camp with another good day, as he intercepted quarterback DJ Uiagalele i and had an impressive pass breakup on a Justin Herbert pass. Shelley was sticky in coverage throughout and had a few pass breakups, celebrating after each.

 The rookies will have their first NFL training camp practice in pads on Tuesday at the University of San Diego, a chance to affirm the way they've been playing.

 

 Other observations:

 
 Edge rusher  Tuli Tuipulotu continued to not participate in team drills, continuing his limited participation as his contract situation remains unresolved. 
 Rookie Jake Slaughter and Kayode Awosika split reps at left guard as the competition for that spot continues. 
 Second-year wide receiver  KeAndre Lambert-Smith , who has been quiet so far, made one of the top highlights of the day with impressive downfield catch while cornerback Deane Leonard was draped in coverage. 
 Quentin Johnston also produced another offensive highlight, tracking a perfectly placed deep ball from Herbert over the outstretched arms of safety Derwin James Jr. along one sideline. 
 
 
 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 Coach Jim Harbaugh declined to say whether outside linebacker Tuli Tuipulotu 's absence from team drills at practice is contract-related, saying only the situation is being "handled internally" and repeatedly describing Tuipulotu as "ramping up."

 Tuipulotu hasn't taken part in team drills amid contract negotiations since camp began this week, as he is heading into the final year of his rookie contract. He finished sixth in the NFL in sacks last season.

 Without Tuipulotu again Saturday, rookie Akheem Mesidor flashed, looking explosive coming off of the edge throughout practice.

 More observations from the day: 

 
 Saturday marked perhaps the highest-energy practice as the Chargers offense had its best day this week. Wide receivers Ladd McConkey and Derius Davis caught deep passes that energized the crowd at the Chargers facility. 
 Cornerback Donte Jackson was active in coverage with a couple of pass breakups, causing fans to cheer in reaction.

title: 2026 Los Angeles Rams training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Rams training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Los Angeles Rams  camp is taking place at Loyola Marymount University in L.A. Rams reporter Sarah Barshop has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Rams camp. We will update this file often. Can the Rams live up to the hype? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Rams camp 
 
 Sean McVay praises Aaron Donald as Rams await DT's decision 
 Myles Garrett out third straight day with soreness 
 Puka Nacua says it 'never crossed my mind' to not take part in camp 
 Rams unveil two new alternate uniforms for 2026 
 
 

 Thursday, Aug. 6 
 Much of the talk during Rams training camp has been about a player not currently on the roster: Aaron Donald.

 On Thursday, as the Rams concluded training camp at Loyola Marymount University, coach Sean McVay said he didn't have an answer on whether the defensive tackle would come out of retirement.

 And if Donald does return? While defensive coordinator Chris Shula emphasized he's focusing on the roster guys now, he said, "I think I'd be lying if I said I hadn't thought about" the possibility of pairing up Donald and reigning NFL Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett .

 "You're anticipating, but at the same time, we're putting it in the core of our defense right now," Shula said. "We're building our defense step by step. If he decides to come, whenever that is, that's not going to affect exactly how we're doing it right now."

 McVay said Thursday that if Donald comes back, "those are things that you have to be able to figure out on the fly."

 "But what we are focusing on is the guys that are here," McVay said. "And then if Aaron is a part of it, it's obviously going to add value to our group, which is a positive."

 Another observation: 

 
 Thursday was the Rams' final practice at LMU before they head back to their team facility in Woodland Hills for the remainder of the preseason. 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 

 The Rams had a familiar face at their team facility this week, as Aaron Donald's name appeared on the NFL's transaction wire on Wednesday as a player taking part in a tryout for the team.

 The workout had to be reported to the league because it was supervised by a member of the Rams' football staff. Defensive coordinator Chris Shula said he was not at the Woodland Hills facility for the tryout, but said he talked to defensive line coach Giff Smith afterward.

 Last week, Rams head coach Sean McVay said he doesn't expect Donald to make a decision about coming out of retirement until after the team returns to its facility in Woodland Hills. The Rams' final practice at LMU is scheduled for Friday.

 

 More observations: 

 
 Defensive end Myles Garrett returned to practice on Wednesday after missing the last four practices with a little "lower body soreness." Garrett said he feels good and that the Rams were just trying to make sure he got back "100%." 
 Garrett was asked whether he feels like he can play with more "freedom" during practices in Los Angeles. He said that was a good way to describe the way the coaching staff allows players to play. "Not being punished or critiqued for trying to make a play," Garrett said. "There's guidelines and boundaries you got to stay within in the defense, but as long as we put ourselves in the right spots, they're all for it." 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 
 The Rams finished their second training camp block on Monday with what head coach Sean McVay called more of an unscripted practice. Matthew Stafford and  Stetson Bennett IV  took all of the quarterback reps for the Rams, with rookie Ty Simpson only taking part in individual drills.

 The first-team offense and the secondary exchanged several standout plays, including a pass breakup on receiver Puka Nacua by cornerback Trent McDuffie . Later, Stafford found wide receiver Davante Adams for a completion down the sideline.

 "I thought there was especially some really good back and forth with the ones," McVay said after practice. "Some really good plays on both sides, but that's what we're looking for is good quality play where you can really see guys playing through the cycle of the snap."

 McVay pointed to "some big breakups down the field" by McDuffie and cornerback Jaylen Watson .

 "Guys made plays on both sides and it felt like it was a quality operation," McVay said.

 More observations from the day: 

 
 
 McVay said he hasn't determined how he will allocate reps during the preseason between the quarterbacks other than Stafford not playing in any preseason games. Last year, Stafford and Jimmy Garoppolo sat out of the preseason while Bennett started the first two preseason games.

 
 
 Rams tight end Davis Allen is dealing with a quad injury. McVay said the Rams will give Allen "some time" before he returns to practice because it's a soft tissue injury. "You don't want to rush him back," McVay said. "He's played a lot of football and it'll give ... some of these other tight ends an opportunity to get snaps they wouldn't otherwise. But Davis is going to be a big part of what we do this year."

 
 
 Garrett (lower body soreness) did not practice for the fourth straight day. The Rams will re-evaluate him after the Tuesday off day.

 
 

 

 Sunday, Aug. 2 
 Coach Sean McVay praised quarterback  Stetson Bennett IV 's growth from last training camp, pointing out "the ownership of the offense" he has now.

 Bennett got the majority of the second-team reps last training camp while Matthew Stafford was dealing with a back injury and Jimmy Garoppolo was with the first team.

 "But then once Matthew came back, he didn't get any reps at all," McVay said. "And so for his ability to come in and to be able to run the one offense the way that he has, I've been really pleased with him."

 McVay said quarterbacks coach Dave Ragone "deserves a ton of credit" for the way he has worked with Bennett.

 "[Bennett has] played really well through the offseason program and up until now," McVay said. "And that's been a real positive for us."

 Bennett, a fourth-round pick in 2023, is competing with rookie first-round pick Ty Simpson to back up Stafford this season.

 More observations from the day: 

 
 The Rams held a jog-through on Sunday, meaning players were in T-shirts and shorts on the practice field. It was one of Stafford's scheduled days off of practice. 
 Defensive end Myles Garrett did not practice for the third straight day, as he is dealing with "a little soreness in his lower half," McVay said. The head coach said the Rams are just erring on the side of caution and that he is not concerned. 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 Rams running back Kyren Williams , who is entering his fifth NFL season, said he changed the way he worked out. While Williams has always prided himself on his versatility, he said he didn't do wide receiver drills this offseason. Instead, he focused on drills specific for a running back.

 "[In the past] I would work out and do a lot of receiver workouts and do a lot of different things because I want to be as versatile as I can," Williams said. "But this year I honed in on running back. I honed in on really training to be running back, training, like I said, those pad levels, those cuts. And when I am cutting, sinking my body. Because if I cut straight up, I'm not going nowhere.

 "My superpowers, when I'm low to the ground, I have both my feet in the ground and I'm playing it and I'm explosive."

title: 2026 Las Vegas Raiders training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Raiders training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Las Vegas Raiders  camp is taking place at Intermountain Health Performance Center in Henderson, Nevada, and Raiders reporter Ryan McFadden has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Raiders camp. We will update this file often. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 
 

 Latest news from Raiders camp 
 
 Maxx Crosby's approaching Raiders training camp with intensity 
 Three-time Pro Bowl guard Andrus Peat announces retirement 
 Cousins gets nod over Mendoza to open Raiders camp 
 What's next for Crosby, WR and CB rooms? 
 

 

 Thursday, Aug. 6 
 Tight end Brock Bowers keeps stacking up good practices.

 On Thursday, Bowers was problematic for the defense and made one of the best plays since the start of camp. During 11-on-11, Bowers caught a deep touchdown pass from quarterback  Kirk Cousins , in which he slipped behind the defense and was left completely wide open near the sideline. Bowers stopped running his route and waited until Cousins launched the ball across the field.

 There were multiple occasions where Bowers beat out linebacker Quay Walker to make catches in the middle of the field.

 Outside of Bowers, it wasn't the best morning for the offense. There were quite a few inaccurate throws and dropped passes. Fernando Mendoza recorded his second interception of camp after his pass slipped through  Malik Benson 's hands and cornerback Darien Porter dove to make a catch.

 Aidan O'Connell  also recorded two interceptions.

 The offense didn't do much during the two-minute period. Cousins' pass to Tre Tucker was broken up by rookie cornerback Hezekiah Masses . Cornerback Eric Stokes broke up Cousins' throw to Benson. The offense was penalized twice during that period, as well.

 Other observations:  

 
 Rookie cornerback Jermod McCoy had a rest day and didn't participate in Thursday's practice. Tight end Michael Mayer returned after missing Tuesday's practice with a nose injury. 
 Defensive end Keyron Crawford left practice early after colliding with edge rusher Malcolm Koonce during the team period. Assistant head coach Mike McCoy did not have an update on the rookie's status. 
 The Raiders mixed things up with their starting offensive line for the first time. They had Caleb Rogers and Jackson Powers-Johnson alternate reps at right guard. 
 Rookie safety Treydan Stukes had his first reps with the starting defense. He had a nice pass breakup while working with the second team during the two-minute period. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 

 

 Through six practices, rookie wide receiver Malik Benson has made a strong case for meaningful snaps this fall.

 In a fairly thin wide receiver room, Benson has been a shining star, and that was the case on Tuesday. His and quarterback  Fernando Mendoza 's connection was on point. Mendoza repeatedly completed throws to Benson on crossing and comeback routes.

 During the one-on-one period, Benson matched up with fellow rookie cornerback Jermod McCoy on a few reps, in which the former Oregon pass catcher showed off his footwork and separation ability to make catches.

 Wide receivers Jalen Nailor and Tre Tucker are essentially options one and two in the room. Benson has emerged as WR3, outplaying Jack Bech and  Dont'e Thornton Jr . thus far. For wide receiver coach Zach Azzanni, the biggest improvement he has seen from Benson has been route running.

 "He's gotten a lot better at it," Azzanni said. "He's got a long way to go, but I'm pleased with where he's at because I knew he had the skill set to do it."

 Other observations: 

 
 Tight end Michael Mayer did not practice after injuring his nose on Monday. Mayer, who was not in uniform, observed practice from the sideline. Tight end Carter Runyon was also absent for the fourth straight practice. 
 Offensive line coach Rick Dennison believes starting right tackle DJ Glaze , who struggled last season, still has untapped potential. "He does have great length, and he uses his arm length well, and he's working really hard at it. He's made some progress," Dennison said. 
 Starting inside linebacker Nakobe Dean said his body feels great after not participating during OTAs and mandatory minicamp. He added that his decision to come to Las Vegas over the Dallas Cowboys was because of a "gut feeling" that the Raiders would be a better situation. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 Fernando Mendoza had an up-and-down practice Monday, but coach Klint Kubiak understands the rookie will not be perfect all the time.

 "There will never be a perfect game or practice," Kubiak said. "I think he is doing a good job. I don't expect him to be perfect right now."

 The lowlights of Mendoza's performance included a few off-target throws during the team period and the one-on-one period between defensive backs and wide receivers. In 11-on-11, Mendoza's pass to Malik Benson in the middle of the field was slightly high and put the rookie wide receiver in a bad position to be nearly hit by safety Tristin McCollum .

 On the next play, he threw an incomplete pass to wide receiver Phillip Dorsett II .

 Mendoza also had snap issues, struggling to maintain control of the ball, but he managed to salvage the play. Kubiak said it's an issue he wants Mendoza to clean up.

 "That's a part of playing the position," Kubiak said. "... That's why the quarterback has to be one of the best athletes on the field. He has to be able to grab a low snap and be able to jump on it when it's over his head."

 

 Mendoza did bounce back toward the end of practice. His best throw was to Benson on a crossing route that led to a big gain. Later, he quickly threw the ball to wideout Shedrick Jackson on a slant.

 Still, Kubiak said it's too early to determine how well Mendoza can handle adversity.

 "There are 60-to-80 plays in a game. There are going to be ups and downs," Kubiak said. "What quarterback is gonna get the other 10 players playing at their best, that's what we're looking for."

 Another observation: 

 
 Tight end Michael Mayer left practice early because of a busted nose, but Kubiak said Mayer should be fine. 
 
 
 Sunday, Aug. 2 
 Sunday featured quarterback  Fernando Mendoza 's worst performance of training camp, as the defense was overpowering throughout the morning.

 During 11-on-11 work, Mendoza attempted a deep pass to rookie wide receiver Malik Benson . However, Mendoza's pass was underthrown, and cornerback Decamerion Richardson deflected the ball. When the Raiders were practicing two-minute situations, Mendoza and the second-team offense had pre-snap issues, prompting a timeout and the second team's replacement with the third team.

 Mendoza also threw his first interception of camp. In the 7-on-7 period, defensive back Greedy Vance intercepted Mendoza's pass attempt to wide receiver  Phillip Dorsett II . Vance perfectly read the pass and jumped in front of Dorsett to secure the ball.

 The offense did make some plays. Kirk Cousins and Brock Bowers connected on a few big throws in the middle of the field. Undrafted rookie running back Roman Hemby had a nice run down the middle. And  Aidan O'Connell  had the play of the day, throwing a touchdown pass to wide receiver E.J. Williams Jr.

 But for the most part, the defense had the upper hand. Linebacker Quay Walker and second-year defensive tackle  JJ Pegues  each recorded a sack. Defensive end Maxx Crosby was a force against the run. In the two-minute period, he quickly blew past right…
