 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Steelers camp 
 
 'Tempered': Inside Mike McCarthy's new vision for Steelers 
 Steelers' Broderick Jones cleared after eight months (neck) 
 Rodgers: 'Zero debate' 2026 will be last season 
 Jalen Ramsey, Joey Porter Jr. placed on PUP list 
 Steelers revamp wide receiver unit 
 Rodgers reunites with family ahead of final NFL season 
 
 
 Thursday, Aug. 6 
Rookie first-round pick Max Iheanachor left practice after about an hour and didn't return after appearing to suffer an upper-body injury Thursday. The team's medical staff extensively evaluated the offensive tackle's shoulder and neck area on the sideline, and he eventually walked up the hill to the locker room with an athletic trainer.
 Coach Mike McCarthy talks to the media before practice only, so he's expected to give an update on Iheanachor before Friday morning's practice.

 Iheanachor was making significant progress through the early portions of camp before the injury. In the initial preseason depth chart, he was listed as the second-team right tackle. And though McCarthy was quick to tell reporters not to put much stock in the required depth chart, Iheanachor has consistently been working with the second-team offensive line.

 "Max has had a great start," center Zach Frazier said. "Obviously for any rookie coming in, it's a lot. It's just an NFL offense, but every day he's taking steps. He doesn't really make the same mistakes twice. So he's coachable, and I'm really happy with how he's done so far."

 With Iheanachor out, Broderick Jones took the bulk of second-team reps at right tackle. He was inconsistent in the role as he continues to work his way back from season-ending neck surgery. Though he has been cleared to return to all football activities, Jones, who was the team's starting left tackle last season before his injury, is still regaining his strength and getting back his technique.

 

 More observations: 

 
 DT Cameron Heyward appeared to have a veteran day on Thursday, his first of training camp. 
 Tempers flared several times throughout Thursday's practice -- the first full-length practice of training camp. RB Lew Nichols and DB D'Shawn Jamison got into a scuffle, and WR Ben Skowronek and LB Payton Wilson got chippy after Skowronek shoved Patrick Queen in his helmet after a play in a team period. "People are tired, people are sore," Wilson said. "We're just competing. We love each other. Brothers fight all the time. So someone messes up, we getting into it a little bit, then we'll be in here eating lunch in 30 minutes together." 
 Actor Joe Manganiello, a Pittsburgh native, was at training camp practice Thursday, and he brought his little dog with him. 
 
 
 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 Midway through an individual period of the Steelers' Tuesday practice, the "Monday Night Football" jingle interrupted the Drake song that had been playing over the speakers on the St. Vincent College practice fields.

 The players paused, processing what they were hearing, then dropped everything and ran to the 5-yard line at the other end of the field. Center Zach Frazier snapped the ball as soon as the first-team offense lined up against the first-team defense, kicking off a series of five quick red zone plays.

 The offense scored just once as Mason Rudolph hit Ben Skowronek in the end zone, while the defense got three stops and was flagged for pass interference in the end zone. As soon as those five snaps were over, the DJ resumed playing Drake, and the players went back to their individual drill stations to finish the period.

 That officially marked the first "Mojo Moment" of coach Mike McCarthy's Steelers tenure.

 "I think that period is awesome because it simulates a real game," defensive lineman Sebastian Joseph-Day said. "Down 14-0, what are you going to do? A sudden change, and now you're on your 5-yard line, you got to get a stop. What do you do? And I feel like that is really going to help us prepare for those moments."

 Named for the Austin Powers movie franchise, the surprise drill Mojo Moment is a midpractice pop quiz. It can come at any time, and it's meant to ingrain the importance of staying ready in the players.

 "If you're prepared, then it's an easy test," safety DeShon Elliott said.

 McCarthy did it during practices in Dallas, too. Elliott remembers waiting out a rain delay against the Cowboys a couple of years ago. The Mojo Moment drill would've come in handy then, he said.

 "You got to sit inside a little bit, and then you got to come back out and get started right now," Elliott said. "So I think that's what he was trying to simulate, just being able to go out there and see who can really [tough it out] when it's time to in situations like that."

 

 More observations from the day: 

 
 Cornerback Jamel Dean had an up-and-down practice. He was burned a couple of times, including by Roman Wilson on a slant in the end zone for a score in an 11-on-11 period. On the very next play, DK Metcalf beat him on a quick out for a score, too. But Dean responded with two pass breakups in the practice-ending two-minute drill, each as he guarded Wilson in tight coverage. 
 Elliott is still working his way back from a season-ending knee injury suffered midway through last season, but he plans to ramp up his practice participation next week. "I really feel good," he said. "I feel fast, explosive, cutting, making plays. It's a process. I'll be ready Week 1." 
 After a relatively mild first day in pads Monday, the Steelers were noticeably more energetic and chippy in Tuesday's practice before Wednesday's light walk-through day. Joseph-Day and tackle Troy Fautanu got into a verbal altercation at the end of a one-on-one pass rush period when Joseph-Day took exception to where Fautanu lined up. McCarthy, though, wanted his team to turn up the intensity Tuesday, and he said as much in team meetings before practice. "Just picking up the urgency, picking up the physicality and things like that," running back Rico Dowdle said of McCarthy's message. "He talked about that before practice, and I think it came out today." 
 

 
 Monday, Aug. 3 
 The Steelers' Monday morning meeting featured a different kind of film study before their first day in pads. Instead of practice footage, coach Mike McCarthy pulled up the viral video of tight end Pat Freiermuth pulling a kid out from the crush of fans crowding the fence in an attempt to get autographs from players after Saturday's practice.

 "That was hilarious," quarterback Will Howard said of the video, adding that they dubbed Freiermuth the "unsung hero of the week" for his quick thinking to protect the young fan.

 "Situational awareness. We talk about it all the time. On and off the field."

 A scrum broke out between a couple of adults Saturday as Freiermuth and his teammates worked the autograph line, a hallmark of the Steelers' practices at St. Vincent College. Freiermuth noticed a child in front of him and snagged him, lifting him up and over the mesh fence as the the shoving escalated.

 "I just saw a bunch of people tumbling down and…

title: 2026 Seattle Seahawks training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Seahawks training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Seattle Seahawks ' camp is taking place in Renton, Washington, and Seahawks reporter Brady Henderson has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Seahawks camp. We will update this file often. What is new with the defending Super Bowl champions? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp previews for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Seahawks camp 
 
 WR Tory Horton healthy after cracking tibia last season 
 Seattle Pro Bowl DL Williams confirms deal talks 
 Seattle's Nick Emmanwori has ankle surgery, expected to play W1 
 Who are the Khoslas? Meet the family set to buy the Seahawks 
 

 
 Thursday, Aug. 6 
 Dante Fowler Jr . is a newcomer to Seattle's defense, but he was hardly a stranger when he arrived in May on a one-year deal.

 The 12th-year veteran has known defensive tackle Leonard Williams since 2012, when the two Florida natives took part in the Under Armour All-America Game. Fowler played for Aden Durde in Atlanta and Dallas, when Seattle's defensive coordinator was a position coach for the Falcons and Cowboys. In Dallas, Fowler was a teammate of fellow outside linebacker DeMarcus Lawrence , who took him under his wing.

 Lawrence helped sell Fowler on the Super Bowl champions this past offseason. A year earlier, Fowler had discussions with Durde about potentially signing with Seattle before opting for a second stint in Dallas instead.

 "I just respect the man he is," Fowler said Thursday of Durde. "He got it out the mud. He got it out the hard way. He's from London. He's not from here, and his IQ of football is just impressive. I love his passion, his intent of the game, the way he coaches his players, that's what I like the most. He demands something out of his players. He's not just telling them the X's and O's. He's going to demand it out of you."

 As Fowler was lauding Durde, Seahawks players were heading out of the team's indoor practice facility after a walk-through. Williams, Lawrence and a few other defensive linemen stopped to hype Fowler up, forcing him to pause mid-sentence and laugh.

 "See, that's why I'm happy to be here," he said. "Literally, right there."

 The Seahawks are happy to have Fowler as a less expensive -- even if older -- replacement for Boye Mafe as the speedy complement to the power-rushing styles of Lawrence, Uchenna Nwosu and Derick Hall in their outside linebacker rotation. Mafe, 27, ranked 17th among all defenders last season with an 11.4% pressure rate, according to ESPN Research. Fowler, who turned 32 earlier this week, was 31st at 10.3%.

 Fowler had 3.0 sacks in 17 games for Dallas, which was one more than Mafe had in 20 games, including playoffs. Yet Mafe got a three-year, $60 million deal from the Cincinnati Bengals at the start of free agency, and Seattle landed Fowler on a one-year, $2.5 million deal two months later.

 According to a copy of Fowler's contract that was obtained by ESPN, there's another $2.5 million available in incentives tied to regular-season sacks. He would make the highest of the following amounts: $500,000 for 7.0 or more sacks, $1 million for 9.0 or more, or $1.5 million for 11.0 or more. If Seattle plays in the NFC Championship Game, Fowler will make an additional $500,000 for 9.0-plus sacks or $1 million for 11.0-plus sacks.

 

 More observations: 

 
 After three straight days of practicing for nearly three hours outside in the heat, the Seahawks held a 55-minute walk-through indoors, with rest and recovery in mind. 
 Seattle signed FB Brock Lampe and waived rookie TE Lance Mason , the team announced. Lampe went undrafted out of Northern Illinois in 2025 and spent his rookie season on injured reserve with the Patriots, who waived him last month. He adds depth at FB as Robbie Ouzts remains sidelined. Coach Mike Macdonald said earlier this week that the team is trying to gather more info on Ouzts' injury. He didn't disclose what it is, but Ouzts was listed as having a neck injury during the playoffs last season. 
 

 
 Wednesday, Aug. 5 

 What does it mean to be a technician as a pass-catcher?

 Jaxon Smith-Njigba provided a few examples during an almost-unstoppable performance Wednesday.

 In one early period, as a deep ball from Sam Darnold was on its descent, the NFL's reigning receiving champion and AP Offensive Player of the Year deked an in-phase cornerback by momentarily gearing down, creating enough last-second separation to haul in the pass uncontested. On a later touchdown catch, the Seahawks' new $168.6 million man slow-played his release on a wheel route from the slot, perfectly timing the traffic before accelerating into a void between the corner and safety. He found the end zone again on a quick slant at the goal line.

 Whether he actually did make another highlight-reel grab while falling out of bounds was in question. An official called it incomplete before coach Mike Macdonald overruled him.

 Either way, Seattle's 10th practice of camp was JSN's best.

 "It was great to see him come alive," Macdonald said. "Some of those in high-leverage situations, too. ... There's defensive attention on where he's at at all times, too, so for him to be able to make those plays, it's great for the Seahawks, great for him."

 Smith-Njigba made this kind of dominance almost routine last season on his way to a league-high and franchise-record 1,793 receiving yards, which was the eighth-highest total in NFL history. That was with Klint Kubiak calling the offensive shots. Now it's up to new coordinator Brian Fleury, a first-time playcaller, to find the best way to utilize Seattle's star receiver.

 "He can get open from wherever, doing whatever, doing all the things from all the places," Macdonald said. "But how do we optimize it? How do we move him around? Where is he in the progression? He's going to be No. 1 in the progression on a lot of plays, but when is it best for him not be that? Those are the things that we're always going to be working through.

 "Today was a really cool step for us and our offense."

 

 
 Tuesday's season premiere of "Hard Knocks" showed Macdonald's mic'd up reaction to the fights during Friday's practice. He was disappointed in outside linebacker Derick Hall for throwing down offensive lineman Bryce Cabeldue from behind, and he felt fullback Brady Russell crossed a line with a verbal dig he took at Hall moments later. Based on what Macdonald and Hall said Wednesday, it's all been smoothed over. "Things get out of control sometimes, but at the end of the day, we all love each other here," Hall said. "We're a team, we're a brotherhood, and at the end of the day, it happens out here, we go in the locker room and hug it out, 'Hey man, I apologize. That was beyond the line of where we are trying to go and what we're trying to get,' and we move forward. I think that's what we do really well here." 
 OLB Jared Ivey has returned to practice after missing several days with an undisclosed injury. Still sidelined are WR Jake Bobo , CB Julian Neal , DL Mike Morris , LBs Jamie Sheriff and Chris Paul Jr ., and RB Jacardia Wright . OT Bobby Hart did not practice after going down Tuesday. 
 Backup LB Tyrice Knight delivered a highlight play when he reached down to intercept a low pass that had bounced off the hands of WR Tory Horton . It'll he hard for Knight to reclaim the starting job he lost last season to Drake Thomas -- who played his way into a two-year, $8 million deal -- but Macdonald has sounded open to finding…

title: 2026 San Francisco 49ers training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from 49ers training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The San Francisco 49ers camp is taking place in Santa Clara, California, and 49ers reporter Nick Wagoner has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at 49ers camp. We will update this file often. What does  Mike Evans  look like as a top receiver on the 49ers? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive into all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp previews for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 
 

 Latest news from 49ers' camp 
 
 What's next for 49ers receivers Aiyuk, Deebo and Pearsall? 
 Deebo Samuel on reunion with 49ers: 'Just matter of time' 
 WR Ricky Pearsall to have season-ending knee surgery 
 VP Paraag Marathe exits to focus on soccer clubs 
 Police: Shanahan not charged in crash at officer's discretion 
 49ers GM Lynch focused on 'players that are here,' not WR Aiyuk 
 
 
 

 Thursday, Aug. 6 
 The 49ers offense struggled in Monday's practice, but that session seems to have led the unit to lock in over the past two days. Quarterback  Brock Purdy  followed up a near-perfect (13-of-14) performance Wednesday with another strong day, featuring three of his best throws of camp.

 Purdy finished 11-of-14, including a pair of perfectly placed deep throws to WRs KhaDarel Hodge and Malik Turner for would-be touchdowns. He also fit a tight throw to Deebo Samuel Sr ., with coverage from Deommodore Lenoir , for a big gain over the middle.

 Defensive coordinator Raheem Morris has been impressed with Purdy's focus and competitiveness in more than a week of going against him every day.

 "The 'Layer King' has some really intensive intensity and I like that about him," Morris said. "Today he got fired up, which was cool, which was fun, which is competitive. And I love that. And when he does those things, it just makes the team go."

 More observations: 

 
 WR De'Zhaun Stribling (hamstring), LB Dre Greenlaw (soreness) and DT Osa Odighizuwa (soreness) were back at practice on a limited basis. All are being eased back into the mix. 
 WR Mike Evans (quad) didn't practice but is still doing plenty of work on the side, including some running. He looks like he'll return relatively soon, though the Niners clearly don't want to rush him. 
 Rookie DT Gracen Halton is back from a knee bone bruise and in a hurry to make an impact. He has been a dominant force in pass rush drills and productive in team drills as well. He has shown the most juice of any interior pass rusher on the Niners aside from Odighizuwa. 
 OL Nick Zakelj , who hurt an elbow in Wednesday's practice, was the only addition to the injury report Thursday. DE Sam Okuayinonu was fine after he was also shaken up Wednesday. 
 
 
 Wednesday, Aug. 5 
 Two years ago, the 49ers canceled joint practice sessions with the Saints because, by the time they got to them, they had 23 players not participating for injury reasons. By the end of Wednesday's session, the Niners were without 20 players on their 90-man roster.

 Some of those absences -- DE Nick Bosa , LB Dre Greenlaw and DT Osa Odighizuwa -- aren't serious and were more about getting past some general soreness. But questions still abound after rookie OL Carver Willis (concussion), FB Kyle Juszczyk (broken finger) and WR Jacob Cowing (hip flexor strain) were added to the injury report Wednesday.

 When asked whether next week's joint sessions with the Titans might be in jeopardy, assistant head coach Chris Foerster indicated that such a move hasn't been something that has come across his desk.

 "We have injuries, we have dings and bumps and bruises where guys are missing practices, but it has yet to come up in anything I've heard," Foerster said. "It doesn't mean it hasn't been discussed ... but that's not come up this week."

 More observations: 

 
 Wide receivers Mike Evans (quad), Christian Kirk (calf) and De'Zhaun Stribling (hamstring) again sat out practice Wednesday. All three did at least some running and conditioning work on the side during the session. 
 OL Brett Toth is also a new addition to the injury report with an undisclosed ailment. 
 In a bit of good injury news, rookie DT Gracen Halton returned from the knee bone bruise he'd been dealing with. Halton's fresh legs seemed to help him, as he was effective in one-on-one pass-rush drills and team work. 
 The Niners released defensive linemen Kevin Givens and  Cameron Sample  on Wednesday to make room for DE Ogbo Okoronkwo and WR KhaDarel Hodge . Okoronkwo, who played under defensive coordinator Raheem Morris with the Rams, is wearing No. 59. Hodge is wearing No. 0. 
 Quarterback  Brock Purdy had a sharp day despite playing musical chairs with wide receivers. In one red zone drill, he accounted for three straight touchdowns, finding running back Patrick Taylor Jr . and receiver Junior Bergen for scores before using his legs to score on a designed run. He also led a touchdown drive in the move-the-ball period, which ended on a deep connection with WR Jordan Watkins . 
 Tight end  Luke Farrell  had a nice day, too. Farrell hasn't offered much as a pass catcher in his time with the Niners, totaling 11 receptions last season. But he and Purdy were in sync Wednesday. 
 The Niners are back at it Thursday and then have a walkthrough set for Friday. 
 
 
 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 The injuries continue to mount for the 49ers, particularly at wide receiver. On Monday, they added veteran Mike Evans to the list as he did not practice because of a quad strain.

 The injury is not believed to be serious and Evans did some work on the side during the session, but it again left the Niners a bit short-handed. With  Ricky Pearsall (knee) done for the season, rookie De'Zhaun Stribling battling hamstring tightness and Christian Kirk out for the better part of the past week with a calf strain, the team's projected top four wideouts were not available Monday.

 Kirk and Stribling also did some work on the side and should be back soon, but the situation bears watching given the number of injury issues that always seem to plague this team at that position group.

 More observations: 

 
 Mike Brown, the title-winning coach of the NBA's New York Knicks, watched practice Monday. His son Cameron is the Niners' defensive quality control coach. 
 Alex Smith, the former 49ers quarterback and current ESPN analyst, was also in attendance. 
 Running back Kaelon Black (adductor) was another addition to the injury report after he missed the second half of Saturday's practice. 
 Defensive tackle C.J. West and edge rusher Romello Height returned from injuries to participate Monday. 
 WR Deebo Samuel continues to show off fresh legs in camp as he was again quite involved in the offense. With all the injuries at receiver, there's an opening for Samuel to establish a role beyond returning kicks. 
 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 While no definitive date has been set for coach Kyle Shanahan to return to full-time duty, he seems to be taking the necessary steps in that direction.

 Before Saturday's practice, Shanahan addressed the team for the first time since his July 14 car accident, according to general manager John Lynch. Then, during practice, Shanahan emerged on the field before team drills and stayed through the end of the session. At one point late in practice, he even stood behind the offense, offering real-time feedback rather than standing next to Lynch in the deep middle of the field.

 "He's doing better," Lynch said. "He got a nice welcome, and it was good to have him up there. We'll continue to do kind of like a phased approach. So that was one threshold. He…

title: 2026 Tampa Bay Buccaneers training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Buccaneers training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Tampa Bay Buccaneers ' camp is taking place at the Advent Health Training Center in Tampa, Florida, and Buccaneers reporter Jenna Laine has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Bucs camp. We will update this file often. We are looking at who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football, and which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest new s from Bucs camp 
 
 Bucs GM Licht: 'No plans' for Vea trade, Mayfield still franchise QB 
 Mayfield felt 'disrespected' and 'undervalued' by contract offers 
 History says Vea, Mayfield will play with Bucs this season 
 Vea requests trade from Bucs after stalled talks 
 2026 Bucs training camp preview 
 
 

 

 Thursday, Aug. 6 

 After going three straight days inside the indoor practice facility and having a rest day Wednesday, the Bucs returned outdoors.

 Quarterback  Baker Mayfield  felt the heat from the sun and from the defense, as the pressure got to him several times, and he was flushed from the pocket and forced to throw the ball away as he couldn't find any downfield options because of tight coverage by the secondary. And he was also picked off.

 Backup linebacker John Bullock jumped a route on a pass intended for tight end Cade Otton and returned the interception for a touchdown. Rookie inside linebacker Josiah Trotter , who has made his presence known now that the pads are on, immediately drilled Otton after catching a short pass from Mayfield. Overall, it wasn't a great day for Mayfield and the tight ends, with rookie Keionte Scott breaking up a Mayfield pass intended for Payne Durham .

 Rookie cornerback Ayden Garnes had a pass breakup on a Mayfield ball intended for rookie wide receiver  Ted Hurst III  along the right sideline. Rookie Rueben Bain Jr . also blew up a screen pass to running back Bucky Irving .

 Other observations: 

 
 Outside linebacker David Walker Jr., who missed his rookie season last year with a torn ACL, had a strip sack of backup quarterback Jake Browning and made the recovery at the end of practice. Walker has had a sack just about every practice. "We didn't get to see him in pads last year, but to see him out there and the way he moves -- he moves like an inside backer, but he plays like an outside backer and he's got great power," coach Todd Bowles said. 
 Wide receiver  Dean Patterson  hauled in an impressive deep ball catch working against cornerback Josh Hayes . 
 Wide receivers Emeka Egbuka (soreness) and  Chris Godwin Jr . (rest day on Tuesday), were back in action. Defensive tackle  A'Shawn Robinson  (rest day on Tuesday) and safety Miles Killebrew (knee) were all back practicing. Cornerback Benjamin Morrison (hamstring) was doing individual drills. 
 Wide receivers Jalen McMillan (knee), Tez Johnson (groin) and David Sills V (knee) were not practicing. Inside linebacker Alex Anzalone also sat out with soreness. The status of nose tackle Vita Vea (back) and left tackle Tristan Wirfs (hamstring) are unchanged. 
 Bucs' 12-time captain and future Ring of Honor member Lavonte David, who retired this spring, surprised teammates by coming out to practice. Also in attendance was former Bucs Super Bowl-winning head coach Jon Gruden, who will call the Bucs' second preseason game against the Kansas City Chiefs on Aug. 22. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 

 Tempers flared as the Bucs put on pads for the second straight day -- this time at their annual night practice. Rookie inside linebacker Josiah Trotter , the Bucs' second-round draft pick and son of NFL great Jeremiah Trotter, had multiple tackles for a loss during Monday's first padded practice. He followed that up with a tackle for a loss during 11-on-11s Tuesday.

 Trotter could be seen jawing with starting right guard Cody Mauch , starting left guard Ben Bredeson , starting right tackle Luke Goedeke and backup swing tackle Justin Skule . Fellow inside linebacker Alex Anzalone had to restrain Trotter as he took him to the sideline. Anzalone could also be seen pointing at the offensive line and chirping as they huddled up, appearing to support his younger teammate and directing everyone to get back to work.

 While coach Todd Bowles stopped practice to address the team, he praised the 21-year-old challenging for the starting MIKE role. "He had a heck of a day yesterday and he buckled some guys," Bowles said. "If they start playing like that yesterday, he shouldn't need the extra energy today. He's probably a guy you really don't want to mess with either."

 He added, "Once you put your helmet on and you go on the field, all is fair game as long as you're doing it the right way. He plays with the right temperament and he plays the right way."

 Other observations:  

 
 During one-on-one drills, rookie outside linebacker Rueben Bain Jr . used a nasty hand swipe to blow by starting right tackle Luke Goedeke , drawing gasps from fans in attendance. Mind you, Goedeke is no slouch and is making $22.5 million a year. Bain also had what would have been a sack of quarterback Jake Browning . 
 Rookie wide receiver Ted Hurst III hauled in a Baker Mayfield red zone touchdown in the corner of the end zone with Zyon McCollum in tight coverage. Defensive tackle Calijah Kancey came flying at Mayfield on that play however, and it would have very likely been a sack. Still, it was good work for Hurst, who also caught a 20-yard pass downfield from Mayfield. 
 Wide receiver Tez Johnson left the practice field early to get treatment for what Bowles said was a groin injury that he sustained while running. Wide receiver David Sills V also left practice early, but Bowles did not have specifics immediately after practice. He was, however, seen with an ice pack on his knee. 
 The team was without its top three wide receivers as  Chris Godwin Jr .,  Emeka Egbuka  and Jalen McMillan all sat out. Godwin has been getting maintenance days in camp, while McMillan - who was spotted wearing a compression sleeve on his left calf - banged his knee in practice, according to Bowles, which forced him to miss Monday as well. Egbuka is still dealing with soreness and "tweaked something," Bowles said, and the team is "trying to keep him off the turf." 
 Rookie  Dean Patterson , an undrafted free agent out of Georgia Tech and FIU (he's also from nearby Lutz), maximized his opportunities in a depleted wide receiver room, hauling in two touchdowns from Browning. 
 Cornerback Ayden Garnes , an undrafted free agent out of Arizona, closed out practice with an interception off quarterback Jalon Daniels . He also picked off Mayfield during one-on-ones Monday on a pass intended for Kameron Johnson . With Benjamin Morrison and Jacob Parrish both missing time, he's gotten a lot more opportunities and is pushing for the last cornerback spot. 
 The team has Wednesday off and will return Thursday at their regular 8:30 a.m. practice time. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 Wide receivers Jalen McMillan and Emeka Egbuka were not practicing for the team's first day in pads -- due to being, as coach Todd Bowles put it, "a little sore." Cornerback Jacob Parrish , last year's starting nickelback who is competing for a starting outside cornerback spot, also missed practice with what Bowles said was soreness.

title: 2026 Tennessee Titans training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Titans training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Tennessee Titans ' camp is taking place at the Vanderbilt Health Football Center, and Titans reporter Turron Davenport has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Titans camp. We will update this file often. We are looking at who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football, and which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Titans news: 

 
 Titans DT Jeffery Simmons throws punch, sent to side field 
 Will Levis: There aren't 32 QBs better than me 
 Titans WRs join Cam Ward in Miami to build chemistry 
 

 

 Thursday, Aug. 6 

 The Titans returned to the field after not practicing Wednesday. The pace was noticeably slower to start, but it livened up during team period.

 The offensive line continues to shuffle, especially along the interior, where Cordell Volson and Jackson Slater are the top contenders for right guard while Austin Schlottmann , Pat Coogan and Andre James are battling for the starting center spot.

 All five players have gotten first-team reps in different tandems. Schlottmann has enjoyed going against Jeffery Simmons during team period because "he's one of the best, if not the best interior defenders in the league." Coach Robert Saleh said they're not close to deciding who will start at this point but expects to be closer to a decision leading into the third preseason game.

 Other observations: 

 
 WR  Elic Ayomanor continues to have a solid camp. He caught a deep pass from Cam Ward on a go route in red zone team period to even the score with Alontae Taylor who broke up a pass on the same route earlier in practice. Ward went to Ayomanor again, but the pass fell incomplete. Ayomanor collided with S  Kevin Winston Jr . as they went up for the pass in what Saleh described as a "bang, bang" play. Ayomanor got up favoring his left shoulder after being down for a bit. He went inside for further evaluation. 
 Left tackle  Dan Moore Jr . returned to practice after leaving team period and walking into the building on his own with a trainer Tuesday. Moore took part in team period and got into a small pushing match with linebacker Cody Barton after one of the plays. 
 JC Latham came out during team period towards the end of practice after taking three reps. Reserve tackle Austin Deculus came on in Latham's place and stayed in when the next group of linemen came in. Latham returned for the final team period and had a couple nice blocks on run plays. 
 The Titans will host a Blue/White scrimmage at Nissan Stadium on Friday night. "We'll play move the ball," Saleh said after practice. "We'll play special teams and it'll flow like a game where you'll see first offense against first defense. We have a full scoring system to make it competitive and as game-like as possible. We'll try to get to like 90 plays." 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 

 The middle linebacker competition is heating up. James Williams Sr . has strung three consecutive standout days.

 Williams said he's lost about 20 pounds this offseason. The converted safety looked like a defensive back on a jumping one-handed interception of a Mitchell Trubisky pass during team period. Williams got a pass breakup later in practice when Trubisky went to tight end  Kylen Granson  on an out-breaking route.

 Titans defensive coordinator Gus Bradley spoke glowingly of Williams before practice.

 "We like those guys that have played safety in their career and move them down the linebacker," Bradley said. "That pass coverage part of it, that safety background that he has, I think allows him to be a little bit more instinctive."

 Williams worked alongside rookie linebacker Anthony Hill Jr . mostly. Hill added a couple of interceptions as well, both off Trubisky. One of the interceptions came because Trubisky hit his hand on an offensive lineman's helmet.

 Other observations:  

 
 DT  Jeffery Simmons and OL  Austin Schlottmann with some extracurricular after a play. Simmons swung at  JC Latham in the scrum before Tanzel Smart grabbed Simmons. Coach Robert Saleh didn't like it. Stopped practice and gathered the group for a cool-down talk. Simmons was forced to work on a side field with Brian Bell (strength coach) and wasn't allowed to return to practice. 
 QB  Cam Ward connected with WR  Carnell Tate on a beautiful pass for the play of the day. Tate ran a post and Ward launched a deep pass that traveled at least 50 yards in the air. Tate showed explosiveness as he pulled away from Alontae Taylor to run down the ball for the touchdown. 
 One-on-ones were a little different for WRs/DBs under Saleh. It's more like seven-on-sevens but only allowing man defense. Saleh said he uses this format to facilitate more authentic route running instead of the unreasonably long-developing routes. The offensive line versus defensive line setup was the same as normal. 
 Backup QB  Will Levis and WR  Bryce Oliver connected on two deep passes. Levis worked a play-action pass to Oliver on a deep crossing route. Oliver caught the pass in between the safety and cornerback Keydrain Calligan . Oliver made a jumping catch on a go route from Levis later in the day. 
 LT  Dan Moore Jr . left practice during the second team period. Saleh acknowledged after practice that Moore was hurt, but he didn't have any specifics regarding the injury immediately after practice. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 

 The first day of pads had a really good pace and tempo. Both the offense and defense did a good job keeping each other off the ground for the most part.

 The defense had big hits from cornerback Nazeeh Johnson and linebacker Sean Brown , and quarterback  Cam Ward had two hiccups throwing across his body while rolling out -- resulting in interceptions.

 Coach Robert Saleh said the throws across the body are non-negotiable, especially the shallow ones. Safety  Amani Hooker came up with the first interception as a result of what Saleh said was a "poor decision" by Ward. Saleh called the second interception an elite play by defensive lineman  Jermaine Johnson II .

 Ward did have a couple of nice spot throws to  Wan'Dale Robinson  between defenders during team period. He also connected with veteran receiver Calvin Ridley on a well-placed pass to towards the sideline.

 Other observations:  

 
 WR  Elic Ayomanor continues to have a solid camp. He beat Micah Robinson at the line of scrimmage and caught a deep pass in the end zone from  Mitchell Trubisky . The two almost connected on another deep pass but Robinson was called for pass interference. Ayomanor caught a pass on a deep in-breaking route from Ward also. Saleh credited Ayomanor for the offseason preparation and confidence he's playing with. 
 Defensive line coach Aaron Whitecotton didn't like the lack of intensity during individual period, so he made the group do pushups. The defensive line goes nonstop during that period. Whitecotton has them do a lot of work on the sled and with bags but at a very fast pace. 
 JC Latham took part in the first team period but worked with a trainer on the third field for the remaining ones. Latham's absence allowed Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson to get some valuable reps as he competes with Austin Deculus for the swing tackle spot. 
 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug.1  
 The Titans hosted fans at training camp for the first time this summer, and they got to see a pretty solid day from quarterback  Cam Ward .

 Ward and Elic Ayomanor connected on a couple of deep passes along the sideline. It's clear Ward trusts Ayomanor to win in jump ball situations, as the…
